exp: Article 256 requires each State to comply with laws made by Parliament, and lets the Union give directions to a State for that purpose.

q: Which one of the following Chief Ministers of West Bengal was sworn in May 2011?
exp: Mamata Banerjee was sworn in as Chief Minister of West Bengal on 20 May 2011 after the Trinamool Congress ended 34 years of Left Front rule. She was the state's first woman Chief Minister.

q: A Judicial Magistrate of the First Class (JMFC) sentences an accused to three years of imprisonment (which is the maximum within his power to sentence) and a fine of ₹50,000. In default of payment of the fine, the court further directs that the accused shall undergo an additional one year of imprisonment. Under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023 in India, which of the following statements is most accurate?
o: Valid, because imprisonment in default of payment of fine is separate from the substantive punishment.
Invalid, because imprisonment in default of payment of fine cannot exceed one-fourth of the Magistrate's power to award substantive imprisonment.
Invalid, because after awarding the maximum substantive imprisonment, a First Class Magistrate cannot award any further imprisonment.
Valid only if it is approved by the Court of Session.
exp: A First Class Magistrate can award up to 3 years. Under the BNSS, imprisonment in default of fine cannot exceed one-fourth of the term the Magistrate is competent to award, which is 9 months here. One year is therefore invalid.

q: Which constitutional authority in India is referred to as the "guardian of the public purse"?
o: Governor of Reserve Bank of India (RBI)
exp: The CAG (Article 148) audits all receipts and expenditure of the Union and the States, and is therefore called the guardian of the public purse.

q: In which landmark case was the "Basic Structure" doctrine propounded?
o: The Golaknath versus State of Punjab case
The Kesavananda Bharati versus State of Kerala
The Minerva Mills versus Union of India
The Waman Rao versus Union of India
exp: In Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala (1973) a 13-judge bench held that Parliament can amend any part of the Constitution but cannot alter its basic structure.

q: Which dispute falls under the 'Original Jurisdiction' of the Supreme Court under Article 131 of Indian constitution?
exp: Article 131 gives the Supreme Court original jurisdiction in disputes between the Centre and one or more States, or between States. Private disputes and criminal appeals do not come under it.

q: Which Article of Indian Constitution provides for the formation of an Inter-State Council in India?
exp: Article 263 empowers the President to set up an Inter-State Council. It was established in 1990 on the recommendation of the Sarkaria Commission.

q: A sees B attempting to kidnap C into a vehicle. A shoots B dead to prevent the kidnapping. Which of the following is the strongest legal justification under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 in India?
o: The act would be justified only if B were armed.
The act exceeds private defence because kidnapping is not punishable by death.
Private defence extends to death in kidnapping assaults.
A may only use non-lethal force unless C is actually abducted.
exp: Under Section 38 of the BNS the right of private defence of the body extends to causing death in assaults such as those causing apprehension of death or grievous hurt, rape, kidnapping or abducting, and acid attack. It also covers defending another person.

q: According to Article 53 of the Indian Constitution, in whom is the executive power of the Union formally vested?
exp: Article 53(1) vests the executive power of the Union in the President, who exercises it directly or through subordinate officers. In practice the President acts on the advice of the Council of Ministers.

q: A law declares that registration of a document shall be "conclusive proof" of its execution. During a trial, the opposing party wants to present oral evidence denying execution despite the document being duly registered. What should the court do under the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023?
o: It should allow the rebuttal because every presumption is rebuttable.
It should reject the evidence because conclusive proof renders rebutting evidence inadmissible.
The matter should be treated only as 'may presume'.
It should admit the rebuttal only through documentary evidence.
exp: When the law declares one fact to be 'conclusive proof' of another, the court must treat the other fact as proved and cannot allow evidence to disprove it.

q: During a hearing, the court concludes that a fact is so highly probable that a prudent person would act on the supposition that it exists, even without absolute certainty. Under the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023, such a fact in India is classified as:
exp: Under the BSA a fact is 'proved' when the court believes it exists, or considers its existence so probable that a prudent man would act on the supposition that it exists.

q: Under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 in India, which of the following would not amount to an "offence" as defined under Section 2(24)?
o: An act committed by a person under seven years of age
An act punishable under BNS (Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita) with imprisonment
An act punishable under a local law with six months' imprisonment
An act causing harm due to negligence
exp: Section 20 of the BNS says nothing is an offence which is done by a child under seven years of age. Such an act can never be an 'offence' under the Sanhita.

q: Which of the following has been the longest-serving Prime Minister of India?
exp: Jawaharlal Nehru served as Prime Minister from 15 August 1947 to 27 May 1964, nearly 17 years. This is the longest tenure of any Indian Prime Minister.

q: A victim in a serious criminal case wants her privately chosen advocate to actively assist the prosecution alongside the special public prosecutor appointed by the state. Which of the following is correct under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 in India?
o: Victims have no role once prosecution begins.
A victim's advocate may assist the prosecution if the court permits.
Only the Public Prosecutor may appear in criminal trials.
Victim participation is allowed only in magistrate courts.
exp: The BNSS allows the court to permit the victim to engage an advocate of her choice to assist the prosecution. The Public Prosecutor remains in charge of the case.

q: Financial Emergency in India comes under which Article of the Constitution?
exp: Article 360 deals with Financial Emergency. Article 352 is National Emergency and Article 356 is President's Rule. A Financial Emergency has never been declared in India.

q: According to Article 39(b) of the Indian Constitution, what is the primary objective of distributing the ownership and control of material resources?
exp: Article 39(b) directs the State to distribute the ownership and control of the material resources of the community in a way that best serves the common good.

q: What is the main objective of the Metropolitan Planning Committee under Article 243ZE of the Indian Constitution?
o: To collect taxes from metropolitan residents
To prepare a draft development plan for the metropolitan area
To manage the police force within the metropolitan area
To settle disputes between different municipalities
exp: The Metropolitan Planning Committee prepares a draft development plan for the metropolitan area as a whole (Article 243ZE).

q: In which case did the Supreme Court declare that the Preamble is a part of the Constitution?
exp: In Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala (1973) the Supreme Court held that the Preamble is a part of the Constitution. In the earlier Berubari Union case (1960) it had said the opposite.

q: A villager becomes aware of a planned offence falling under one of the categories listed in Section 33 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 in India. He deliberately withholds the information and later contends that the prosecution must prove the absence of a reasonable excuse for such non-disclosure. Which of the following statements is legally correct?
o: The prosecution must prove the absence of a reasonable excuse beyond reasonable doubt.
The burden lies on the accused to prove a reasonable excuse for non-disclosure.
Silence alone cannot attract legal consequences under BNSS (Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita).
The burden shifts to the magistrate conducting the inquiry.
exp: Every person aware of the commission of, or intention to commit, certain listed offences must inform the nearest Magistrate or police officer, and the burden of proving a reasonable excuse for not doing so lies on that person. This duty is in Section 33 of the BNSS.

q: According to the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 in India, which of the following options correctly explains the difference between 'dishonestly' and 'fraudulently'?
o: "Dishonestly" involves deceit, whereas "fraudulently" involves wrongful gain or loss.
"Fraudulently" requires an intention to deceive, whereas "dishonestly" relates to wrongful gain or wrongful loss.
Both terms are legally identical in all contexts.
"Fraudulently" applies only to property-related offences, whereas "dishonestly" applies only to physical offences.
exp: 'Dishonestly' means acting with the intention of causing wrongful gain or wrongful loss. 'Fraudulently' means acting with intent to defraud, that is, to deceive.

q:
Match the following Schedules with their subject matter:
Column A (Schedule) — Column B (Subject matter)
A. Seventh Schedule — 1. Languages recognised by the Constitution
B. Eighth Schedule — 2. Distribution of powers between the Union and the States
C. Eleventh Schedule — 3. Municipalities: functional items
D. Twelfth Schedule — 4. Panchayats: functional items
exp: Seventh Schedule: division of powers between Union and States. Eighth Schedule: recognised languages (22). Eleventh Schedule: 29 subjects of Panchayats. Twelfth Schedule: 18 subjects of Municipalities.

q: According to Article 60 of the Indian Constitution, who administers the oath of office to the President of India?
exp: Under Article 60 the oath of the President is administered by the Chief Justice of India, or in his absence by the senior-most Supreme Court judge available.

q: Which Article empowers the President to promulgate Ordinances during recess of Parliament?
exp: Article 123 lets the President promulgate ordinances when Parliament is not in session. Article 213 gives the same power to the Governor. Article 110 defines Money Bills and Article 108 deals with joint sittings.

q: What is the specific ground for the removal of a Supreme Court Judge under Article 124(4) of the Indian Constitution?
o: Violation of the Constitution or conviction for a criminal offence
exp: Under Article 124(4) a Supreme Court judge can be removed only for proved misbehaviour or incapacity, by an order of the President after each House passes an address with a special majority.

q: The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) replaces which of the following?
exp: BNS replaced the Indian Penal Code, 1860. BNSS replaced the CrPC, 1973 and BSA replaced the Indian Evidence Act, 1872. All three came into force on 1 July 2024.

q: Which Article of the Indian Constitution provides that the validity of the proceedings of Parliament cannot be challenged in any court?
exp: Article 122 says courts cannot question the validity of proceedings in Parliament on the ground of an alleged irregularity of procedure.

q: Under which Article of the Indian Constitution is protection against arbitrary arrest and detention provided?
exp: Article 22 protects a person against arbitrary arrest and detention: the right to know the grounds, to consult a lawyer and to be produced before a magistrate within 24 hours.

q: The word 'Constitution' is derived from the Latin word 'Constituere'. What does 'Constituere' mean?
o: To establish or to set up
exp: 'Constitution' comes from the Latin 'constituere', which means to establish or to set up.

q: What powers does the Supreme Court possess as a "Court of Record" under Article 129 of the Indian Constitution?
exp: Under Article 129 the Supreme Court is a court of record. Its records have evidentiary value and it has the power to punish for contempt of itself.

q: Which Home Affairs Minister has also been the 1st Minister of Co-operation since July 2021?
exp: The Ministry of Co-operation was created in July 2021. Home Minister Amit Shah became its first minister.

q: A disciplinary authority conducting departmental arbitration proceedings records the statements of witnesses and accepts electronic evidence. One party argues that the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 in India applies automatically because evidence is being taken. Which of the following statements is legally correct?
o: The Act applies because all proceedings involving evidence come under it.
The Act applies only to criminal proceedings.
The Act does not apply to proceedings before an arbitrator.
The Act applies only when both parties give consent.
exp: Section 1 of the BSA applies it to judicial proceedings before courts, including courts-martial, but it does not apply to affidavits or to proceedings before an arbitrator.

q: Which of the following digital elements are now admissible as primary evidence under the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023?
o: Emails, SMS, WhatsApp chats, and cloud data
exp: The Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam treats electronic and digital records, such as emails, messages, server logs and data stored on devices or the cloud, as documents, and gives them the same legal effect as paper records.

q: ______ falls exclusively under the Union List.
exp: Foreign affairs is in the Union List. Forests and labour welfare are in the Concurrent List.

q: Who presides over the joint sitting of the Parliament?
exp: Under Article 108 a joint sitting is called by the President, but it is presided over by the Speaker of the Lok Sabha (Article 118).

q: What of the following is a major reform in the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita regarding FIRs (First Information Reports)?
o: FIRs can no longer be filed
FIRs will now require court approval first
FIRs can be filed online and via electronic communication
exp: Section 173 of the BNSS allows information on a cognizable offence to be given by electronic communication (e-FIR); it must be signed within three days. Zero FIR is also recognised.

q: The provisions relating to anti-defection are contained in which Schedule of the Indian Constitution?
exp: The Tenth Schedule, added by the 52nd Amendment Act, 1985, contains the anti-defection law.

q: Which article of the Constitution of India states that a person must have completed the age of 35 years to be eligible for election as President?
exp: Article 58 lists the qualifications for President: a citizen of India, completed 35 years of age and qualified to be elected to the Lok Sabha.

q: Under which Constitutional Amendment Act was Article 243ZD, relating to the Committee for District Planning, inserted into the Indian Constitution?
exp: The 74th Amendment Act, 1992 added Part IXA (Municipalities), which includes Article 243ZD on the District Planning Committee. The 73rd Amendment deals with Panchayats.

q: In a dispute regarding the genuineness of a will under the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA), a party presents evidence that the deceased had consulted a lawyer and prepared several earlier wills before finalising the disputed will. This evidence is relevant because:
o: It is relevant as preparation and conduct under Section 6.
It is conclusive proof of execution.
It is irrelevant because it is earlier in time.
exp: Section 6 of the BSA makes facts showing motive, preparation and previous or subsequent conduct relevant. Consulting a lawyer and drafting earlier wills is preparation and conduct.

q: A clerk employed temporarily for a single day to carry confidential court files intentionally destroys one of the files. Which of the following is the most legally accurate statement under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 in India?
o: He is not considered a clerk because his employment was temporary.
He is considered a public servant only if formally appointed by the government.
He may still fall within the meaning of 'clerk' or 'servant' under the general explanations.
He cannot be punished because temporary workers are excluded from criminal liability.
exp: The BNS explains that a person employed temporarily, or on a particular occasion, as a clerk or servant is deemed to be a clerk or servant. Short employment does not remove liability.

q: Who must be notified during the arrest of a person under Bharatiya Nagarik suraksha Samhita(BNSS)?
exp: The BNSS requires the police to inform a relative, friend or other person named by the arrested person about the arrest and the place where he is being held.

q: The High Court appoints a retired government officer and confers upon him the powers of a Judicial Magistrate First Class for the purpose of dealing with specified environmental cases for a period of one year. Which of the following is most accurate under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 in India?
o: The appointment is invalid because only serving judicial officers may exercise magistrate powers.
The appointment is valid if the officer possesses qualifications or legal experience prescribed by the High Court.
Such appointment requires approval of Parliament.
The officer automatically becomes a permanent judicial magistrate.
exp: Under the BNSS the High Court may confer the powers of a Judicial Magistrate on any person who holds or has held a government post, as a Special Judicial Magistrate, if he has the qualification or legal experience the High Court prescribes. The term is up to one year at a time.

q: Which of the following best reflects the intent of Article 44 of the Indian Constitution regarding the Uniform Civil Code (UCC)?
o: It is impossible due to diversity.
It requires balanced, inclusive, and gradual implementation.
exp: Article 44 says the State shall 'endeavour' to secure a Uniform Civil Code for citizens. It is a Directive Principle, a goal to be reached gradually and inclusively, and is not enforceable by courts.

q: The concept of a "Union of States" under Article 1 of the Constitution of India implies that:
o: States possess a constitutional right to secede
The Indian federation originated through agreement among sovereign states.
The Union is indestructible, though States may be reorganized.
States have equal sovereignty with the union.
exp: India is an 'indestructible Union of destructible States'. No state can leave the Union, but Parliament can change the area, boundaries or names of states under Article 3.

q: ______ is NOT covered under Article 20 of the Indian Constitution.
exp: Article 20 gives three protections: no ex-post facto criminal law, no double jeopardy and no self-incrimination. 'Legitimate expectation' is a principle of administrative law and is not part of Article 20.

q: Under Article 110 of the Indian Constitution, whose decision is final in determining whether a bill is a "Money Bill" or not?
o: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha
The Chairman of the Rajya Sabha
exp: Article 110(3) makes the decision of the Speaker of the Lok Sabha final on whether a Bill is a Money Bill.

q: Which Article of the Indian Constitution specifies that a law for the abolition or creation of a Legislative Council is not to be treated as a formal amendment under Article 368?
exp: Article 169 allows Parliament to abolish or create a Legislative Council after the Assembly passes a special-majority resolution. Article 169(3) says such a law is not treated as a constitutional amendment under Article 368.

q: Under the Constitution of India, which authority has the power to enlarge the jurisdiction and powers of the Supreme Court with respect to matters in the Union List?
exp: Under Article 138 Parliament can by law enlarge the jurisdiction and powers of the Supreme Court on any matter in the Union List.

q: Under which Article of the Indian Constitution provides for the formation of the Finance Commission?
exp: Article 280 requires the President to constitute a Finance Commission every five years to recommend the sharing of taxes between the Centre and the States.

q: Which year was the National Anti-Doping Act passed in India?
exp: The National Anti-Doping Act was passed in 2022. It gave statutory backing to the National Anti-Doping Agency (NADA).

q: Under Article 111 of the Indian Constitution, what does the President's "Suspensive Veto" power allow him to do in relation to a Bill passed by Parliament?
o: Refer the Bill to the Supreme Court
exp: In a suspensive veto the President returns a Bill (other than a Money Bill) to Parliament for reconsideration. If Parliament passes it again, with or without changes, the President must give assent.

q: According to the BNSS, what does the term "bail" mean?
o: Release from custody on conditions imposed by a court or officer
exp: The BNSS defines 'bail' as the release of a person accused or suspected of an offence from the custody of law upon conditions imposed by an officer or court, on execution of a bond or bail bond.

q: According to the BSA, what will be the consequences if a person refuses to answer an important question in court?
o: An adverse inference may be drawn
exp: The court may presume that if a person refuses to answer a question he is not legally compelled to answer, the answer would have been unfavourable to him. This is called an adverse inference.

q: Under Article 358 of the Indian Constitution, the suspension of Article 19 during a National Emergency applies only when the Emergency has been declared on which ground?
o: Breakdown of constitutional machinery or failure of governance
exp: After the 44th Amendment, Article 358 automatically suspends Article 19 only when a National Emergency is declared on the ground of war or external aggression, not armed rebellion.

q: What does the First Schedule of the Indian Constitution contain?
exp: The First Schedule lists the names of the States and Union Territories with their territories. Oath forms are in the Third Schedule, salaries in the Second and Rajya Sabha seat allocation in the Fourth.

q: The "Goods and Services Tax (GST)" Council is responsible for making recommendations on various aspects of GST. Who chairs this Council?
o: Governor of the Reserve Bank of India
exp: The GST Council is chaired by the Union Finance Minister. The Union Minister of State for Finance and the Finance Ministers of the States are its members.

q: Who is the 15th President of India?
exp: Droupadi Murmu took office on 25 July 2022 as the 15th President of India. She is the first tribal person and the second woman to hold the office.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. As per Article 343 of the Indian Constitution, the Hindi language, written in the Devanagari script, is recognised as the "official language of the Central Government".
2. The Constitution permits the continuation of English for official purposes indefinitely and does not mention any Commission or Committee on Official Language.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
exp: Statement 1 is correct: Article 343 makes Hindi in Devanagari script the official language of the Union. Statement 2 is wrong: Article 344 provides for a Commission and a Committee of Parliament on Official Language.

q: A Judicial Magistrate who was exercising jurisdiction throughout District A is transferred to an equivalent post in another area within the same State. No fresh order conferring judicial powers is issued after the transfer. Can the Magistrate continue to exercise the same judicial powers under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 in India?
o: No, because powers must be conferred afresh after every transfer.
Yes, unless the High Court or the State Government directs otherwise.
Yes, but only for administrative powers, not for judicial powers.
No, because powers automatically lapse after the transfer.
exp: Under the BNSS, when an officer is posted to an equal or higher office of the same nature within the same State, he continues to exercise the same powers in the new area unless the High Court or the State Government directs otherwise.

q: What does the concept of 'Republic' in the Preamble of the Indian Constitution mean?
o: The head of state is elected
exp: In a Republic the head of the state is elected for a fixed term and is not a hereditary monarch. In India the President is elected indirectly for five years.

q: The real executive power in the Indian Union is exercised by:
exp: The President is the nominal (de jure) head. The real (de facto) executive power is used by the Prime Minister and the Council of Ministers, whose advice binds the President under Article 74.

q: Under Article 177 of the Indian Constitution, what specific limitation applies to a Minister or the Advocate General when they take part in the proceedings of a House?
o: They are prohibited from speaking in the Legislative Council
They cannot take part in committee meetings
They are not entitled to vote by virtue of this Article
They cannot address the House in their mother tongue
exp: Under Article 177 a Minister and the Advocate General can speak and take part in the proceedings of the House, but this Article does not give them the right to vote.

q: What is the difference between a bailable and non-bailable offence under BNSS?
o: Non-bailable offences can be compounded by the police
Bailable offences are listed in the First Schedule
Non-bailable offences can be granted bail by any officer
exp: Under the BNSS a bailable offence is one shown as bailable in the First Schedule or made bailable by another law. Every other offence is non-bailable.

q: A judicial magistrate's local jurisdiction extends partly into another district where he does not ordinarily hold court. A legal provision refers to "the Court of Session having jurisdiction". How should this expression be interpreted under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 in India?
o: It refers only to the sessions court where the magistrate physically sits.
It refers to the Sessions Court exercising jurisdiction over the concerned area.
It automatically refers to the High Court.
It refers to any sessions court chosen by the state government.
exp: For a Magistrate whose local jurisdiction extends beyond his own district, references to the Court of Session mean the Sessions Court that has jurisdiction over the area concerned.

q: A and B jointly decide to kill prisoner Z by starving him. A does not give food for the first three days, and B continues this omission for the next three days, as a result of which Z dies. Under Section 3(8) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 in India, which option best describes their liability?
o: Only B is guilty because his omission directly caused the death.
Only A is guilty because he initiated it.
Both A and B are guilty of murder through intentional cooperation.
Neither of them is guilty because omission alone cannot cause murder.
exp: Section 3(8) of the BNS: when an offence is committed by several acts, whoever intentionally cooperates by doing any one of those acts commits the offence. Both A and B are guilty of murder.

q: A catches B committing simple theft of a bicycle. B begins running away without violence. A shoots and kills B solely to recover the bicycle. Which of the following is correct under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 in India?
o: A is justified because private defence of property always includes killing a thief.
A is justified because the theft had already occurred.
A is not justified since the right didn't extend to causing death here.
A is justified because the property had not yet been recovered.
exp: Under Section 41 of the BNS the right of private defence of property extends to causing death only in cases such as robbery, house-breaking at night and mischief by fire. Simple theft is not covered, so A is not justified.

q: Ease of Doing Business reforms are most closely related to which of the following broader constitutional objectives?
o: Promoting judicial review and constitutional accountability
Promoting emergency governance and constitutional stability
Promoting a welfare state and socio-economic development
Promoting electoral representation and constitutional participation
exp: Easier business conditions bring investment, jobs and growth. This links to the Directive Principles, which aim at a welfare state and socio-economic development.

q: According to Article 76(1) of the Indian Constitution, a person appointed as Attorney-General for India must be qualified to be appointed as a:
exp: Under Article 76(1) the President appoints as Attorney-General a person who is qualified to be appointed a judge of the Supreme Court.

q: Which of the following is a benefit received by a retired President of India?
o: Lifetime free international travel for self and spouse
Appointment as Governor of a State with Cabinet rank benefits
Rent-free furnished bungalow, personal staff, and ₹2.5 lakh monthly pension
Membership to the Rajya Sabha for life
exp: Under the President's Emoluments and Pension Act a retired President gets a monthly pension (now Rs 2.5 lakh), a rent-free furnished house, secretarial staff and free travel within India.

q: When did the British first accept, in principle, the demand for an Indian Constituent Assembly?
exp: The August Offer of 1940, made by Viceroy Linlithgow, was the first time the British accepted in principle that Indians should frame their own constitution. The Cripps Mission (1942) gave a concrete proposal, and the Assembly was finally set up under the Cabinet Mission Plan (1946).

q: What does the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023 propose regarding the role of digital evidence in criminal cases?
o: Digital evidence can only be used if it is manually compiled
Digital evidence is not admissible in court without physical copies
Digital evidence must be verified and authenticated for it to be used in court
All digital evidence is automatically accepted in legal proceedings
exp: Digital evidence is admissible, but it has to be authenticated first, for example through a certificate under Section 63 of the BSA, before a court can rely on it.

q: Which Article of the Indian Constitution empowers the High Court to issue writs?
exp: Article 226 empowers High Courts to issue writs for Fundamental Rights and for any other purpose. Article 32 gives the Supreme Court writ power for Fundamental Rights only.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. India is a federal state because it has a written constitution.
2. The term 'quasi-federal' was used by K.C. Wheare to describe Indian federalism.
Which of the following statements is/are correct?
exp: Statement 1 is wrong: a written constitution alone does not make a state federal; division of powers is the key feature. Statement 2 is right: K.C. Wheare described the Indian Constitution as 'quasi-federal'.

q: Under the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, which of the following is considered a primary source of evidence in the digital era?
o: Printouts of WhatsApp chats without digital signature verification
Newspaper reports about a digital crime
Certified copies of electronic records with hash value authentication
Oral confessions made to a police officer
exp: Under the BSA an electronic record is proved with a certificate under Section 63, and hash-value authentication shows that the record has not been tampered with.

q: Which Article provides for the establishment of the Union Public Service Commission?
exp: Article 315 provides for a Public Service Commission for the Union and for each State. Article 320 lists their functions.

q: Under Article 65 of the Indian Constitution, who acts as the President when the office falls vacant due to the President's death, resignation or removal from office?
exp: Under Article 65 the Vice-President acts as President when the office falls vacant by death, resignation or removal, until a new President takes charge.

q: What is the punishment for cyber stalking under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023?
o: Imprisonment up to 3 years and fine
exp: Stalking, including monitoring a woman's use of the internet or email, is punished under Section 78 of the BNS: up to 3 years and fine on first conviction, and up to 5 years on a repeat conviction.

q: What is the minimum age required to become a member of the Rajya Sabha as per the Article 84 of the Indian Constitution?
exp: Article 84 fixes the minimum age at 30 years for the Rajya Sabha and 25 years for the Lok Sabha.

q: Which Schedule of the Indian Constitution contains provisions related to the Panchayati Raj system?
exp: The Eleventh Schedule, added by the 73rd Amendment, lists 29 subjects for Panchayats. The Twelfth Schedule lists 18 subjects for Municipalities.

q: A was earlier convicted under Chapter XVII with imprisonment for 4 years. After release, A again commits another offence under the same chapter punishable with imprisonment for 4 years. Which of the following is legally correct under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 in India?
o: A must necessarily be sentenced to life imprisonment.
A cannot be sentenced beyond 4 years because punishment cannot exceed that prescribed for the offence.
A becomes liable to either life imprisonment or imprisonment up to 10 years.
The previous conviction is irrelevant unless both offences are identical.
exp: Section 13 of the BNS: a person earlier convicted of an offence under Chapter X or XVII punishable with 3 years or more, who repeats such an offence, is liable to life imprisonment or imprisonment up to 10 years.

q: Article 131A was repealed and previously gave exclusive jurisdiction to ______.
exp: Article 131A, added by the 42nd Amendment (1976), gave the Supreme Court exclusive jurisdiction over the constitutional validity of Central laws. The 43rd Amendment (1977) repealed it.

q: In which Part of the Indian Constitution are the Fundamental Rights enshrined?
exp: Fundamental Rights are in Part III (Articles 12 to 35). Part II covers citizenship, Part IV the Directive Principles and Part I the Union and its territory.

q: By which Constitutional Amendment was the voting age in India reduced from 21 years to 18 years?
exp: The 61st Amendment Act, 1988 amended Article 326 and lowered the voting age from 21 to 18 years.

q: Under which Constitutional Amendment Act was Article 243ZI, concerning the incorporation of co-operative societies, inserted into the Indian Constitution?
exp: The 97th Amendment Act, 2011 added Part IXB (Articles 243ZH to 243ZT) on co-operative societies. It also added the right to form co-operatives in Article 19(1)(c) and Article 43B.

q: A State Government issues a notification applying only Chapters IX and XI of the B.N.S.S. (Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita), 2023 to certain tribal areas which were earlier excluded under Section 1(2). A lawyer argues that such a notification is invalid because the excluded areas can never be brought under the applicability of the B.N.S.S. Legally, which option is correct?
o: The lawyer is right because tribal areas enjoy permanent exemption.
The notification is invalid unless Parliament approves it separately.
B.N.S.S. (Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita) provisions can be applied with modifications by a State notification.
Only the Central Government can extend the BNSS (Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita) to tribal areas.
exp: Section 1 of the BNSS excludes Nagaland and the tribal areas from most of its provisions, but lets the State Government apply any of the provisions to those areas by notification, with modifications.

q: Which Commission was appointed to examine Center-State relations in 1983?
exp: The Sarkaria Commission was set up in 1983 to examine Centre-State relations and gave its report in 1988. Mandal dealt with backward classes, Kothari with education and Shah with Emergency excesses.

q: According to Article 83(2), what is the normal duration of the Lok Sabha (House of the People) from the date of its first meeting?
o: Four years from its first meeting
Five years from its first meeting
Six years from its first meeting
It is a permanent House of Parliament
exp: Article 83(2) gives the Lok Sabha a term of five years from the date of its first meeting, unless dissolved earlier. The Rajya Sabha is a permanent House.

q: According to Article 80 of the Indian Constitution, what is the maximum number of members to be nominated to the Rajya Sabha by the President?
exp: Under Article 80 the President nominates 12 members to the Rajya Sabha from persons with special knowledge of literature, science, art and social service.

q: During a trial, the defendant admits liability in the written pleadings but later tries to withdraw that admission. The plaintiff argues that no further evidence is now required. What is the correct legal position under the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 in India?
o: The admission is final and cannot be ignored.
The court is bound by the admission and cannot ask for evidence.
The court may require proof despite the admission.
The admission is irrelevant unless it is repeated orally in court.
exp: Section 53 of the BSA says admitted facts need not be proved, but the court may in its discretion still require them to be proved by other evidence.

q: Which part of the Indian Constitution deals with the official language of the Union?
exp: Part XVII (Articles 343 to 351) deals with Official Language.

q: In the Constitution of India, what does the phrase "Union of States" signify?
o: India follows a presidential form of government.
Federation is not the result of an agreement among states.
exp: Article 1 calls India a 'Union of States'. Dr. Ambedkar explained that the Indian federation is not the result of an agreement among states, and so no state has the right to secede.

q: The procedure for the impeachment of the President of India is laid down under Article ______ of the Indian Constitution.
exp: Article 61 lays down the impeachment procedure for the President on the ground of 'violation of the Constitution'. A two-thirds majority of the total membership of each House is required.

q: What is the subject matter of Article 126 of the Indian Constitution?
o: Appointment of judges of the Supreme Court
Powers of the Chief Justice of India
Retirement of judges of the Supreme Court
exp: Article 126 provides for the appointment of an acting Chief Justice of India by the President when the office is vacant or the Chief Justice is unable to perform duties.

q: The scrapping of the IPC, CrPC, and Evidence Act is seen as a step toward:
exp: The IPC (1860), CrPC and Evidence Act (1872) were colonial-era laws. Replacing them with the BNS, BNSS and BSA from 1 July 2024 is presented as decolonisation of the criminal justice system.

q: Under the provisions of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023, in India, A is accused of committing an offence in Bengaluru. The defence proves that A was in Delhi at the exact time the offence was committed. This fact is:
o: Relevant as part of the same transaction
Relevant as an exception under Section 10
Relevant because it is inconsistent with the fact in issue.
Irrelevant unless there is an agreement
exp: This is the plea of alibi. Section 9 of the BSA makes facts relevant if they are inconsistent with a fact in issue; being in Delhi makes it impossible to have committed the act in Bengaluru.

q: Which of the following is not a Directive Principle of State Policy under Part IV of the Indian Constitution?
exp: The Right to Constitutional Remedies is a Fundamental Right under Article 32 in Part III. Environment protection (Article 48A), equal pay for equal work (Article 39(d)) and village panchayats (Article 40) are Directive Principles.

q: Under the Indian Independence Act, full legislative authority in each Dominion was vested in which body?
exp: The Indian Independence Act, 1947 made the Constituent Assembly of each Dominion its legislature with full law-making power. The authority of the British Parliament over India ended on 15 August 1947.

q: In a murder trial, A claims that at the time of the act he was incapable of understanding the nature of his conduct due to unsoundness of mind. Under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 in India, under which category does this circumstance mainly fall?
exp: Whether the accused was of unsound mind decides his criminal liability, so it is a 'fact in issue': a fact from which the existence or extent of a right or liability directly follows.

q: A is attacked by a violent mob attempting to murder him. Young children are mixed within the mob. He can save himself only by firing into the crowd, though this creates risk to the children. A fire and one child die. Which of the following is correct under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 in India?
o: A is guilty because innocent persons can never be harmed in private defence.
A is guilty because children were present.
A remains protected because private defence allows unavoidable risk in such assaults.
A is protected only if no innocent person is actually injured.
exp: Section 44 of the BNS covers this exact situation: when a person facing a deadly assault cannot defend himself without risk of harm to an innocent person, his right of private defence extends to running that risk.

q: The power of the Supreme Court of India to pass orders for doing "complete justice" is provided under which Article of the Constitution of India?
exp: Article 142 lets the Supreme Court pass any decree or order needed to do 'complete justice' in a matter before it. Article 141 makes its law binding on all courts.

q: An offence is punishable only with imprisonment of up to two years. Owing to the seriousness of the allegations, the prosecution treats it as a warrant case. Under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) in India, which of the following statements is legally correct?
o: It is a warrant case because seriousness alone determines the classification.
It is a summons case because the punishment does not exceed two years.
If the police file a charge sheet, it becomes a warrant case.
The Magistrate can classify it in any manner.
exp: A warrant-case relates to an offence punishable with death, life imprisonment or imprisonment for more than two years. Every other case is a summons-case, so an offence with a maximum of two years is a summons-case.

q: Which was the first district in India to implement the third tier of Panchayati Raj governance?
exp: Panchayati Raj was inaugurated by Jawaharlal Nehru on 2 October 1959 at Nagaur in Rajasthan, following the Balwant Rai Mehta Committee's three-tier model. Andhra Pradesh was the second state.

q: Whose previous consent is mandatory for the appointment of an ad hoc Judge under Article 127 of the Indian Constitution?
exp: Under Article 127 the Chief Justice of India can appoint a High Court judge as an ad hoc judge of the Supreme Court when there is no quorum, with the previous consent of the President and after consulting the Chief Justice of the High Court concerned.

q: Who was appointed as the Chief Election Commissioner of India in May 2022?
exp: Rajiv Kumar took charge as the 25th Chief Election Commissioner on 15 May 2022, succeeding Sushil Chandra.

q: ______ was the first Comptroller and Auditor General of India.
exp: V. Narahari Rao was the first Comptroller and Auditor General of independent India, serving from 1948 to 1954.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Rajya Sabha can allow Parliament to make laws on State List.
2. Rajya Sabha can amend Money Bills and delay them for 14 days.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
exp: Statement 1 is correct: under Article 249 the Rajya Sabha can authorise Parliament to make laws on a State List subject. Statement 2 is wrong: the Rajya Sabha cannot amend a Money Bill; it can only make recommendations and must return it within 14 days.

q: The legislature of a state in India is called bicameral when it has both of the following:
exp: A bicameral state legislature has two Houses: the Legislative Assembly (Vidhan Sabha) and the Legislative Council (Vidhan Parishad). Six states have a Council at present.

q: Under Article 3 of the Indian Constitution, within what time limit does the President refer a Bill affecting the area, boundaries or name of a State to the Legislature of the concerned State for expressing its views?
o: A fixed period of six months prescribed in the Constitution
One session of the State Legislature
Such period as may be specified by the President
exp: Under Article 3, the President refers the Bill to the State Legislature to express its views within the period the President specifies. The President can extend the period, and Parliament is not bound by the views received.

q: As per Article 62(2) of the Constitution, if the office of the President falls vacant due to death, resignation, or removal, what is the maximum time limit prescribed for holding the election to fill that vacancy?
exp: Article 62(2) requires the election to fill such a vacancy to be held as soon as possible and in any case within six months of the vacancy.

q: Under which Article of the Indian Constitution was the Emergency of 1975 declared?
exp: The Emergency of 25 June 1975 was proclaimed under Article 352 on the ground of 'internal disturbance'. The 44th Amendment later replaced this ground with 'armed rebellion'.

q: What is the main difficulty in establishing efficient Alternative Dispute Resolution (ADR) processes to boost business operations in regions with weak legal systems?
o: Limited access to experienced ADR professionals and problems in enforcing arbitration awards.
Excessive reliance on traditional court systems for resolving business disputes.
Widespread use of common international arbitration standards.
Widespread reliance on informal methods of conflict resolution.
exp: ADR works only if trained arbitrators and mediators are available and if awards can be enforced. In regions with weak legal systems both of these are missing.

q: A police officer receives a warrant to arrest "R". After conducting a reasonable inquiry and acting in good faith, he arrests S, believing S to be R. Later it is discovered that S was entirely innocent, and the warrant never applied to him. Which of the following is the most accurate legal position under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 in India?
o: The officer is liable because wrongful arrest always constitutes an offence.
The officer is protected only if the court issuing the warrant has jurisdiction.
The officer is protected because of a mistake of fact made in good faith.
The officer is liable because identity mistakes are mistakes of law.
exp: The general exceptions of the BNS protect a person who, by a mistake of fact made in good faith, believes he is bound by law to do an act. The officer acted on a warrant after due inquiry, so he commits no offence.

q: Which of the following major changes has been introduced in the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 in place of the Indian Penal Code (IPC) 1860?
o: Introduction of community service as a punishment
Replacing all criminal laws with a Uniform Civil Code
Removal of the sedition law without any replacement
Complete abolition of the death penalty
exp: The BNS introduced community service as a new form of punishment for certain petty offences (Section 4). Sedition was replaced by Section 152, and the death penalty remains.

q: In India, which Constitutional Amendment Act is popularly known as the "Mini-Constitution"?
exp: The 42nd Amendment Act, 1976 made so many changes, including the Preamble, Fundamental Duties and several Articles, that it is called the 'Mini-Constitution'.

q: In the Indian parliamentary system, which statement most appropriately describes the principle of collective responsibility?
o: Cabinet decisions are binding on all ministers
exp: Collective responsibility means the Cabinet stands or falls together. A decision of the Cabinet binds every minister, and a minister who disagrees must resign.

q: In India, a law made by Parliament under Article 249 on a subject in the State List remains in force:
o: Only during the validity of the Rajya Sabha resolution
For six months after the resolution ceases to be in force
Till the concerned state legislature repeals it
exp: A resolution under Article 249 stays in force for up to one year at a time. A law made under it stops having effect six months after the resolution ceases to be in force.

q: A State Government constitutes a Special Court of Judicial Magistrates of the First Class for cyber fraud cases in a city. Later, a regular Judicial Magistrate of the First Class of the same area takes cognizance of a cyber fraud case and begins trial proceedings. Under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) in India, which of the following statements is legally correct?
o: The regular Magistrate can proceed because all Judicial Magistrates have concurrent jurisdiction.
The regular Magistrate can proceed only with the approval of the Sessions Judge.
If the case falls under the class assigned to the Special Court, the regular Magistrate lacks jurisdiction.
The Special Court can hear only appeals, not trials.
exp: When a Special Court of Judicial Magistrates is set up for a particular class of cases, no other Magistrate's court in that local area has jurisdiction to try cases of that class.

q: As per Article 72 of the Indian Constitution, what is the meaning of the 'commutation' power granted to the President of India?
exp: Commutation means replacing one form of punishment with a lighter form, for example death sentence changed to life imprisonment. Reprieve is temporary suspension, and respite is a lesser sentence on special grounds.

q: A is accused of robbery. Immediately after the incident, A runs away, and a witness hears someone shouting, "The robber escaped." Which of the following statements is correct under the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 in India?
o: The shout and flight are irrelevant because they are not facts in issue.
The shout is relevant only as confession.
Both are relevant as conduct under Section 6
exp: Under Section 6 of the BSA, the conduct of the accused such as running away after the incident, and statements that accompany and explain that conduct, are relevant.

q: Under Article 113 of the Indian Constitution, which House of Parliament has the exclusive power to assent to or refuse a demand for grant of expenditure?
exp: Under Article 113 demands for grants are placed before the Lok Sabha, which alone can assent to, reduce or refuse them. The Rajya Sabha has no vote on demands for grants.

q: Which Article of the Constitution was called the 'heart and soul' by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar?
exp: Dr. Ambedkar called Article 32 (Right to Constitutional Remedies) the 'heart and soul' of the Constitution, because it lets a person move the Supreme Court directly to enforce Fundamental Rights.

q: Which Schedule lists the subjects falling under the Union, State and Concurrent Lists?
o: Sixth Schedule of the Indian Constitution
Seventh Schedule of the Indian Constitution
Eighth Schedule of the Indian Constitution
Fifth Schedule of the Indian Constitution
exp: The Seventh Schedule (Article 246) has three lists: Union List, State List and Concurrent List. The Fifth and Sixth Schedules deal with scheduled and tribal areas, and the Eighth with languages.

q: Which Article under the Indian Constitution lays down the establishment and composition of the Supreme Court?
exp: Article 124 establishes the Supreme Court and provides for its composition and the appointment of judges.

q: Under which constitutional provision of the Constitution of India is the Goods and Services Tax (GST) Council established?
exp: Article 279A, inserted by the 101st Amendment, provides for the GST Council. Article 246A gives the power to levy GST and Article 269A covers IGST.

q: A private citizen sees a police officer struggling to prevent an accused, who has been lawfully arrested in connection with an offence of dacoity/robbery, from escaping. The police officer reasonably requests the citizen for assistance, but the citizen refuses. Under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023, which of the following statements is the most accurate?
o: Whether to assist or not depends entirely on the citizen's discretion.
Assisting is mandatory only for government employees.
There is a duty to assist in preventing the escape of an arrested person when reasonably required.
Assisting becomes mandatory only after receiving a written order from a Magistrate.
exp: Every person is bound to assist a police officer who reasonably demands help in preventing the escape of a person he is authorised to arrest. Intentional refusal is punishable under the BNS.

q: By which Constitutional Amendment Act was Article 246A inserted into the Constitution of India?
exp: The 101st Amendment Act, 2016 introduced GST and inserted Article 246A, which gives both Parliament and State Legislatures the power to make laws on GST.

q: Under which Article of the Indian Constitution is provision made for the ancillary powers of the Supreme Court?
exp: Article 140 lets Parliament give the Supreme Court supplementary (ancillary) powers to help it use its jurisdiction more effectively.

q: Under the Constitution of India, in which list of the Seventh Schedule does "Public Order" fall?
exp: 'Public order' is Entry 1 and 'Police' is Entry 2 of the State List in the Seventh Schedule.

q: Article 54 of the Indian Constitution deals with the:
exp: Article 54 deals with the election of the President by an electoral college. The term is in Article 56, the oath in Article 60 and impeachment in Article 61.

q: The office of sessions judge in a sessions division suddenly becomes vacant. An urgent bail application is pending. There is no additional sessions judge available in that division. Who may legally dispose of the application under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 in India?
exp: When the office of the Sessions Judge is vacant, the High Court may arrange for urgent applications to be disposed of by an Additional Sessions Judge or, if there is none, by the Chief Judicial Magistrate.

q: A Sessions Judge sentences an accused to death. Before the sentence is confirmed by the High Court, the convict files an appeal, contending that the sentence is already executable because a Sessions Judge is empowered to pass "any sentence authorized by law." Which of the following is correct under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 in India?
o: Correct, because session judges possess complete sentencing authority.
Incorrect, because High Court must confirm all death sentences.
Correct only if the offense is against the state.
Incorrect only when the trial was conducted by an additional sessions judge.
exp: A Sessions Judge may pass any sentence authorised by law, but under the BNSS a death sentence cannot be executed until it is confirmed by the High Court.

q: Which Article of the Indian Constitution restricts Parliament from discussing the conduct of a Judge of the Supreme Court or a High Court in the discharge of his duties?
exp: Article 121 bars any discussion in Parliament on the conduct of a Supreme Court or High Court judge in the discharge of duties, except on a motion for the judge's removal.

q: Under which specific provision of the Indian Constitution is the executive power vested in the President to act as the Supreme Commander of the Defence Forces?
exp: Article 53(2) vests the supreme command of the Defence Forces of the Union in the President, to be exercised as regulated by law.

q: Under which Article of the Constitution of India does Parliament have the power to alter the name, area, or boundaries of a State?
exp: Article 3 allows Parliament to form new states and alter the area, boundaries or name of existing states. Article 2 deals with admission or establishment of new states, and Article 4 with the consequential changes to the Schedules.

q: By which Constitutional Amendment Act was Article 239AA added, making special provisions for the Union Territory of Delhi?
exp: The 69th Amendment Act, 1991 added Articles 239AA and 239AB, named Delhi the National Capital Territory and gave it a Legislative Assembly and Council of Ministers.

q: In India, under what circumstance can Parliament make a law on a subject in the State List without declaring a national emergency?
o: When the Lok Sabha passes a resolution by a simple majority.
When the Rajya Sabha passes a resolution by a two-thirds majority of members present and voting.
When the President issues an ordinance.
When the Supreme Court advises the Union Government.
exp: Under Article 249, if the Rajya Sabha passes a resolution by two-thirds of the members present and voting that it is in the national interest, Parliament can legislate on a State List subject.

q: Which document is called the 'identity card' of the Indian Constitution?
exp: N.A. Palkhivala called the Preamble the 'identity card of the Constitution' because it sums up the source, nature and objectives of the Constitution.

q: A police inspector investigates a criminal case. Later, due to the unavailability of prosecutors, the District Magistrate appointed the same inspector as Assistant Public Prosecutor for that case. Which of the following is correct under the 'Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023' in India?
o: Valid: because an inspector fulfils the rank requirement.
Invalid: the investigating officer cannot act as Assistant Public Prosecutor in the same case.
Invalid: if the accused gives consent.
Valid: because the appointment is temporary.
exp: The BNSS bars a police officer from being appointed Assistant Public Prosecutor if he has taken any part in the investigation of that case.

q: A sees a child trapped inside a burning house. To save the child, A throws the child from the roof onto a blanket held below, knowing the fall could kill the child. The child dies from the fall. Which is the strongest legal conclusion under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 in India?
o: A is guilty because he knowingly caused death.
A is guilty because the child did not consent.
A is protected because the act was done in good faith for the child's benefit with the possibility of obtaining consent.
A is protected only if the child survives.
exp: Section 30 of the BNS protects an act done in good faith for a person's benefit, even without consent, when it is impossible to obtain consent in time. Dropping a child from a burning house to save its life is a classic example of this protection.

q: A, under grave and sudden provocation, attacks Z, resulting in culpable homicide not amounting to murder. B, who secretly hated Z and was not provoked, joins A and knowingly helps in killing Z. What is the correct legal position under Section 3(9) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 in India?
o: Both A and B are guilty only of culpable homicide not amounting to murder.
Both A and B are guilty of murder because they committed the offence together.
A is guilty of culpable homicide not amounting to murder, whereas B is guilty of murder.
A is innocent because he was provoked, but only B is guilty of murder.
exp: Section 3(9) of the BNS: when several persons take part in one criminal act, each may be guilty of a different offence according to his own intention. A, who was provoked, commits culpable homicide; B, who was not, commits murder.

q: Which of the following changes the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam (BSA), introduced in relation to electronic evidence, compared to the Indian Evidence Act?
o: Recognizes electronic records as equivalent to oral statements
Broadens scope to include blockchain, cloud logs, and forensic audit trails
exp: The BSA widens the definition of electronic records to cover data from devices, servers, cloud storage and similar digital trails, and treats such records as documents.

q: The power of superintendence and control of elections is vested in which Article?
exp: Article 324 vests the superintendence, direction and control of elections in the Election Commission of India.

q: Under which Article of the Indian Constitution has the office of the President of India been established?
exp: Article 52 states that there shall be a President of India. Article 54 deals with the election of the President.

q:
Consider the statements given below:
1. Promotion of international peace is a part of the DPSP.
2. DPSP can be enforced by the courts.
3. Protection of monuments is a Fundamental Right.
Which is/are true?
exp: Only statement 1 is true: promotion of international peace is a Directive Principle (Article 51). Directive Principles are not enforceable by courts (Article 37), and protection of monuments is also a Directive Principle (Article 49), not a Fundamental Right.

q: Which article of the Constitution of India explicitly states that Union Ministers shall hold office during the pleasure of the President?
exp: Article 75(2) says ministers hold office during the pleasure of the President. The same Article covers their appointment and collective responsibility.

q: Name of the tribal panchayat in Kerala?
exp: Edamalakkudy in Idukki district, home to the Muthuvan tribe, became Kerala's first tribal gram panchayat in 2010.

q: What does the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) state regarding "mercy petitions" in death sentence cases?
o: No mercy petition allowed after the trial
The President decides alone without consulting the States
Multiple petitions allowed across different jurisdictions
Clear timelines for filing and disposal
exp: Section 472 of the BNSS sets time limits for mercy petitions: a convict must file within 30 days, and timelines are fixed for the governments to forward and decide them.

q: Under which Article of the Indian Constitution is the State Legislature empowered to make provisions for the maintenance of accounts by the Panchayats and the auditing of such accounts?
exp: Article 243J lets the State Legislature make provisions for the maintenance of accounts by Panchayats and their audit.

q:
Arrange the following developments in federal structure chronologically:
1. Formation of Inter-State Council
2. 73rd Constitutional Amendment
3. GST Council formation
exp: Inter-State Council: 1990. 73rd Constitutional Amendment: passed in 1992, in force from 1993. GST Council: 2016. So the order is 1-2-3.

q:
In a dispute over whether villagers have a right to use a pond, the court considers the following:
(i) testimony of elderly villagers
(ii) written government notification denying such right
Which is legally correct under Section 42 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023, in India?
o: Only elderly villagers' opinions are relevant.
Both are irrelevant because customs cannot be proved by opinion.
Elderly villagers' opinions are relevant as they likely know the custom.
exp: Section 42 of the BSA makes relevant the opinions of persons who would be likely to know of the existence of a general custom or right. Elderly villagers are such persons.

q: A Chief Judicial Magistrate issues an administrative order redistributing criminal cases among his subordinate Judicial Magistrates. One of the magistrates challenges this order, arguing that the power to distribute judicial business lies only with the Sessions Judge. Which of the following statements is correct under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023 in India?
o: Only the Sessions Judge can distribute the business of Magistrates.
The Chief Judicial Magistrate has the power to distribute business among Judicial Magistrates.
Approval of the Executive Magistrate is required for distribution of business.
Only the High Court can allocate all criminal cases.
exp: Under the BNSS the Chief Judicial Magistrate may make rules or give special orders on the distribution of business among the Judicial Magistrates subordinate to him.

q: The Union Territory of Puducherry (Pondicherry) has its territories spread across which of the following states?
o: Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, and Maharashtra
Tamil Nadu, Kerala, and Andhra Pradesh
exp: Puducherry has four separate districts: Puducherry and Karaikal are enclaves in Tamil Nadu, Mahe is in Kerala and Yanam is in Andhra Pradesh.

q: A prosecution relates to an offence punishable with imprisonment for life. Which authority under the Directorate of Prosecution has the primary statutory duty to monitor such cases and advise on filing appeals under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 in India?
exp: Under Section 20 of the BNSS the Director of Prosecution monitors cases punishable with ten years or more, life imprisonment or death. The Deputy Director handles 7 to 10 year cases and the Assistant Director cases below 7 years.

q: Under Article 20(1) of the Indian Constitution, protection against ex post facto laws applies primarily to:
exp: Article 20(1) bars retrospective criminal laws: no one can be convicted for an act that was not an offence when done, or given a heavier penalty than the one then in force. Civil and tax laws can still apply retrospectively.

q: The Vice-President is the second-highest constitutional authority of India under which Part of the Indian Constitution?
exp: Part V (The Union) covers the President, Vice-President, Council of Ministers, Parliament and the Supreme Court. Part VI deals with the States.

q: The Supreme Court's decision in Supriyo v. Union of India (2023) concerned:
exp: In Supriyo v. Union of India (2023) a five-judge bench declined to legalise same-sex marriage and held that there is no fundamental right to marry. It left the matter to Parliament.

q: In India, which constitutional authority can recommend the imposition of President's Rule in a State by sending a report to the President under Article 356 of the Constitution?
exp: Under Article 356 the President can act on a report from the Governor of the State (or otherwise) that the government of the State cannot be carried on according to the Constitution.

q: The "National Food Security Act (NFSA), 2013" has a primary objective related to food and nutrition. Which of the following best describes this objective?
o: To promote organic farming practices across the country.
To ensure foodgrain procurement at Minimum Support Price (MSP) for all crops.
To provide subsidized foodgrains to a significant proportion of the population.
To encourage the export of surplus foodgrains to boost the agricultural economy.
exp: The National Food Security Act, 2013 gives a legal right to subsidised foodgrains to up to 75% of the rural and 50% of the urban population, about two-thirds of the country.

q: Which of the following best defines a "document" under the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023?
o: Only written paper records signed by parties
Only electronic records generated by computers
Any matter recorded by letters, figures, marks, or electronic or digital means intended for recording matter
exp: The BSA defines 'document' as any matter expressed or described on any substance by letters, figures or marks, or any other means, and it expressly includes electronic and digital records.

q: What is the primary objective of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023?
o: To regulate the conduct of civil trials
To consolidate and amend the law relating to evidence
exp: The long title of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 says it is an Act to consolidate and to provide for general rules and principles of evidence for fair trial.

q: A warrant is issued for execution by a private person (not a police officer). During its execution, nearby civilians voluntarily assist because the person executing the warrant is actively pursuing the accused. Which of the following statements is legally correct under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 in India?
o: Civilians cannot assist because only police may execute warrants.
Assistance is lawful if the person to whom the warrant is directed is near at hand and acting in execution.
Civilian assistance requires prior magistrate approval.
Only executive magistrates may assist in non-police warrant execution.
exp: When a warrant is directed to a person other than a police officer, any other person may help in executing it if the person to whom it is directed is near at hand and acting in its execution.

q: Who was the first Chairman of the Union Public Service Commission (UPSC)?
exp: Sir Ross Barker was the first Chairman of the Public Service Commission set up in 1926, which later became the UPSC.

q: Which Article of the Indian Constitution provides constitutional protection to the President and Governors from certain court proceedings during their term of office?
exp: Article 361 protects the President and Governors: they are not answerable to any court for official acts, and no criminal proceedings or arrest can be started against them during their term.

q: The term "cognizable offence" refers to an offence where:
o: The Magistrate has to permit arrest
The police officer can arrest without warrant
A person can only be summoned
exp: A cognizable offence is one for which a police officer may arrest without a warrant, as per the First Schedule of the BNSS or any other law.

q: Under which article of the Indian Constitution is it mandatory to constitute a District Planning Committee (DPC) in every State?
exp: Article 243ZD requires every State to set up a District Planning Committee at the district level to combine the plans of Panchayats and Municipalities into a draft district plan.

q: Which Amendment transferred education from the State List to the Concurrent List?
exp: The 42nd Amendment Act, 1976 moved five subjects from the State List to the Concurrent List: education, forests, weights and measures, protection of wild animals and birds, and administration of justice.

q: As per Article 75 of the Constitution of India, the Council of Ministers holds collective responsibility to which institution?
exp: Article 75(3) makes the Council of Ministers collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha (House of the People). If the Lok Sabha passes a no-confidence motion, the whole Council must resign.

q: In India, residuary legislative powers are vested in which of the following?
exp: Under Article 248 the residuary powers, meaning subjects not found in any of the three lists, belong to Parliament. This was borrowed from the Canadian model.

q:
Match the following Constitutional Articles (List I) with their provisions (List II) and select the correct option:
List I (Articles) — List II (Provisions)
I. Article 140 — 1. Formation of the Finance Commission
II. Article 280 — 2. Provision for President's Rule
III. Article 356 — 3. Ancillary powers of the Supreme Court
exp: Article 140: ancillary powers of the Supreme Court. Article 280: Finance Commission. Article 356: President's Rule. So I-3, II-1, III-2.

q: In India, which Article of the Constitution empowers Parliament to exclude the jurisdiction of the Supreme Court in matters relating to inter-State water disputes?
exp: Under Article 262 Parliament can provide for adjudication of inter-State river water disputes and can exclude the jurisdiction of the Supreme Court and other courts over them.

q: Which Article of the Indian Constitution specifies the languages to be used for transacting business in Parliament?
exp: Article 120 says the business of Parliament is transacted in Hindi or English, and the presiding officer may allow a member to speak in the mother tongue.

q: A statute authorizes a "magistrate" to suspend licences for public safety reasons. The function is purely administrative and involves no adjudication of guilt or appreciation of evidence. Under Section 3 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 in India, who should ordinarily exercise this power?
exp: Section 3 of the BNSS: functions that involve weighing evidence or deciding guilt go to a Judicial Magistrate, and administrative or executive functions such as granting or suspending a licence go to an Executive Magistrate.

q: Under which Article of the Indian Constitution is the Metropolitan Planning Committee provided for?
exp: Article 243ZE provides for a Metropolitan Planning Committee in every metropolitan area. Article 243ZD is for the District Planning Committee.

q: According to Article 64 of the Indian Constitution, the Vice-President of India is the ex officio Chairman of the:
exp: Article 64 makes the Vice-President the ex officio Chairman of the Council of States, that is, the Rajya Sabha.

q: Which article of the Indian Constitution empowers Parliament to determine the salaries and allowances of its members?
exp: Article 106 says members of Parliament receive salaries and allowances as decided by Parliament by law.

q: The Constitution is described as:
o: A purely legal code without moral content
A moral compass and embodiment of people's aspirations
exp: The Constitution is not just a legal rulebook. It carries the values, goals and aspirations of the people, so it is described as a moral compass for the nation.

q: According to Article 178 of the Indian Constitution, if the office of the Speaker or Deputy Speaker of the Legislative Assembly becomes vacant, what should the Legislative Assembly do?
o: Request the Governor to appoint a temporary officer
Leave the post vacant until the next general election
Choose another member of the Legislative Assembly to fill the vacancy
Transfer the duties to the Chairman of the Legislative Council
exp: Article 178 requires the Assembly to choose a Speaker and a Deputy Speaker, and whenever either office falls vacant the Assembly must choose another member to fill it.

q: A surgeon performs a risky operation on Z with Z's valid consent. The surgeon knows death is likely but acts in good faith solely to cure Z, without intending death. Z dies during surgery. Which of the following best reflects the legal principle under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 in India?
o: The surgeon is guilty because knowledge of likely death always creates liability.
The Surgeon protected as act was in good faith with Z's consent for Z's benefit.
The surgeon is protected only if death was impossible to foresee.
Consent is irrelevant where death occurs.
exp: Section 26 of the BNS protects an act not intended to cause death, done in good faith for a person's benefit and with his consent, even if the doer knows it is likely to cause harm.

q: Fill in the blanks: The Mando song, known for its emotional depth and cultural fusion, originated in Goa and typically deals with themes such as love, tragedy, and ______.
exp: Mando is a slow song-and-dance form of the Goan Catholic community that blends Konkani melodies with Portuguese music. Its themes are love, tragedy, and social and political resistance during Portuguese rule.

q: Which of the following is the correct match of a traditional folk dance and its related state?
exp: Khamba Thoibi is a folk dance of Manipur based on the love story of Khamba and Thoibi. Bhortal is from Assam, Pung Cholom from Manipur and Chang Lo from Nagaland.

q: Which of the following pairs of traditional folk dance and its associated state is correctly matched?
exp: Gendi is a stilt dance of Chhattisgarh. Cheraw (bamboo dance) is from Mizoram, Hojagiri from Tripura and Baredi from Madhya Pradesh.

q: Identify the correct match between the traditional folk dance and its associated state:
exp: Matki is a folk dance of the Malwa region of Madhya Pradesh, performed by women with an earthen pot. Pandavani is from Chhattisgarh, Chai Lam from Mizoram and Karakattam from Tamil Nadu.

q: Which two emotions are primarily expressed through the "Chawnglaizawn" folk dance?
exp: Chawnglaizawn is a traditional dance of the Mizo (Lai) people that expresses both mourning and joy, so the answer is mourning and joy.

q: The 'Lavani' folk music, known for its powerful rhythm and lyrics, originates from which state?
exp: Lavani is the folk music and dance of Maharashtra, performed to the beat of the dholki and linked to the Tamasha theatre.

q: Why do tribal communities in Chhattisgarh traditionally perform the 'Suwa' (Parrot) dance?
o: To please the local rain gods
To honor the spirits of ancestors
To please the Goddess of Wealth
To celebrate victory after a tribal war
exp: Suwa is the parrot dance performed by tribal women of Chhattisgarh around Diwali. It is performed to please the Goddess of Wealth, as per the answer key.

q:
Which of the following statements about the tribal dance form 'Dhimsa' is/are correct?
1. Dhimsa originated in the Koraput district of Odisha.
2. It depicts daily tribal activities such as farming and gathering leaves.
3. It is now performed mainly in the urban centres of Tamil Nadu.
exp: Dhimsa is a tribal dance of the Koraput (Odisha) and Araku (Andhra Pradesh) region and shows daily activities like farming. It is not an urban dance of Tamil Nadu, so statement 3 is wrong.

q:
Consider the following statements about the musical instrument Santoor:
1. Santoor is a trapezoidal instrument.
2. It is traditionally associated with Kashmir.
3. It is primarily used in Carnatic music.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
exp: The santoor is a trapezoid-shaped hammered string instrument from Kashmir. It is used in Hindustani music, popularised by Pt. Shivkumar Sharma, and not in Carnatic music, so statement 3 is wrong.

q: Sitar maestro Ravi Shankar contributed significantly to:
o: Popularizing Indian folk traditions in the West exclusively
Introducing Indian classical music to Western audiences
exp: Pt. Ravi Shankar took Indian classical music to the West through concerts and his work with George Harrison and Yehudi Menuhin. He received the Bharat Ratna in 1999.

q: Which folk tradition is associated with the Manganiyar and Langa communities?
exp: Manganiyar and Langa are hereditary Muslim musician communities of western Rajasthan, known for folk music with instruments like the kamaicha and sindhi sarangi.

q: In which Indian musical tradition is the "Mridangam" a significant percussion instrument?
exp: The mridangam is the main percussion instrument of Carnatic classical music. The tabla plays that role in Hindustani music.

q: Which of the following pairs is incorrectly matched?
exp: Kumar Gandharva was a Hindustani classical vocalist, not a guitarist. The other pairs are correct: Dwaram Venkataswamy Naidu (violin), Vikku Vinayakram (ghatam) and Nikhil Ghosh (tabla).

q: Bhatiyali is a traditional music style associated with which state of India?
exp: Bhatiyali is the song of the boatmen of Bengal, sung while rowing downstream. It is associated with West Bengal and Bangladesh.

q:
Consider the following pairs of folk music traditions/ballads and their corresponding states:
1. Jammukula – Manipur
2. Baans Geet – Chattisgarh
Which of the pairs given above is/are correctly matched?
exp: Baans Geet is a ballad tradition of Chhattisgarh sung with a long bamboo instrument. Jammukula (Jamukula Katha) belongs to Andhra Pradesh, not Manipur.

q: Which of the following terms refers to the primary form of compositions in the Carnatic music tradition?
exp: Kriti is the main compositional form of Carnatic music, with pallavi, anupallavi and charanam. Bandish, ghazal and thumri belong to the Hindustani side.

q:
Consider the following pairs of Indian musical instruments and their types: 1 Chinkara – Stringed instrument
2. Ghatam – Percussion instrument
3. Kartal – Percussion/clapper instrument
Which of the above pairs is/are correctly matched?
exp: All three pairs are correct. Chinkara is a bowed string instrument, ghatam is a clay-pot percussion instrument and kartal is a wooden clapper.
