exp: Karl Marx set out the idea of a socialist economy in 'The Communist Manifesto' (1848) and 'Das Kapital'. Adam Smith, Marshall and Ricardo belong to the classical school.

q: Which dimension of the Human Development Index (HDI) is most directly linked to longevity?
exp: The health dimension of HDI is measured by life expectancy at birth, which is a direct measure of longevity.

q: For what purpose is Purchasing Power Parity (PPP) mainly used in the calculation of the Human Development Index (HDI)?
o: To compare income levels of different countries, taking into account differences in the cost of living
To compare unemployment levels in different countries, taking into account differences in labour-force participation
To compare population growth rates in different countries, taking into account differences in demographic trends
To compare literacy levels in different countries, taking into account differences in educational systems
exp: Purchasing Power Parity converts incomes into a common unit that allows for the different cost of living in each country, so real income levels can be compared.

q: What does the increasing contribution of the services sector after India's 1991 economic reforms mainly indicate?
o: Structural decline of the agricultural sector
Structural decline in the industrial sector
exp: A rising share of services in output is a sign of structural transformation, in which the economy shifts from agriculture to industry and services.

q: Which of the following is the best example of dynamic economic analysis?
o: Examining consumer demand at a particular point in time
Comparing the inflation rates of two countries during the same year
Analysing the changes in consumer demand over a period of several years
Examining an economy assuming all variables remain unchanged
exp: Dynamic analysis studies change over time. Looking at how consumer demand changes over several years is dynamic; studying a single point in time is static analysis.

q: The human development approach underlying the Human Development Index is mainly concerned with which of the following?
exp: The human development approach of Mahbub ul Haq and Amartya Sen treats development as the expansion of people's capabilities and choices, not just a rise in income.

q: Why does the fundamental economic problem of scarcity arise?
o: Because governments intentionally limit all production
Because firms always attempt to maximise profits
Because the prices of all goods remain high
exp: Scarcity arises because human wants are unlimited while the resources to satisfy them are limited. This forces choice, which is the basic economic problem.

q: Which of the following effects does a rise in the price of goods have on consumer surplus?
exp: Consumer surplus is the gap between what a buyer is willing to pay and what is actually paid. A higher price narrows that gap, so consumer surplus falls.

q: Which of the following would cause a movement along a supply curve rather than a shift in the supply curve?
o: An increase in the number of producers
An increase in the commodity's own price
exp: A change in the good's own price causes a movement along the supply curve. Technology, input prices and the number of producers shift the whole curve.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes movement along a demand curve from a shift in the demand curve?
o: Both are caused only by price changes.
Movement occurs due to income changes and shifts due to price changes.
Movement occurs due to own price changes, shift due to other determinants.
A shift means only a change in quantity demanded.
exp: A change in the good's own price moves the consumer along the demand curve. A change in income, tastes or the price of related goods shifts the entire curve.

q: If the selling price of milk rises sharply, what is the most likely effect on the supply of butter, assuming milk can either be sold directly or used to produce butter?
exp: If milk sells at a high price, producers prefer to sell milk directly rather than convert it into butter. So less milk goes into butter and the supply of butter falls.

q: A leftward shift of the demand curve of a commodity indicates:
exp: A leftward shift means less is bought at every price, which is a decrease in demand. A change caused by price alone would be a movement along the curve.

q: A university raises its tuition fee by 20%. As a result, student enrolment decreases by 30%, while all other factors remain unchanged. Which of the following statements correctly describes the price elasticity of demand and the resulting change in the university's total tuition revenue?
o: Demand is inelastic, and total tuition revenue increases.
Demand is elastic, and total tuition revenue decreases.
Demand is unit elastic, and total tuition revenue remains unchanged.
Demand is perfectly elastic, and total tuition revenue becomes zero.
exp: Elasticity = 30% fall in quantity / 20% rise in price = 1.5, which is greater than 1, so demand is elastic. When demand is elastic, a price rise lowers total revenue.

q: Which of the following factors does not determine demand?
exp: The price of factors of production, such as wages and rent, affects cost and therefore supply. Demand depends on the good's price, consumer income and the price of related goods.

q: Who among the following explained the substitution and income effect?
exp: J.R. Hicks and R.G.D. Allen separated the price effect into the substitution effect and the income effect in their 1934 work on ordinal utility.

q: Which of the following factors will increase the demand for laptops and shift their demand curve to the right?
o: Increase in the price of laptops
Decrease in consumer income, assuming laptops are normal goods
Increase in the price of internet services used with laptops
Increase in consumers' preference for online education
exp: A stronger preference for online education raises the demand for laptops at every price, so the demand curve shifts to the right.

q: If a consumer's income increases, resulting in greater consumption of good X and lower consumption of good Y, which of the following is correct?
o: Both X and Y are inferior goods.
X is an inferior good, while Y is a normal good.
X is a normal good, while Y is an inferior good.
Both X and Y are normal goods.
exp: When income rises, demand for a normal good goes up and demand for an inferior good goes down. Here X rises and Y falls, so X is normal and Y is inferior.

q: If the price of a commodity decreases from ₹100 to ₹105 and the quantity demanded decreases from 100 to 115, what is the value of price elasticity?
exp: Elasticity = percentage change in quantity / percentage change in price = 15/100 divided by 5/100 = 3. (The question's wording says 'decreases' for both figures, but the numbers given are increases.)

q: Why is the demand for salt generally less price-elastic than the demand for branded chocolate?
o: Salt has more close substitutes than branded chocolate.
Salt takes up a large share of consumers' income.
Salt is a necessity and has relatively few close substitutes.
exp: Salt is a necessity with few substitutes and takes a tiny share of income, so buyers keep buying it when the price rises. That makes its demand inelastic.

q: What does a consumption combination lying below the consumer's budget line indicate?
o: Some portion of the consumer's utility remains unattained.
Some portion of the required expenditure exceeds the consumer's income.
Some portion of the consumer's income remains unspent.
Some portion of the maximum possible utility remains unattained.
exp: A point below the budget line costs less than the consumer's income, so part of the income is left unspent. Points on the line use up the whole income.

q: Which of the following is the correct explanation of a consumer surplus?
o: What the consumer pays (-) what it is worth
What the consumer is ready to pay (-) what they actually pay
What the seller quotes as the price (-) what the consumer actually pays
What the seller quotes as the price (-) cost of manufacturing to the seller
exp: Consumer surplus is what the buyer was ready to pay minus what the buyer actually paid. The idea comes from Alfred Marshall.

q: Which of the following indicators is used to measure the standard of living dimension of the Human Development Index (HDI)?
o: Gross National Income (GNI) per capita based on Purchasing Power Parity (PPP)
Gross Domestic Product (GDP) per capita based on Purchasing Power Parity (PPP)
Net National Product (NNP) per capita based on Purchasing Power Parity (PPP)
Disposable income per capita based on Purchasing Power Parity (PPP)
exp: The standard of living dimension of the HDI is measured by Gross National Income per capita at Purchasing Power Parity.

q: Which country has the highest GDP in South Asia?
exp: India has the largest economy in South Asia by a wide margin, far ahead of Pakistan, Bangladesh and Sri Lanka.

q: Why were high rates of domestic savings and investment important for India's economic growth after the 1991 reforms?
o: They increase the fiscal deficit and weaken financial stability
They discourage entrepreneurship and limit business expansion.
They boost capital formation and long-term growth potential.
They reduce productive capacity and limit economic growth.
exp: Savings finance investment, and investment builds capital. Higher capital formation raises the economy's capacity to produce, so it supports long-term growth.

q: Which of the following statements is correct regarding nominal GDP (Gross Domestic Product) and real GDP (Gross Domestic Product)?
o: Real GDP is calculated using current year prices, while nominal GDP uses base year prices.
Real GDP and nominal GDP always remain the same in every accounting year.
Real GDP removes the effect of price changes through constant base year prices.
Real GDP does not include services, while nominal GDP includes both goods and services.
exp: Real GDP is measured at the prices of a fixed base year, so it strips out the effect of price changes. Nominal GDP uses current prices and so includes inflation.

q: Which structural change in the sectoral composition of India's national income is most consistent with the post-1991 reform period?
o: Decline in industry's and services' shares, rise in agriculture's share
Equalisation of agriculture's, industry's, and services' shares
Rise in agriculture's share, decline in industry's and services' shares
Decline in agriculture's share, rise in industry and services
exp: After 1991 the share of agriculture in national income fell while the shares of industry and, above all, services rose.

q: The Human Development Index (HDI) focuses on Gross National Income (GNI) per capita, rather than Gross Domestic Product (GDP) per capita, and aims to:
o: Exclude foreign income earned within a country.
Include income earned by a country's residents abroad.
exp: GDP counts output produced inside the country, while GNI also counts income earned abroad by the country's residents. HDI uses GNI for this reason.

q: What is the formula for net investment?
exp: Net investment = gross investment minus depreciation. Depreciation is the wearing out of existing capital, so only the rest is a net addition to capital stock.

q: Which of the following statement regarding Net Domestic Product (NDP) at market prices is correct? (GDP =Gross Domestic Product)
o: Net Domestic Product at market prices exceeds GDP at market prices by the amount of depreciation.
Net Domestic Product at market prices equals GDP at market prices after deducting depreciation.
Net Domestic Product at market prices equals GDP at market prices after adding indirect taxes.
Net Domestic Product at market prices excludes both depreciation and net factor income abroad.
exp: NDP at market prices = GDP at market prices minus depreciation. 'Net' always means that depreciation has been deducted.

q: Under Article 112 of the Indian Constitution, what is the official constitutional term for the document commonly called the "Budget"?
exp: Article 112 calls the Budget the 'Annual Financial Statement'. The word 'Budget' does not appear in the Constitution.

q: Which of the following refers to the purchase of government bonds by the central bank to finance the spending needs of the government?
exp: Monetised deficit is the part of the deficit financed by the central bank buying government securities, which puts fresh money into circulation.

q: Under which article of the Indian Constitution are both Parliament and State Legislatures granted the simultaneous power to make laws with respect to Goods and Services Tax (GST)?
exp: Article 246A, added by the 101st Amendment, gives both Parliament and the State Legislatures the power to make laws on GST.

q: What was the main goal of the indirect tax reforms introduced as part of India's 1991 economic liberalisation?
o: To facilitate a common national market
exp: Indirect tax reform after 1991 aimed at a simpler, uniform tax structure so that goods could move freely and the country would work as one common market. GST later carried this forward.

q: The "Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management (FRBM) Act" was implemented in India with the aim of bringing fiscal discipline. Which of the following is the main goal or provision of the FRBM Act?
o: To ensure a fixed exchange rate for the Indian rupee.
To set limits on government borrowing and to reduce the fiscal deficit and revenue deficit.
To establish the National Planning Commission for economic development.
To regulate the flow of foreign portfolio investment in the country.
exp: The FRBM Act, 2003 sets targets and limits for government borrowing in order to cut the fiscal and revenue deficits and bring fiscal discipline.

q: An example of a direct tax is:
exp: Corporation tax is paid directly by the company on its income, so it is a direct tax. GST, excise duty and sales tax are indirect taxes passed on to the buyer.

q: Which of the following ministries prepares the budget in India?
exp: The Union Budget is prepared by the Ministry of Finance, through the Budget Division of the Department of Economic Affairs.

q: Fill in the blank: Tax reforms under 1991 economic reforms were concerned with______.
exp: Taxation is part of fiscal policy, which covers government revenue, spending and borrowing. So the 1991 tax reforms came under fiscal policy.

q: One of the key objectives of the Chelliah Committee during the 1991 economic reforms was to make India's taxation system:
exp: The Chelliah Committee (1991) recommended lower rates with a wider tax base, so that the system would be broad-based, simple and fair.

q: In open market operations, the RBI buys and sells ______ to regulate the money supply.
exp: In open market operations the RBI buys or sells government securities. Buying them puts money into the system, selling them takes money out.

q: In money supply, M2 refers to which of the following?
o: M1 + savings deposits with post office savings banks
M1 + net time deposits of banks
M1 - savings deposits with post office savings banks
M1 - net time deposits of banks
exp: M2 = M1 + savings deposits with post office savings banks. M1 is currency with the public, demand deposits and other deposits with the RBI.

q: The foreign investment limit in banks was raised to around what percentage under the 1991 reform policies?
exp: After the Narasimham Committee reforms, foreign investment in private banks was allowed up to 74%.

q: Which committee was appointed in 1993 to examine insurance sector reforms following the 1991 economic reforms?
exp: The Malhotra Committee, under former RBI Governor R.N. Malhotra, was set up in 1993 to suggest insurance reforms. Its report led to the creation of the IRDA.

q: The banking sector reforms implemented after the 1991 economic reforms were implemented under the Regulatory Oversight of which of the following?
o: Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India
National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development
exp: Banking reforms after 1991 were carried out under the regulatory control of the Reserve Bank of India, which is the regulator of banks.

q: Who was the Governor of the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) at the time of the 1991 balance of payments crisis?
exp: S. Venkitaramanan was the RBI Governor from December 1990 to December 1992, which covers the 1991 balance of payments crisis.

q: As part of the 1991 economic reforms, the Narasimham Committee recommended a four-tier structure for which sector?
exp: The Narasimham Committee (1991) suggested a four-tier banking structure, with the SBI and a few large banks at the top and local and rural banks at the base.

q: Who served as Deputy Governor of the Reserve Bank of India alongside Governor S. Venkitaramanan during the 1991 economic crisis?
exp: C. Rangarajan was Deputy Governor of the RBI during the 1991 crisis and later became Governor in 1992.

q: In money supply, M3 is related to which of the following?
o: M1 + Savings deposits with Post Office savings banks
M1 - Savings deposits with Post Office savings banks
M1 + Net time deposits of banks
M1 - Net time deposits of banks
exp: M3, or broad money, = M1 + net time deposits of banks. M2 is the one that adds post office savings deposits.

q: Which committee was appointed in 1991 to recommend reforms in India's banking and financial sector?
exp: The Narasimham Committee on the Financial System was set up in 1991 to recommend banking and financial sector reforms.

q: Which of the following constitutes foreign investment in India after the introduction of the New Economic Policy (1991)?
o: Foreign Institutional Investment and Bilateral Development Finance
Foreign Direct Investment and Official Development Assistance
Foreign Portfolio Investment and External Commercial Borrowings
Foreign Direct Investment and Foreign Institutional Investment
exp: After the New Economic Policy of 1991, foreign investment came in two main forms: Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) and Foreign Institutional Investment (FII).

q: Which of the following was an outcome of the devaluation of the rupee under India's foreign exchange reforms of 1991?
o: Increase in the inflow of foreign exchange.
Replacement of the rupee by a foreign currency.
exp: Devaluation made the rupee cheaper, so Indian exports became cheaper abroad. Exports and remittances rose, which increased the inflow of foreign exchange.

q: India approached which institution for financial assistance during the 1991 economic crisis?
exp: India turned to the International Monetary Fund for emergency assistance in 1991, and accepted its conditions for structural reform.

q: Which reform under globalisation reduces custom duties, quotas and quantitative restrictions to facilitate the free flow of goods and services?
exp: Trade liberalisation means cutting customs duties, quotas and other restrictions so that goods and services can move freely across borders.

q: What does Overseas Direct Investment (ODI) by Indian firms primarily indicate?
exp: Overseas Direct Investment is investment by Indian firms abroad, through joint ventures or subsidiaries. It shows Indian companies expanding their presence overseas.

q: Quantitative restrictions introduced in 1991 reforms on imports on manufactured consumer goods and agricultural products, were fully removed in which year?
exp: Quantitative restrictions on imports of manufactured consumer goods and farm products were finally removed in April 2001, after a WTO ruling.

q: Which of the following best explains how Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) differs from Foreign Institutional Investment (FII)?
o: Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) cannot be made in developing economies and is limited to developed countries.
Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) includes only money invested by foreign governments, and private investors are excluded.
Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) mainly involves short-term investment and trading in financial securities.
Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) establishes a long-term interest and significant managerial influence in an enterprise.
exp: FDI brings a lasting interest and a say in management of the firm. FII or portfolio investment is mostly short-term buying of shares and bonds without management control.

q: What was the primary expected outcome of abolishing import licensing requirements under India's economic reforms?
o: Complete elimination of imports and foreign goods
Increase in government control and regulation over trade
Restrictions on foreign competition and market access
exp: Ending import licensing exposed Indian producers to foreign goods. The resulting competition was expected to push firms to become more efficient.

q: Fill in the blank: Integration of the economy of the country with the world economy is known as______.
exp: Globalisation is the integration of a country's economy with the world economy through free flows of goods, services, capital and technology.

q: In which year did India face a Balance of Payments crisis, which led to the beginning of economic reforms?
exp: India faced a severe balance of payments crisis in 1991, when reserves fell to about two weeks of imports. This led to the New Economic Policy.

q: Which international institutions provided financial assistance to India to overcome the severe Balance of Payments crisis in 1991?
o: World Trade Organization and World Bank
Asian Development Bank and World Trade Organization
World Bank and International Monetary Fund
International Monetary Fund and Asian Development Bank
exp: India received emergency assistance in 1991 from both the International Monetary Fund and the World Bank.

q: During the First Five Year Plan, which of the following most accurately represents the balance of trade scenario?
o: India maintained a consistent trade surplus due to strong export performance
Trade data is not available for this period
The trade balance remained neutral, with exports and imports roughly equal
India generally faced a trade deficit due to large-scale imports for industrialisation
exp: During the First Five Year Plan India had to import capital goods and food, so it generally ran a trade deficit.

q: Following the economic reforms implemented in India in 1991, why did many domestic industries have to face stronger competition in the Indian market?
o: Due to the expansion of public sector manufacturing enterprises
Due to greater availability of cheap imported goods
Due to an increase in industrial licensing requirements
Due to an increase in minimum support prices across the country
exp: After 1991 import restrictions were eased, so cheaper foreign goods entered the market and domestic firms faced tougher competition.

q: Which of the following trade policy measures was adopted under India's liberalisation policy in 1991?
exp: Under liberalisation, India cut its customs tariffs sharply. Peak rates came down from over 200% to much lower levels.

q: Which of the following outcomes resulted from the devaluation of the rupee in 1991?
o: Increase in the inflow of foreign exchange
exp: The two-step devaluation of July 1991 made exports cheaper for foreign buyers, which raised the inflow of foreign exchange.

q: The shift from an officially administered exchange-rate system to a market-determined exchange-rate system is an example of which type of reform?
exp: Moving from a fixed, officially set exchange rate to a market-determined rate is a foreign exchange (external sector) reform. It happened in stages after 1991.

q: As a result of post-1991 agricultural reforms, Indian policy encouraged a shift away from food grain production for domestic consumption. Under these new policy strategies, which of the following became the primary market for agricultural production?
exp: After 1991 and the WTO agreement, agricultural policy encouraged commercial and export-oriented farming, so the international export market became the main target.

q: What economic crisis prompted India to introduce the New Economic Policy (NEP) in 1991?
exp: The New Economic Policy of 1991 was a direct response to the balance of payments crisis, when foreign exchange reserves were almost exhausted.

q: Adult literacy rate was replaced in Human Development Index (HDI) methodology mainly because:
o: It did not receive adequate acceptance from most countries.
It did not adequately reflect the education dimension.
It did not adequately capture differences in educational attainment.
It did not provide reliable calculations for developing countries.
exp: In 2010 the UNDP replaced the adult literacy rate with mean years of schooling and expected years of schooling, because a simple literacy figure did not show differences in how much education people actually had.

q: What is a key goal of the Human Development Index (HDI)?
o: To shift the focus from solely economic development to human development.
exp: The HDI was created to move the measure of progress beyond income and economic growth alone, to the development of people themselves.

q: During the 1991 economic crisis, India's foreign exchange reserves dropped to a level that was sufficient to finance imports for only how long?
exp: By June 1991 India's foreign exchange reserves had fallen to about one billion dollars, enough for only about two weeks of imports.

q: In the Human Development Index (HDI), the dimension of a decent standard of living is primarily measured by which of the following?
exp: A decent standard of living in the HDI is measured by Gross National Income per capita at purchasing power parity.

q: What is the central idea of the Harrod-Domar model of economic growth?
o: Fiscal policy interventions drive growth trajectories
Growth is driven by a foreign trade surplus
Growth is determined by the interaction of savings and investment
Factor endowments, particularly land and labor, constrain growth possibilities
exp: The Harrod-Domar model says that growth depends on how much a country saves and invests, and on how productive that capital is. The Second Five Year Plan of India drew on it in part.

q: Which of the following areas experienced limits on public expenditure during the economic reforms introduced in India in 1991?
exp: Under fiscal consolidation after 1991, spending on social sectors such as education, health and rural development was held back.

q: Which committee highlighted the potential of small-scale industries for rural development in 1955?
exp: The Karve Committee (Village and Small Scale Industries Committee, 1955) stressed small-scale industry for rural development and employment.

q: In the Third Five-Year Plan, which trade policy approach was primarily adopted to enhance the nation's foreign exchange earnings?
exp: The Third Five Year Plan (1961-66) stressed export promotion, so that India could earn the foreign exchange needed for its imports.

q: The economic reforms initiated in 1991 promoted which of the following policy combinations?
o: Market based pricing and industrial dereservation
Public ownership and centralised price fixation
Export controls and mandatory production quotas
exp: The 1991 reforms moved towards market-based pricing and removed the reservation of industries for the public sector, together with the end of licensing.

q: Which of the following was a specific, monitorable social target set out in India's Eleventh Five-Year Plan (2007–2012)?
exp: The Eleventh Five Year Plan (2007-12), 'Towards Faster and More Inclusive Growth', had monitorable targets including a cut in child malnutrition.

q: Which institution was envisaged to play a greater role in the planning process under the Tenth Five-Year Plan to promote balanced development?
exp: The Tenth Five Year Plan (2002-07) gave a bigger role to Panchayati Raj Institutions so that planning would be decentralised and balanced.

q: During which of the following was the Industries (Development and Regulation) Act (IDRA) 1951 enacted, which aimed to regulate India's industrial sector?
exp: The Industries (Development and Regulation) Act was passed in 1951, during the First Five Year Plan (1951-56). It set up the licensing system for industry.

q: In the context of the economic reforms after 1991, which form of privatisation relates to transferring the ownership of public enterprises completely to the private sector?
exp: Complete denationalisation means the whole ownership of a public enterprise passes to private hands. Partial disinvestment sells only a part of the equity.

q: What was the main reason for the increase in demand for food items after the 1991 reforms?
exp: Faster growth after 1991 raised incomes, and higher incomes raised the demand for food.

q: After the 1991 reforms, which sector continued to remain reserved for the public sector?
exp: The New Industrial Policy of 1991 cut the list of reserved industries to a few, which included atomic energy and railway transport.

q: Politically administered prices were replaced under which economic reform strategy?
exp: Under the reforms, prices fixed by the government were replaced by prices set by demand and supply in the market.

q: What is meant by disinvestment of public sector enterprises in India?
o: Merging two loss-making public sector companies
Selling off part of the equity of PSEs to the public
Closing down a public sector enterprise permanently
exp: Disinvestment is the sale of a part of the government's shareholding in a public sector enterprise. Full sale of ownership is privatisation.

q: Which of the following sectors was declared the "prime moving force" of the Indian economy under the Tenth Five-Year Plan (2002–2007)?
exp: The Tenth Five Year Plan (2002-07) called agriculture the 'prime moving force' of the economy, because most people depend on it.

q: Fill in the blank: Privatisation of public sector enterprises by selling off part of the equity of Public Sector Enterprise (PSE) to the public is known as______.
exp: Selling a part of the equity of a public sector enterprise to the public is called disinvestment.

q: Who was appointed as the Finance Minister of India in June 1991 to lead the economic reforms?
exp: Dr. Manmohan Singh became Finance Minister in June 1991 under Prime Minister P.V. Narasimha Rao and led the reforms.

q: Which statement accurately describes the actual growth outcomes of the First Five-Year Plan?
exp: The First Five Year Plan targeted 2.1% growth and achieved about 3.6%, so it exceeded its target.

q: The significant devaluation of the Indian rupee in 1966 (from ₹4.76 to ₹7.50 per US dollar) was largely a result of the economic challenges and policy failures associated with the ______ Five-Year Plan.
exp: The rupee was devalued in June 1966, after the Third Five Year Plan (1961-66) had been hit by wars and drought.

q: Under the post-1991 economic reforms, what kind of autonomy was given to Maharatna, Navratna and Miniratna public sector enterprises?
exp: Maharatna, Navratna and Miniratna status gives these public enterprises greater financial, managerial and operational freedom, such as the power to invest without case-by-case approval.

q: What was the primary objective of reducing import duties after the 1991 economic reforms?
o: Integrate the Indian economy with the global market
Increase monopoly power of Indian firms
exp: Lower import duties were meant to link India with the world market and expose Indian industry to global competition.

q: After the economic reforms implemented in India in 1991, what kind of change in production was encouraged by export-oriented agricultural policies?
o: From horticultural crops to pulse crops
From pulse crops to horticultural crops
From food grain crops to cash crops
From cash crops to food grain crops
exp: Export-oriented policy made cash crops more profitable than foodgrains, so farmers shifted towards cash crops.

q: Which of the following was the main thrust area of the Rolling Plan (1978-1980), which superseded the Fifth Five-Year Plan in its policy orientation?
o: Rural development and social welfare programmes
Strategic disinvestment and privatisation of state-owned enterprises
exp: The Rolling Plan (1978-80) of the Janata government stressed rural development, employment and social welfare, in place of the Fifth Plan's approach.

q:
According to the Seventh Five-Year Plan (1985-
1990) , why was the railway system considered vital to the Indian economy?
o: It was the only mode of transport available
It reduced the need for road transport
It was the backbone of the country's transport infrastructure
exp: The Seventh Five Year Plan (1985-90) treated the railways as the backbone of the country's transport system and gave them priority.

q: Under India's economic reforms since 1991, disinvestment was undertaken mainly to achieve which of the following objectives?
o: Improve financial discipline and facilitate modernisation
Expand industrial licensing and increase public ownership
Promote import substitution and restrict private investment
Increase budgetary support and reduce market competition
exp: Disinvestment was meant to raise resources, impose financial discipline on public enterprises and help them modernise.

q: What major policy action was taken during the "Three Annual Plans" of India (1966–1969), colloquially called the "Plan Holiday"?
exp: During the Plan Holiday (1966-69) India adopted the new agricultural strategy, which brought high-yielding varieties and started the Green Revolution.

q: Indian planning was inspired by which of the following?
exp: India's Five Year Plans followed the Soviet example of centralised planning, which Nehru supported, although India kept a mixed economy.

q: Which of the following best describes a limitation of open planning in India?
o: It complicates forming an optimal development strategy
It excludes citizens from policy formation
exp: Open planning means the plan is debated publicly by many groups. The many competing views make it harder to settle on a single best strategy.

q: Which of the following economic approaches best reflects the principle of 'Minimum Government, Maximum Governance'?
exp: 'Minimum Government, Maximum Governance' means less state interference in business with better administration, which fits economic liberalisation.

q: Under the economic reforms implemented since 1991, which of the following pairs of Central Public Sector Enterprises (CPSEs) has been granted Maharatna status?
o: Indian Oil Corporation Limited and Steel Authority of India Limited
Hindustan Aeronautics Limited and Mahanagar Telephone Nigam Limited
Bharat Sanchar Nigam Limited and Airports Authority of India
Tourism Corporation Limited and Mahanagar Telephone Nigam Limited
exp: Indian Oil Corporation and Steel Authority of India are both Maharatna companies. HAL became a Maharatna later; MTNL, BSNL and AAI are not Maharatnas.

q: Which of these was the main stabilisation measure adopted under the New Economic Policy (NEP) of 1991?
o: Measures to remove rigidities in the economy
exp: The 1991 policy had two parts. Stabilisation measures were short-term steps to control inflation and the balance of payments, while structural reforms were long-term changes.

q: At the time of its establishment in March 1950, what task was mainly assigned to the Planning Commission of India?
o: Conducting the national demographic census survey
Managing the flow of foreign direct investment
Formulating a plan for the balanced utilisation of national resources
exp: The Planning Commission was set up in March 1950 to make plans for the balanced and effective use of the country's resources.

q: Under the post-1991 economic reforms, what was the main objective of granting Maharatna, Navratna and Miniratna status to select Central Public Sector Enterprises?
o: To increase government ownership in all sectors
To expand industrial licensing and price regulation
To replace private investment with public investment
To enhance autonomy and improve competitiveness
exp: The ratna schemes were created to give selected public enterprises more autonomy so that they could compete better, at home and abroad.

q: What specific growth rate targets were set for real GDP and the agriculture sector under the Twelfth Five-Year Plan (2012–2017)?
exp: The Twelfth Five Year Plan (2012-17) aimed at 8% real GDP growth and 4% growth in agriculture.

q: Why is Indian planning considered a democratic political process?
o: Because only elected officials approve the budget
Because the planning process is secretive and efficient
Because it is driven by market forces, not politics
Because it passes through parliamentary presentation and public input
exp: Indian planning is democratic because plans are discussed in Parliament, in the National Development Council and in public debate before being adopted.

q: After the economic reforms introduced in India in 1991, which factors limited industrial expansion in many sectors?
o: Reduction in the use of foreign technology
exp: Even after licensing was removed, weak infrastructure such as power, roads and ports held back industrial growth.

q:
Which specific sub-title and main theme was officially adopted for India's Twelfth Five-Year Plan (2012–
2017) ?
o: Growth with social justice and regional equality
Towards faster and more inclusive growth
Faster, more inclusive and sustainable growth
exp: The theme of the Twelfth Five Year Plan was 'Faster, More Inclusive and Sustainable Growth'. The Eleventh Plan's theme was 'Towards Faster and More Inclusive Growth'.

q: With which structural change did the Second Five-Year Plan (1956–1961) begin in India?
o: Giving priority to heavy basic industries
exp: The Second Five Year Plan (1956-61) shifted the focus from agriculture to heavy and basic industries.

q: Which of these is a Maharatna Central Public Sector Enterprise?
exp: Indian Oil Corporation is a Maharatna company, a status it received in 2010.

q: Which of these was the major obstacle in achieving the targets of the Third Five Year Plan and ultimately the main reason for its failure?
o: Steep rise in international crude oil prices
Political instability in the Central Government
Large-scale implementation of Pay Commission recommendations
exp: The Third Five Year Plan failed mainly because of the wars of 1962 and 1965 and a severe drought, which drained resources and hit food output.

q: Which of the following Indian institutions, established during the Sixth Five-Year Plan, was entrusted with strengthening external trade financing?
o: Small Industries Development Bank of India (SIDBI)
Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI)
exp: The EXIM Bank was set up in 1982, during the Sixth Five Year Plan, as the apex institution for financing foreign trade.

q: In the economic reform period after 1991, which development made it possible to outsource services such as accounting, banking, music recording, film editing and clinical consultation to India?
exp: Cheaper and better telecommunication links made it possible to do services work in India for clients abroad, which is the basis of outsourcing and BPO.

q: Which of these industries is an example of a 'basic industry'?
exp: A basic industry supplies raw material or capital goods to other industries. Iron and steel is the classic example; soap and toothpaste are consumer goods.

q: What was the main objective of Token Privatisation or Disinvestment adopted under the economic reforms of 1991?
o: To expand public ownership in various industries
To raise revenue to reduce the budgetary deficit
To increase industrial licensing requirements across the country
To promote administrative control over prices
exp: Token disinvestment, selling small blocks of shares, was done mainly to raise money and reduce the budget deficit, not to transfer control.

q: What was the main objective of implementing Liberalisation in 1991?
o: To impose restrictions on more sectors of the economy
To open up various sectors of the economy
exp: Liberalisation in 1991 meant opening sectors of the economy by removing licensing and other controls, so that private firms could enter freely.

q: On which economic model was the Second Five-Year Plan based and what was its primary objective?
exp: The Second Five Year Plan was based on the Mahalanobis model and aimed at rapid industrialisation through heavy industry.

q: Which of the following is the most prominent criticism of excessive reliance on market forces after the 1991 economic reforms in India?
o: Without government support, markets may neglect deprived communities
exp: The main criticism is that markets work for profit, so without government support the poor and weaker sections can be left out.

q: What does the Business Reforms Action Plan (BRAP) framework primarily encourage States and Union Territories to do?
o: Restrict investments by imposing additional regulatory controls
Increase business compliance costs by introducing more procedures
Avoid adopting digital systems for delivering regulatory services
Promote competitive federalism by implementing business regulatory reforms
exp: The Business Reforms Action Plan ranks states on the business reforms they carry out, which sets up a healthy competition between them, called competitive federalism.

q: Which of the following is commonly cited as a major advantage of privatisation?
o: It guarantees the achievement of all social-welfare objectives and equitable outcomes
It removes competition from the market and reduces market rivalry
It eliminates every form of market failure and economic inefficiency
It may improve organisational accountability and operational efficiency
exp: Private ownership brings clearer accountability to owners and a profit motive, which can raise efficiency. It does not by itself ensure welfare or remove market failure.

q: Which of the following was a key objective of the Fifth Five-Year Plan in the industrial sector?
exp: The Fifth Five Year Plan (1974-79), with its slogan 'Garibi Hatao', continued to expand public sector enterprises in industry.

q: As an outcome of the economic reforms initiated in 1991, which sector recorded the highest average annual growth rate during 2007–12?
exp: Services grew fastest during 2007-12, well ahead of agriculture and industry.

q: Which sector was accorded the highest priority under the Second Five-Year Plan?
exp: The Second Five Year Plan gave the highest priority to heavy and basic industries, following the Mahalanobis model.

q: Which of the following industries continued to remain under industrial licensing even after the economic reforms initiated in 1991?
exp: After 1991, compulsory licensing was kept for a short list of industries, which includes alcohol, hazardous chemicals, tobacco, explosives, and defence equipment.

q: The Twenty-Point Programme (TPP), introduced during the ______ Five-Year Plan.
exp: The Twenty-Point Programme was announced by Indira Gandhi in 1975, during the Fifth Five Year Plan.

q: Which aspect of agriculture witnessed a decline after the economic reforms of 1991?
exp: Public investment in agriculture, such as irrigation and rural infrastructure, declined after 1991 as the government tried to cut spending.

q: Which of the following policy shifts characterized the Tenth Five-Year Plan (2002–2007) in terms of target setting?
exp: The Tenth Five Year Plan was the first to set eleven monitorable targets, covering poverty, literacy, infant mortality and forest cover.

q: The growth of Business Process Outsourcing (BPO) in India is mainly associated with which 1991 economic reform?
exp: BPO work for foreign clients came with globalisation, which linked India to world markets for services.

q: Which of the following sectors was intended to increase its international competitiveness through the trade and investment policy reforms introduced under the Economic Reforms of 1991?
o: Public sector production and domestic investment
exp: Trade and investment reforms in 1991 were meant to make Indian industry competitive and to bring in foreign technology.

q: The economic liberalisation reforms in India were introduced during which Five-Year Plan?
exp: The reforms began in July 1991 and were carried through the Eighth Five Year Plan (1992-97).

q: In the context of the Happiness Index, how is 'generosity' typically measured?
o: Number of charitable organizations per capita
exp: In the World Happiness Report, generosity is measured by asking whether people have donated to charity recently.

q: The Break-event Chart portrays the relationship between:
exp: A break-even chart shows how cost, volume of output and profit are related. The break-even point is where total revenue equals total cost.

q: Which department is primarily responsible for promoting and coordinating Ease of Doing Business (EoDB) reforms in India?
o: Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry
Department of Legal Affairs under the Ministry of Law and Justice
Department of Economic Affairs under the Ministry of Finance
Development Monitoring and Evaluation Office under NITI Aayog
exp: The Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT), under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry, is the nodal department for Ease of Doing Business reforms.

q: Which of the following represents the most comprehensive institutional reform underpinning the "Resolving Insolvency" component in the Ease of Doing Business Index?
exp: The Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 brought in a single time-bound process for resolving insolvency, replacing the older scattered laws.

q: In the capability approach to human development, the term "capabilities" primarily refers to:
o: What nations can export and compete
What governments can spend and provide
What people can do and become
What nations can achieve in military strength
exp: In Amartya Sen's capability approach, capabilities are the real freedoms a person has, that is, what people are actually able to do and to be.

q: India's Ease of Doing Business reform agenda primarily emphasizes which of the following?
o: The use of manual procedures for granting business approvals.
The use of centralized physical offices for issuing business licences.
The digitization and online delivery of business related regulatory services.
The use of physical documentation for completing business compliance procedures.
exp: The Ease of Doing Business agenda focuses on taking approvals, licences and filings online, so that business can be done without visiting offices.

q: Which of the following best describes the Business Reform Action Plan (BRAP)?
o: A framework for assessing business related judicial reforms implemented by States and Union Territories
A framework for assessing business related taxation reforms implemented by States and Union Territories
A framework for assessing business related constitutional reforms implemented by States and Union Territories
A framework for assessing business regulatory reforms implemented by States and Union Territories
exp: BRAP is a framework by which DPIIT assesses the business regulatory reforms carried out by states and union territories.

q: According to the World Happiness Report, corruption is assessed primarily through which of the following?
exp: The World Happiness Report measures corruption by asking people whether they think corruption is widespread in government and business, so it uses perceptions.

q: Ease of Doing Business reforms aim to make India an attractive investment destination for which of the following?
o: Only domestic investors, excluding foreign investors
Only foreign investors, excluding domestic investors
Government agencies instead of private investors
exp: Ease of Doing Business reforms are meant to attract both domestic and foreign investors.

q:
Consider the following statements regarding international comparisons of human development:
1. The territorial size and per capita income of a country are directly related to human development.
2. In general, countries with low levels of human development spend more on defence than on social sectors.
3. Countries with high levels of human development invest more in social sectors.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
exp: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong because a country's size and per capita income alone do not decide its human development; small countries with modest incomes can rank high.

q: The Human Development Index mainly encourages public debate on which of the following?
exp: The HDI was designed to start a public debate about what governments should be spending on, that is, about their development priorities.

q: What is the main objective of introducing a risk-based inspection system?
o: To focus inspections on high-risk units and reduce unnecessary inspections
To conduct risk-based inspection of all business units equally
To focus risk-based inspection on increasing the frequency of inspections
To abolish digital governance systems and implement an inspection system in their place
exp: A risk-based inspection system checks the units that carry higher risk more closely, and spares low-risk units from needless inspections.

q: In the World Happiness Report, the ranking of countries is based on what type of measure derived from respondents' answers?
o: Growth rate of Gross Domestic Product
exp: Rankings in the World Happiness Report come from average life-evaluation scores given by people in the Gallup World Poll.

q: What is the main objective of the Business Reforms Action Plan (BRAP)?
o: To improve the business regulatory environment of the defence sector in States and Union Territories
To improve the business regulatory environment in States and Union Territories
To improve the business regulatory environment of the agriculture sector in States and Union Territories
To improve the business regulatory environment of the banking sector in States and Union Territories
exp: The aim of BRAP is to improve the business regulatory environment in all states and union territories, not in any one sector.

q: Literacy is considered essential for human development because it enables people to acquire what?
exp: Literacy lets people gain knowledge, skills and awareness, which is why it is treated as basic to human development.

q: Which of the following is represented in the knowledge dimension of the Human Development Index (HDI)?
exp: The knowledge dimension of the HDI is measured by educational attainment: mean years of schooling and expected years of schooling.

q: Which statement most appropriately expresses a major paradox associated with industrialisation?
o: Industrialisation reduces urban migration and decreases the concentration of population.
Economic growth can occur, and along with it ecological damage and inequality can also arise.
Industrial development reduces consumerism and limits material consumption.
Urban centres are not self-sufficient and do not function as independent ecosystems.
exp: The paradox of industrialisation is that it raises output and incomes while also causing environmental damage and widening inequality.

q: What is the general rating scale used for happiness in the Gallup survey?
exp: The Gallup survey uses the Cantril ladder, on which people rate their life from 0, the worst possible life, to 10, the best possible life.

q: Which of the following is a key principle underlying Ease of Doing Business (EoDB) reforms?
o: Promoting transparency and efficiency in regulatory processes
Promoting secrecy and inefficiency in regulatory processes
Promoting complexity and delays in regulatory processes
Promoting multiple approvals and duplication in regulatory processes
exp: Ease of Doing Business reforms rest on transparency and efficiency in regulation: fewer procedures, clear rules and faster decisions.

q: Which government department coordinates the Business Reforms Action Plan (BRAP) exercise in India?
o: Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade
Department for National Planning and Institutional Transformation
Department for Securities Regulation and Investor Protection
Department for Banking Regulation and Monetary Policy
exp: The Business Reforms Action Plan is coordinated by the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT).

q: What is the primary objective of the Central Inspection System under the Business Reforms Action Plan?
exp: The Central Inspection System under BRAP brings different inspections together into one integrated, risk-based system.

q: Which dimension of the Human Development Index (HDI) is most directly linked to longevity?
exp: The health dimension of HDI is measured by life expectancy at birth, which is a direct measure of longevity.

q: Which of these is a Maharatna Central Public Sector Enterprise?
exp: Indian Oil Corporation is a Maharatna company, a status it received in 2010.

q: Which of the following would cause a movement along a supply curve rather than a shift in the supply curve?
o: An increase in the number of producers
An increase in the commodity's own price
exp: A change in the good's own price causes a movement along the supply curve. Technology, input prices and the number of producers shift the whole curve.

q: Fill in the blank: Integration of the economy of the country with the world economy is known as______.
exp: Globalisation is the integration of a country's economy with the world economy through free flows of goods, services, capital and technology.

q: Which aspect of agriculture witnessed a decline after the economic reforms of 1991?
exp: Public investment in agriculture, such as irrigation and rural infrastructure, declined after 1991 as the government tried to cut spending.

q: What is the main objective of the Business Reforms Action Plan (BRAP)?
o: To improve the business regulatory environment of the defence sector in States and Union Territories
To improve the business regulatory environment in States and Union Territories
To improve the business regulatory environment of the agriculture sector in States and Union Territories
To improve the business regulatory environment of the banking sector in States and Union Territories
exp: The aim of BRAP is to improve the business regulatory environment in all states and union territories, not in any one sector.

q: The Human Development Index mainly encourages public debate on which of the following?
exp: The HDI was designed to start a public debate about what governments should be spending on, that is, about their development priorities.

q: After the economic reforms introduced in India in 1991, which factors limited industrial expansion in many sectors?
o: Reduction in the use of foreign technology
exp: Even after licensing was removed, weak infrastructure such as power, roads and ports held back industrial growth.

q: The economic liberalisation reforms in India were introduced during which Five-Year Plan?
exp: The reforms began in July 1991 and were carried through the Eighth Five Year Plan (1992-97).

q: Which of the following constitutes foreign investment in India after the introduction of the New Economic Policy (1991)?
o: Foreign Institutional Investment and Bilateral Development Finance
Foreign Direct Investment and Official Development Assistance
Foreign Portfolio Investment and External Commercial Borrowings
Foreign Direct Investment and Foreign Institutional Investment
exp: After the New Economic Policy of 1991, foreign investment came in two main forms: Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) and Foreign Institutional Investment (FII).

q: Politically administered prices were replaced under which economic reform strategy?
exp: Under the reforms, prices fixed by the government were replaced by prices set by demand and supply in the market.

q: The Human Development Index can be used to compare which of the following?
o: Human development outcomes across different countries
Human development outcomes only in Asian countries
Human development outcomes only in developed countries
exp: The HDI is a composite index of health, education and income, published by the UNDP since 1990. It is used to compare human development across all countries, developed and developing alike.

q:
According to the Seventh Five-Year Plan (1985-
1990) , why was the railway system considered vital to the Indian economy?
o: It was the only mode of transport available
It reduced the need for road transport
It was the backbone of the country's transport infrastructure
exp: The Seventh Five Year Plan (1985-90) treated the railways as the backbone of the country's transport system and gave them priority.

q: Which department is primarily responsible for promoting and coordinating Ease of Doing Business (EoDB) reforms in India?
o: Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry
Department of Legal Affairs under the Ministry of Law and Justice
Department of Economic Affairs under the Ministry of Finance
Development Monitoring and Evaluation Office under NITI Aayog
exp: The Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT), under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry, is the nodal department for Ease of Doing Business reforms.

q: Which of the following Indian institutions, established during the Sixth Five-Year Plan, was entrusted with strengthening external trade financing?
o: Small Industries Development Bank of India (SIDBI)
Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI)
exp: The EXIM Bank was set up in 1982, during the Sixth Five Year Plan, as the apex institution for financing foreign trade.

q: Which country has the highest GDP in South Asia?
exp: India has the largest economy in South Asia by a wide margin, far ahead of Pakistan, Bangladesh and Sri Lanka.

q: In open market operations, the RBI buys and sells ______ to regulate the money supply.
exp: In open market operations the RBI buys or sells government securities. Buying them puts money into the system, selling them takes money out.

q: What was the main objective of Token Privatisation or Disinvestment adopted under the economic reforms of 1991?
o: To expand public ownership in various industries
To raise revenue to reduce the budgetary deficit
To increase industrial licensing requirements across the country
To promote administrative control over prices
exp: Token disinvestment, selling small blocks of shares, was done mainly to raise money and reduce the budget deficit, not to transfer control.

q: What was the primary expected outcome of abolishing import licensing requirements under India's economic reforms?
o: Complete elimination of imports and foreign goods
Increase in government control and regulation over trade
Restrictions on foreign competition and market access
exp: Ending import licensing exposed Indian producers to foreign goods. The resulting competition was expected to push firms to become more efficient.

q: The significant devaluation of the Indian rupee in 1966 (from ₹4.76 to ₹7.50 per US dollar) was largely a result of the economic challenges and policy failures associated with the ______ Five-Year Plan.
exp: The rupee was devalued in June 1966, after the Third Five Year Plan (1961-66) had been hit by wars and drought.

q: According to the World Happiness Report, corruption is assessed primarily through which of the following?
exp: The World Happiness Report measures corruption by asking people whether they think corruption is widespread in government and business, so it uses perceptions.

q: Which of the following industries continued to remain under industrial licensing even after the economic reforms initiated in 1991?
exp: After 1991, compulsory licensing was kept for a short list of industries, which includes alcohol, hazardous chemicals, tobacco, explosives, and defence equipment.

q: Ease of Doing Business reforms aim to make India an attractive investment destination for which of the following?
o: Only domestic investors, excluding foreign investors
Only foreign investors, excluding domestic investors
Government agencies instead of private investors
exp: Ease of Doing Business reforms are meant to attract both domestic and foreign investors.

q: Which of the following trade policy measures was adopted under India's liberalisation policy in 1991?
exp: Under liberalisation, India cut its customs tariffs sharply. Peak rates came down from over 200% to much lower levels.

q: Which of the following indicators is used to measure the standard of living dimension of the Human Development Index (HDI)?
o: Gross National Income (GNI) per capita based on Purchasing Power Parity (PPP)
Gross Domestic Product (GDP) per capita based on Purchasing Power Parity (PPP)
Net National Product (NNP) per capita based on Purchasing Power Parity (PPP)
Disposable income per capita based on Purchasing Power Parity (PPP)
exp: The standard of living dimension of the HDI is measured by Gross National Income per capita at Purchasing Power Parity.

q: Which of the following sectors was intended to increase its international competitiveness through the trade and investment policy reforms introduced under the Economic Reforms of 1991?
o: Public sector production and domestic investment
exp: Trade and investment reforms in 1991 were meant to make Indian industry competitive and to bring in foreign technology.

q: Under Article 112 of the Indian Constitution, what is the official constitutional term for the document commonly called the "Budget"?
exp: Article 112 calls the Budget the 'Annual Financial Statement'. The word 'Budget' does not appear in the Constitution.

q: Which of the following best describes a limitation of open planning in India?
o: It complicates forming an optimal development strategy
It excludes citizens from policy formation
exp: Open planning means the plan is debated publicly by many groups. The many competing views make it harder to settle on a single best strategy.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes movement along a demand curve from a shift in the demand curve?
o: Both are caused only by price changes.
Movement occurs due to income changes and shifts due to price changes.
Movement occurs due to own price changes, shift due to other determinants.
A shift means only a change in quantity demanded.
exp: A change in the good's own price moves the consumer along the demand curve. A change in income, tastes or the price of related goods shifts the entire curve.

q: As part of the 1991 economic reforms, the Narasimham Committee recommended a four-tier structure for which sector?
exp: The Narasimham Committee (1991) suggested a four-tier banking structure, with the SBI and a few large banks at the top and local and rural banks at the base.

q: Which of these industries is an example of a 'basic industry'?
exp: A basic industry supplies raw material or capital goods to other industries. Iron and steel is the classic example; soap and toothpaste are consumer goods.

q: Which of the following was an outcome of the devaluation of the rupee under India's foreign exchange reforms of 1991?
o: Increase in the inflow of foreign exchange.
Replacement of the rupee by a foreign currency.
exp: Devaluation made the rupee cheaper, so Indian exports became cheaper abroad. Exports and remittances rose, which increased the inflow of foreign exchange.

q: Which of the following is the best example of dynamic economic analysis?
o: Examining consumer demand at a particular point in time
Comparing the inflation rates of two countries during the same year
Analysing the changes in consumer demand over a period of several years
Examining an economy assuming all variables remain unchanged
exp: Dynamic analysis studies change over time. Looking at how consumer demand changes over several years is dynamic; studying a single point in time is static analysis.

q: Which of the following policy shifts characterized the Tenth Five-Year Plan (2002–2007) in terms of target setting?
exp: The Tenth Five Year Plan was the first to set eleven monitorable targets, covering poverty, literacy, infant mortality and forest cover.

q: As a result of post-1991 agricultural reforms, Indian policy encouraged a shift away from food grain production for domestic consumption. Under these new policy strategies, which of the following became the primary market for agricultural production?
exp: After 1991 and the WTO agreement, agricultural policy encouraged commercial and export-oriented farming, so the international export market became the main target.

q: A university raises its tuition fee by 20%. As a result, student enrolment decreases by 30%, while all other factors remain unchanged. Which of the following statements correctly describes the price elasticity of demand and the resulting change in the university's total tuition revenue?
o: Demand is inelastic, and total tuition revenue increases.
Demand is elastic, and total tuition revenue decreases.
Demand is unit elastic, and total tuition revenue remains unchanged.
Demand is perfectly elastic, and total tuition revenue becomes zero.
exp: Elasticity = 30% fall in quantity / 20% rise in price = 1.5, which is greater than 1, so demand is elastic. When demand is elastic, a price rise lowers total revenue.

q: Which of the following best describes the Business Reform Action Plan (BRAP)?
o: A framework for assessing business related judicial reforms implemented by States and Union Territories
A framework for assessing business related taxation reforms implemented by States and Union Territories
A framework for assessing business related constitutional reforms implemented by States and Union Territories
A framework for assessing business regulatory reforms implemented by States and Union Territories
exp: BRAP is a framework by which DPIIT assesses the business regulatory reforms carried out by states and union territories.

q: Which of the following best explains how Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) differs from Foreign Institutional Investment (FII)?
o: Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) cannot be made in developing economies and is limited to developed countries.
Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) includes only money invested by foreign governments, and private investors are excluded.
Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) mainly involves short-term investment and trading in financial securities.
Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) establishes a long-term interest and significant managerial influence in an enterprise.
exp: FDI brings a lasting interest and a say in management of the firm. FII or portfolio investment is mostly short-term buying of shares and bonds without management control.

q: What is meant by disinvestment of public sector enterprises in India?
o: Merging two loss-making public sector companies
Selling off part of the equity of PSEs to the public
Closing down a public sector enterprise permanently
exp: Disinvestment is the sale of a part of the government's shareholding in a public sector enterprise. Full sale of ownership is privatisation.

q: In the capability approach to human development, the term "capabilities" primarily refers to:
o: What nations can export and compete
What governments can spend and provide
What people can do and become
What nations can achieve in military strength
exp: In Amartya Sen's capability approach, capabilities are the real freedoms a person has, that is, what people are actually able to do and to be.

q: Which of the following statement regarding Net Domestic Product (NDP) at market prices is correct? (GDP =Gross Domestic Product)
o: Net Domestic Product at market prices exceeds GDP at market prices by the amount of depreciation.
Net Domestic Product at market prices equals GDP at market prices after deducting depreciation.
Net Domestic Product at market prices equals GDP at market prices after adding indirect taxes.
Net Domestic Product at market prices excludes both depreciation and net factor income abroad.
exp: NDP at market prices = GDP at market prices minus depreciation. 'Net' always means that depreciation has been deducted.

q: Which of the following is the most prominent criticism of excessive reliance on market forces after the 1991 economic reforms in India?
o: Without government support, markets may neglect deprived communities
exp: The main criticism is that markets work for profit, so without government support the poor and weaker sections can be left out.

q: In money supply, M2 refers to which of the following?
o: M1 + savings deposits with post office savings banks
M1 + net time deposits of banks
M1 - savings deposits with post office savings banks
M1 - net time deposits of banks
exp: M2 = M1 + savings deposits with post office savings banks. M1 is currency with the public, demand deposits and other deposits with the RBI.

q: What does a consumption combination lying below the consumer's budget line indicate?
o: Some portion of the consumer's utility remains unattained.
Some portion of the required expenditure exceeds the consumer's income.
Some portion of the consumer's income remains unspent.
Some portion of the maximum possible utility remains unattained.
exp: A point below the budget line costs less than the consumer's income, so part of the income is left unspent. Points on the line use up the whole income.

q: Under which article of the Indian Constitution are both Parliament and State Legislatures granted the simultaneous power to make laws with respect to Goods and Services Tax (GST)?
exp: Article 246A, added by the 101st Amendment, gives both Parliament and the State Legislatures the power to make laws on GST.

q: What is a key goal of the Human Development Index (HDI)?
o: To shift the focus from solely economic development to human development.
exp: The HDI was created to move the measure of progress beyond income and economic growth alone, to the development of people themselves.

q: Why were high rates of domestic savings and investment important for India's economic growth after the 1991 reforms?
o: They increase the fiscal deficit and weaken financial stability
They discourage entrepreneurship and limit business expansion.
They boost capital formation and long-term growth potential.
They reduce productive capacity and limit economic growth.
exp: Savings finance investment, and investment builds capital. Higher capital formation raises the economy's capacity to produce, so it supports long-term growth.

q: Which of the following was a key objective of the Fifth Five-Year Plan in the industrial sector?
exp: The Fifth Five Year Plan (1974-79), with its slogan 'Garibi Hatao', continued to expand public sector enterprises in industry.

q: The human development approach underlying the Human Development Index is mainly concerned with which of the following?
exp: The human development approach of Mahbub ul Haq and Amartya Sen treats development as the expansion of people's capabilities and choices, not just a rise in income.

q: What was the main reason for the increase in demand for food items after the 1991 reforms?
exp: Faster growth after 1991 raised incomes, and higher incomes raised the demand for food.

q: Which of the following outcomes resulted from the devaluation of the rupee in 1991?
o: Increase in the inflow of foreign exchange
exp: The two-step devaluation of July 1991 made exports cheaper for foreign buyers, which raised the inflow of foreign exchange.

q: The foreign investment limit in banks was raised to around what percentage under the 1991 reform policies?
exp: After the Narasimham Committee reforms, foreign investment in private banks was allowed up to 74%.

q: Why is Indian planning considered a democratic political process?
o: Because only elected officials approve the budget
Because the planning process is secretive and efficient
Because it is driven by market forces, not politics
Because it passes through parliamentary presentation and public input
exp: Indian planning is democratic because plans are discussed in Parliament, in the National Development Council and in public debate before being adopted.

q: Which of the following is represented in the knowledge dimension of the Human Development Index (HDI)?
exp: The knowledge dimension of the HDI is measured by educational attainment: mean years of schooling and expected years of schooling.

q: In the context of the economic reforms after 1991, which form of privatisation relates to transferring the ownership of public enterprises completely to the private sector?
exp: Complete denationalisation means the whole ownership of a public enterprise passes to private hands. Partial disinvestment sells only a part of the equity.

q: Which of the following was the main thrust area of the Rolling Plan (1978-1980), which superseded the Fifth Five-Year Plan in its policy orientation?
o: Rural development and social welfare programmes
Strategic disinvestment and privatisation of state-owned enterprises
exp: The Rolling Plan (1978-80) of the Janata government stressed rural development, employment and social welfare, in place of the Fifth Plan's approach.

q: Which of the following ministries prepares the budget in India?
exp: The Union Budget is prepared by the Ministry of Finance, through the Budget Division of the Department of Economic Affairs.

q: What does the Business Reforms Action Plan (BRAP) framework primarily encourage States and Union Territories to do?
o: Restrict investments by imposing additional regulatory controls
Increase business compliance costs by introducing more procedures
Avoid adopting digital systems for delivering regulatory services
Promote competitive federalism by implementing business regulatory reforms
exp: The Business Reforms Action Plan ranks states on the business reforms they carry out, which sets up a healthy competition between them, called competitive federalism.

q: What was the primary objective of reducing import duties after the 1991 economic reforms?
o: Integrate the Indian economy with the global market
Increase monopoly power of Indian firms
exp: Lower import duties were meant to link India with the world market and expose Indian industry to global competition.

q: On which economic model was the Second Five-Year Plan based and what was its primary objective?
exp: The Second Five Year Plan was based on the Mahalanobis model and aimed at rapid industrialisation through heavy industry.

q: Which sector was accorded the highest priority under the Second Five-Year Plan?
exp: The Second Five Year Plan gave the highest priority to heavy and basic industries, following the Mahalanobis model.

q: Under the post-1991 economic reforms, what kind of autonomy was given to Maharatna, Navratna and Miniratna public sector enterprises?
exp: Maharatna, Navratna and Miniratna status gives these public enterprises greater financial, managerial and operational freedom, such as the power to invest without case-by-case approval.

q: Which of the following sectors was declared the "prime moving force" of the Indian economy under the Tenth Five-Year Plan (2002–2007)?
exp: The Tenth Five Year Plan (2002-07) called agriculture the 'prime moving force' of the economy, because most people depend on it.

q: Indian planning was inspired by which of the following?
exp: India's Five Year Plans followed the Soviet example of centralised planning, which Nehru supported, although India kept a mixed economy.

q: After the 1991 reforms, which sector continued to remain reserved for the public sector?
exp: The New Industrial Policy of 1991 cut the list of reserved industries to a few, which included atomic energy and railway transport.

q: A leftward shift of the demand curve of a commodity indicates:
exp: A leftward shift means less is bought at every price, which is a decrease in demand. A change caused by price alone would be a movement along the curve.

q: Which of the following factors does not determine demand?
exp: The price of factors of production, such as wages and rent, affects cost and therefore supply. Demand depends on the good's price, consumer income and the price of related goods.

q: Which of the following effects does a rise in the price of goods have on consumer surplus?
exp: Consumer surplus is the gap between what a buyer is willing to pay and what is actually paid. A higher price narrows that gap, so consumer surplus falls.

q: After the economic reforms implemented in India in 1991, what kind of change in production was encouraged by export-oriented agricultural policies?
o: From horticultural crops to pulse crops
From pulse crops to horticultural crops
From food grain crops to cash crops
From cash crops to food grain crops
exp: Export-oriented policy made cash crops more profitable than foodgrains, so farmers shifted towards cash crops.

q: Literacy is considered essential for human development because it enables people to acquire what?
exp: Literacy lets people gain knowledge, skills and awareness, which is why it is treated as basic to human development.

q: Which structural change in the sectoral composition of India's national income is most consistent with the post-1991 reform period?
o: Decline in industry's and services' shares, rise in agriculture's share
Equalisation of agriculture's, industry's, and services' shares
Rise in agriculture's share, decline in industry's and services' shares
Decline in agriculture's share, rise in industry and services
exp: After 1991 the share of agriculture in national income fell while the shares of industry and, above all, services rose.

q: The shift from an officially administered exchange-rate system to a market-determined exchange-rate system is an example of which type of reform?
exp: Moving from a fixed, officially set exchange rate to a market-determined rate is a foreign exchange (external sector) reform. It happened in stages after 1991.

q:
Consider the following statements regarding international comparisons of human development:
1. The territorial size and per capita income of a country are directly related to human development.
2. In general, countries with low levels of human development spend more on defence than on social sectors.
3. Countries with high levels of human development invest more in social sectors.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
exp: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong because a country's size and per capita income alone do not decide its human development; small countries with modest incomes can rank high.

q: What is the general rating scale used for happiness in the Gallup survey?
exp: The Gallup survey uses the Cantril ladder, on which people rate their life from 0, the worst possible life, to 10, the best possible life.

q: Fill in the blank: Tax reforms under 1991 economic reforms were concerned with______.
exp: Taxation is part of fiscal policy, which covers government revenue, spending and borrowing. So the 1991 tax reforms came under fiscal policy.

q: The Twenty-Point Programme (TPP), introduced during the ______ Five-Year Plan.
exp: The Twenty-Point Programme was announced by Indira Gandhi in 1975, during the Fifth Five Year Plan.

q: Who was the Governor of the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) at the time of the 1991 balance of payments crisis?
exp: S. Venkitaramanan was the RBI Governor from December 1990 to December 1992, which covers the 1991 balance of payments crisis.

q: Why does the fundamental economic problem of scarcity arise?
o: Because governments intentionally limit all production
Because firms always attempt to maximise profits
Because the prices of all goods remain high
exp: Scarcity arises because human wants are unlimited while the resources to satisfy them are limited. This forces choice, which is the basic economic problem.

q: What specific growth rate targets were set for real GDP and the agriculture sector under the Twelfth Five-Year Plan (2012–2017)?
