exp: The Twelfth Five Year Plan (2012-17) aimed at 8% real GDP growth and 4% growth in agriculture.

q: In the Human Development Index (HDI), the dimension of a decent standard of living is primarily measured by which of the following?
exp: A decent standard of living in the HDI is measured by Gross National Income per capita at purchasing power parity.

q: Which of the following economic approaches best reflects the principle of 'Minimum Government, Maximum Governance'?
exp: 'Minimum Government, Maximum Governance' means less state interference in business with better administration, which fits economic liberalisation.

q: What is the primary objective of the Central Inspection System under the Business Reforms Action Plan?
exp: The Central Inspection System under BRAP brings different inspections together into one integrated, risk-based system.

q: Which international institutions provided financial assistance to India to overcome the severe Balance of Payments crisis in 1991?
o: World Trade Organization and World Bank
Asian Development Bank and World Trade Organization
World Bank and International Monetary Fund
International Monetary Fund and Asian Development Bank
exp: India received emergency assistance in 1991 from both the International Monetary Fund and the World Bank.

q: What was the main objective of implementing Liberalisation in 1991?
o: To impose restrictions on more sectors of the economy
To open up various sectors of the economy
exp: Liberalisation in 1991 meant opening sectors of the economy by removing licensing and other controls, so that private firms could enter freely.

q: Who served as Deputy Governor of the Reserve Bank of India alongside Governor S. Venkitaramanan during the 1991 economic crisis?
exp: C. Rangarajan was Deputy Governor of the RBI during the 1991 crisis and later became Governor in 1992.

q: What was the main goal of the indirect tax reforms introduced as part of India's 1991 economic liberalisation?
o: To facilitate a common national market
exp: Indirect tax reform after 1991 aimed at a simpler, uniform tax structure so that goods could move freely and the country would work as one common market. GST later carried this forward.

q: India approached which institution for financial assistance during the 1991 economic crisis?
exp: India turned to the International Monetary Fund for emergency assistance in 1991, and accepted its conditions for structural reform.

q: India's Ease of Doing Business reform agenda primarily emphasizes which of the following?
o: The use of manual procedures for granting business approvals.
The use of centralized physical offices for issuing business licences.
The digitization and online delivery of business related regulatory services.
The use of physical documentation for completing business compliance procedures.
exp: The Ease of Doing Business agenda focuses on taking approvals, licences and filings online, so that business can be done without visiting offices.

q: Which of the following statements is correct regarding nominal GDP (Gross Domestic Product) and real GDP (Gross Domestic Product)?
o: Real GDP is calculated using current year prices, while nominal GDP uses base year prices.
Real GDP and nominal GDP always remain the same in every accounting year.
Real GDP removes the effect of price changes through constant base year prices.
Real GDP does not include services, while nominal GDP includes both goods and services.
exp: Real GDP is measured at the prices of a fixed base year, so it strips out the effect of price changes. Nominal GDP uses current prices and so includes inflation.

q: Adult literacy rate was replaced in Human Development Index (HDI) methodology mainly because:
o: It did not receive adequate acceptance from most countries.
It did not adequately reflect the education dimension.
It did not adequately capture differences in educational attainment.
It did not provide reliable calculations for developing countries.
exp: In 2010 the UNDP replaced the adult literacy rate with mean years of schooling and expected years of schooling, because a simple literacy figure did not show differences in how much education people actually had.

q: Quantitative restrictions introduced in 1991 reforms on imports on manufactured consumer goods and agricultural products, were fully removed in which year?
exp: Quantitative restrictions on imports of manufactured consumer goods and farm products were finally removed in April 2001, after a WTO ruling.

q: Which of the following is a key principle underlying Ease of Doing Business (EoDB) reforms?
o: Promoting transparency and efficiency in regulatory processes
Promoting secrecy and inefficiency in regulatory processes
Promoting complexity and delays in regulatory processes
Promoting multiple approvals and duplication in regulatory processes
exp: Ease of Doing Business reforms rest on transparency and efficiency in regulation: fewer procedures, clear rules and faster decisions.

q: In money supply, M3 is related to which of the following?
o: M1 + Savings deposits with Post Office savings banks
M1 - Savings deposits with Post Office savings banks
M1 + Net time deposits of banks
M1 - Net time deposits of banks
exp: M3, or broad money, = M1 + net time deposits of banks. M2 is the one that adds post office savings deposits.

q: The Human Development Index (HDI) uses a logarithmic transformation for Gross National Income (GNI) per capita, and its aim is:
o: To reduce the impact of extremely high incomes.
To give more weight to high incomes.
To exclude income obtained from natural resource extraction.
exp: Income is used in log form because every extra rupee adds less to well-being once income is already high. The log therefore damps down the effect of very high incomes.

q: With which structural change did the Second Five-Year Plan (1956–1961) begin in India?
o: Giving priority to heavy basic industries
exp: The Second Five Year Plan (1956-61) shifted the focus from agriculture to heavy and basic industries.

q: What is the central idea of the Harrod-Domar model of economic growth?
o: Fiscal policy interventions drive growth trajectories
Growth is driven by a foreign trade surplus
Growth is determined by the interaction of savings and investment
Factor endowments, particularly land and labor, constrain growth possibilities
exp: The Harrod-Domar model says that growth depends on how much a country saves and invests, and on how productive that capital is. The Second Five Year Plan of India drew on it in part.

q: Under the post-1991 economic reforms, what was the main objective of granting Maharatna, Navratna and Miniratna status to select Central Public Sector Enterprises?
o: To increase government ownership in all sectors
To expand industrial licensing and price regulation
To replace private investment with public investment
To enhance autonomy and improve competitiveness
exp: The ratna schemes were created to give selected public enterprises more autonomy so that they could compete better, at home and abroad.

q: In the context of the Happiness Index, how is 'generosity' typically measured?
o: Number of charitable organizations per capita
exp: In the World Happiness Report, generosity is measured by asking whether people have donated to charity recently.

q: As an outcome of the economic reforms initiated in 1991, which sector recorded the highest average annual growth rate during 2007–12?
exp: Services grew fastest during 2007-12, well ahead of agriculture and industry.

q: If the selling price of milk rises sharply, what is the most likely effect on the supply of butter, assuming milk can either be sold directly or used to produce butter?
exp: If milk sells at a high price, producers prefer to sell milk directly rather than convert it into butter. So less milk goes into butter and the supply of butter falls.

q: Which government department coordinates the Business Reforms Action Plan (BRAP) exercise in India?
o: Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade
Department for National Planning and Institutional Transformation
Department for Securities Regulation and Investor Protection
Department for Banking Regulation and Monetary Policy
exp: The Business Reforms Action Plan is coordinated by the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT).

q: In the Third Five-Year Plan, which trade policy approach was primarily adopted to enhance the nation's foreign exchange earnings?
exp: The Third Five Year Plan (1961-66) stressed export promotion, so that India could earn the foreign exchange needed for its imports.

q: An example of a direct tax is:
exp: Corporation tax is paid directly by the company on its income, so it is a direct tax. GST, excise duty and sales tax are indirect taxes passed on to the buyer.

q: The Human Development Index (HDI) focuses on Gross National Income (GNI) per capita, rather than Gross Domestic Product (GDP) per capita, and aims to:
o: Exclude foreign income earned within a country.
Include income earned by a country's residents abroad.
exp: GDP counts output produced inside the country, while GNI also counts income earned abroad by the country's residents. HDI uses GNI for this reason.

q: Which of these was the main stabilisation measure adopted under the New Economic Policy (NEP) of 1991?
o: Measures to remove rigidities in the economy
exp: The 1991 policy had two parts. Stabilisation measures were short-term steps to control inflation and the balance of payments, while structural reforms were long-term changes.

q: Who was appointed as the Finance Minister of India in June 1991 to lead the economic reforms?
exp: Dr. Manmohan Singh became Finance Minister in June 1991 under Prime Minister P.V. Narasimha Rao and led the reforms.

q: During which of the following was the Industries (Development and Regulation) Act (IDRA) 1951 enacted, which aimed to regulate India's industrial sector?
exp: The Industries (Development and Regulation) Act was passed in 1951, during the First Five Year Plan (1951-56). It set up the licensing system for industry.

q:
Which specific sub-title and main theme was officially adopted for India's Twelfth Five-Year Plan (2012–
2017) ?
o: Growth with social justice and regional equality
Towards faster and more inclusive growth
Faster, more inclusive and sustainable growth
exp: The theme of the Twelfth Five Year Plan was 'Faster, More Inclusive and Sustainable Growth'. The Eleventh Plan's theme was 'Towards Faster and More Inclusive Growth'.

q: If a consumer's income increases, resulting in greater consumption of good X and lower consumption of good Y, which of the following is correct?
o: Both X and Y are inferior goods.
X is an inferior good, while Y is a normal good.
X is a normal good, while Y is an inferior good.
Both X and Y are normal goods.
exp: When income rises, demand for a normal good goes up and demand for an inferior good goes down. Here X rises and Y falls, so X is normal and Y is inferior.

q: Under India's economic reforms since 1991, disinvestment was undertaken mainly to achieve which of the following objectives?
o: Improve financial discipline and facilitate modernisation
Expand industrial licensing and increase public ownership
Promote import substitution and restrict private investment
Increase budgetary support and reduce market competition
exp: Disinvestment was meant to raise resources, impose financial discipline on public enterprises and help them modernise.

q: Which of the following refers to the purchase of government bonds by the central bank to finance the spending needs of the government?
exp: Monetised deficit is the part of the deficit financed by the central bank buying government securities, which puts fresh money into circulation.

q: The concept of socialist economy was propounded by:
exp: Karl Marx set out the idea of a socialist economy in 'The Communist Manifesto' (1848) and 'Das Kapital'. Adam Smith, Marshall and Ricardo belong to the classical school.

q: In which year did India face a Balance of Payments crisis, which led to the beginning of economic reforms?
exp: India faced a severe balance of payments crisis in 1991, when reserves fell to about two weeks of imports. This led to the New Economic Policy.

q: Which statement most appropriately expresses a major paradox associated with industrialisation?
o: Industrialisation reduces urban migration and decreases the concentration of population.
Economic growth can occur, and along with it ecological damage and inequality can also arise.
Industrial development reduces consumerism and limits material consumption.
Urban centres are not self-sufficient and do not function as independent ecosystems.
exp: The paradox of industrialisation is that it raises output and incomes while also causing environmental damage and widening inequality.

q: The banking sector reforms implemented after the 1991 economic reforms were implemented under the Regulatory Oversight of which of the following?
o: Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India
National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development
exp: Banking reforms after 1991 were carried out under the regulatory control of the Reserve Bank of India, which is the regulator of banks.

q: Which institution was envisaged to play a greater role in the planning process under the Tenth Five-Year Plan to promote balanced development?
exp: The Tenth Five Year Plan (2002-07) gave a bigger role to Panchayati Raj Institutions so that planning would be decentralised and balanced.

q: During the First Five Year Plan, which of the following most accurately represents the balance of trade scenario?
o: India maintained a consistent trade surplus due to strong export performance
Trade data is not available for this period
The trade balance remained neutral, with exports and imports roughly equal
India generally faced a trade deficit due to large-scale imports for industrialisation
exp: During the First Five Year Plan India had to import capital goods and food, so it generally ran a trade deficit.

q: Why is the demand for salt generally less price-elastic than the demand for branded chocolate?
o: Salt has more close substitutes than branded chocolate.
Salt takes up a large share of consumers' income.
Salt is a necessity and has relatively few close substitutes.
exp: Salt is a necessity with few substitutes and takes a tiny share of income, so buyers keep buying it when the price rises. That makes its demand inelastic.

q: Which of the following was a specific, monitorable social target set out in India's Eleventh Five-Year Plan (2007–2012)?
exp: The Eleventh Five Year Plan (2007-12), 'Towards Faster and More Inclusive Growth', had monitorable targets including a cut in child malnutrition.

q: During the 1991 economic crisis, India's foreign exchange reserves dropped to a level that was sufficient to finance imports for only how long?
exp: By June 1991 India's foreign exchange reserves had fallen to about one billion dollars, enough for only about two weeks of imports.

q: Which of these was the major obstacle in achieving the targets of the Third Five Year Plan and ultimately the main reason for its failure?
o: Steep rise in international crude oil prices
Political instability in the Central Government
Large-scale implementation of Pay Commission recommendations
exp: The Third Five Year Plan failed mainly because of the wars of 1962 and 1965 and a severe drought, which drained resources and hit food output.

q: Which committee highlighted the potential of small-scale industries for rural development in 1955?
exp: The Karve Committee (Village and Small Scale Industries Committee, 1955) stressed small-scale industry for rural development and employment.

q: Which committee was appointed in 1993 to examine insurance sector reforms following the 1991 economic reforms?
exp: The Malhotra Committee, under former RBI Governor R.N. Malhotra, was set up in 1993 to suggest insurance reforms. Its report led to the creation of the IRDA.

q: What major policy action was taken during the "Three Annual Plans" of India (1966–1969), colloquially called the "Plan Holiday"?
exp: During the Plan Holiday (1966-69) India adopted the new agricultural strategy, which brought high-yielding varieties and started the Green Revolution.

q: The "Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management (FRBM) Act" was implemented in India with the aim of bringing fiscal discipline. Which of the following is the main goal or provision of the FRBM Act?
o: To ensure a fixed exchange rate for the Indian rupee.
To set limits on government borrowing and to reduce the fiscal deficit and revenue deficit.
To establish the National Planning Commission for economic development.
To regulate the flow of foreign portfolio investment in the country.
exp: The FRBM Act, 2003 sets targets and limits for government borrowing in order to cut the fiscal and revenue deficits and bring fiscal discipline.

q: In the World Happiness Report, the ranking of countries is based on what type of measure derived from respondents' answers?
o: Growth rate of Gross Domestic Product
exp: Rankings in the World Happiness Report come from average life-evaluation scores given by people in the Gallup World Poll.

q: The growth of Business Process Outsourcing (BPO) in India is mainly associated with which 1991 economic reform?
exp: BPO work for foreign clients came with globalisation, which linked India to world markets for services.

q: Who among the following explained the substitution and income effect?
exp: J.R. Hicks and R.G.D. Allen separated the price effect into the substitution effect and the income effect in their 1934 work on ordinal utility.

q: Following the economic reforms implemented in India in 1991, why did many domestic industries have to face stronger competition in the Indian market?
o: Due to the expansion of public sector manufacturing enterprises
Due to greater availability of cheap imported goods
Due to an increase in industrial licensing requirements
Due to an increase in minimum support prices across the country
exp: After 1991 import restrictions were eased, so cheaper foreign goods entered the market and domestic firms faced tougher competition.

q: Under the economic reforms implemented since 1991, which of the following pairs of Central Public Sector Enterprises (CPSEs) has been granted Maharatna status?
o: Indian Oil Corporation Limited and Steel Authority of India Limited
Hindustan Aeronautics Limited and Mahanagar Telephone Nigam Limited
Bharat Sanchar Nigam Limited and Airports Authority of India
Tourism Corporation Limited and Mahanagar Telephone Nigam Limited
exp: Indian Oil Corporation and Steel Authority of India are both Maharatna companies. HAL became a Maharatna later; MTNL, BSNL and AAI are not Maharatnas.

q: What economic crisis prompted India to introduce the New Economic Policy (NEP) in 1991?
exp: The New Economic Policy of 1991 was a direct response to the balance of payments crisis, when foreign exchange reserves were almost exhausted.

q: At the time of its establishment in March 1950, what task was mainly assigned to the Planning Commission of India?
o: Conducting the national demographic census survey
Managing the flow of foreign direct investment
Formulating a plan for the balanced utilisation of national resources
exp: The Planning Commission was set up in March 1950 to make plans for the balanced and effective use of the country's resources.

q: Which of the following is commonly cited as a major advantage of privatisation?
o: It guarantees the achievement of all social-welfare objectives and equitable outcomes
It removes competition from the market and reduces market rivalry
It eliminates every form of market failure and economic inefficiency
It may improve organisational accountability and operational efficiency
exp: Private ownership brings clearer accountability to owners and a profit motive, which can raise efficiency. It does not by itself ensure welfare or remove market failure.

q: Which reform under globalisation reduces custom duties, quotas and quantitative restrictions to facilitate the free flow of goods and services?
exp: Trade liberalisation means cutting customs duties, quotas and other restrictions so that goods and services can move freely across borders.

q: In the economic reform period after 1991, which development made it possible to outsource services such as accounting, banking, music recording, film editing and clinical consultation to India?
exp: Cheaper and better telecommunication links made it possible to do services work in India for clients abroad, which is the basis of outsourcing and BPO.

q: What is the main objective of introducing a risk-based inspection system?
o: To focus inspections on high-risk units and reduce unnecessary inspections
To conduct risk-based inspection of all business units equally
To focus risk-based inspection on increasing the frequency of inspections
To abolish digital governance systems and implement an inspection system in their place
exp: A risk-based inspection system checks the units that carry higher risk more closely, and spares low-risk units from needless inspections.

q: Which of the following is the correct explanation of a consumer surplus?
o: What the consumer pays (-) what it is worth
What the consumer is ready to pay (-) what they actually pay
What the seller quotes as the price (-) what the consumer actually pays
What the seller quotes as the price (-) cost of manufacturing to the seller
exp: Consumer surplus is what the buyer was ready to pay minus what the buyer actually paid. The idea comes from Alfred Marshall.

q: One of the key objectives of the Chelliah Committee during the 1991 economic reforms was to make India's taxation system:
exp: The Chelliah Committee (1991) recommended lower rates with a wider tax base, so that the system would be broad-based, simple and fair.

q: Fill in the blank: Privatisation of public sector enterprises by selling off part of the equity of Public Sector Enterprise (PSE) to the public is known as______.
exp: Selling a part of the equity of a public sector enterprise to the public is called disinvestment.

q: Which statement accurately describes the actual growth outcomes of the First Five-Year Plan?
exp: The First Five Year Plan targeted 2.1% growth and achieved about 3.6%, so it exceeded its target.

q: What does Overseas Direct Investment (ODI) by Indian firms primarily indicate?
exp: Overseas Direct Investment is investment by Indian firms abroad, through joint ventures or subsidiaries. It shows Indian companies expanding their presence overseas.

q: What is the formula for net investment?
exp: Net investment = gross investment minus depreciation. Depreciation is the wearing out of existing capital, so only the rest is a net addition to capital stock.

q: Which of the following areas experienced limits on public expenditure during the economic reforms introduced in India in 1991?
exp: Under fiscal consolidation after 1991, spending on social sectors such as education, health and rural development was held back.

q: Which committee was appointed in 1991 to recommend reforms in India's banking and financial sector?
exp: The Narasimham Committee on the Financial System was set up in 1991 to recommend banking and financial sector reforms.

q: The economic reforms initiated in 1991 promoted which of the following policy combinations?
o: Market based pricing and industrial dereservation
Public ownership and centralised price fixation
Export controls and mandatory production quotas
exp: The 1991 reforms moved towards market-based pricing and removed the reservation of industries for the public sector, together with the end of licensing.

q: Which of the following factors will increase the demand for laptops and shift their demand curve to the right?
o: Increase in the price of laptops
Decrease in consumer income, assuming laptops are normal goods
Increase in the price of internet services used with laptops
Increase in consumers' preference for online education
exp: A stronger preference for online education raises the demand for laptops at every price, so the demand curve shifts to the right.

q: The Break-event Chart portrays the relationship between:
exp: A break-even chart shows how cost, volume of output and profit are related. The break-even point is where total revenue equals total cost.

q: What does the increasing contribution of the services sector after India's 1991 economic reforms mainly indicate?
o: Structural decline of the agricultural sector
Structural decline in the industrial sector
exp: A rising share of services in output is a sign of structural transformation, in which the economy shifts from agriculture to industry and services.

q: Which of the following represents the most comprehensive institutional reform underpinning the "Resolving Insolvency" component in the Ease of Doing Business Index?
exp: The Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 brought in a single time-bound process for resolving insolvency, replacing the older scattered laws.

q: For what purpose is Purchasing Power Parity (PPP) mainly used in the calculation of the Human Development Index (HDI)?
o: To compare income levels of different countries, taking into account differences in the cost of living
To compare unemployment levels in different countries, taking into account differences in labour-force participation
To compare population growth rates in different countries, taking into account differences in demographic trends
To compare literacy levels in different countries, taking into account differences in educational systems
exp: Purchasing Power Parity converts incomes into a common unit that allows for the different cost of living in each country, so real income levels can be compared.

q: What is the SI unit of electric current?
exp: The SI unit of electric current is the ampere (A). Volt is for potential difference, ohm for resistance and watt for power.

q: What is the SI unit of magnetic flux density?
exp: The SI unit of magnetic flux density (B) is the tesla. Weber is the unit of magnetic flux and gauss is the older CGS unit.

q: Which of the following is equivalent to the SI unit of electrical resistance?
exp: From Ohm's law, R = V/I, so resistance is volt per ampere, which is the ohm.

q: What is the commercial unit used for measuring electrical energy?
exp: Electrical energy is sold in kilowatt-hours (kWh), which is what an electricity bill calls one 'unit'. One kWh = 3.6 million joules.

q: Which of the following is the SI unit of electrical capacitance?
exp: The SI unit of capacitance is the farad, named after Michael Faraday. One farad is one coulomb per volt.

q: Ampere-second is the unit of which physical quantity?
exp: Current is charge per unit time, so charge = current x time. Ampere-second is therefore a unit of electric charge, the same as the coulomb.

q: Of which of the following physical quantities is 'candela' the SI unit?
exp: The candela is the SI base unit of luminous intensity, that is, the light given out by a source in a particular direction.

q: Which of the following pairs correctly matches the physical quantity with its SI unit?
exp: Inductance is measured in henry, so pair C is right. Magnetic flux is in weber, flux density in tesla and charge in coulomb.

q: Which of the following is the SI unit of magnetic flux?
exp: The SI unit of magnetic flux is the weber. One weber equals one tesla times one square metre.

q: Which of the following is the SI unit of resistivity?
exp: Resistivity is a property of the material and its SI unit is the ohm-metre. Resistance alone is measured in ohms.

q: A body is projected vertically upward with an initial speed of 20 metres per second. Neglecting air resistance and taking g (gravity) = 10 m/s², what is the maximum height it reaches above the point of projection?
exp: Using v squared = u squared - 2gh with v = 0: h = u squared / 2g = 400 / 20 = 20 metres.

q: Two trains of equal length are running on parallel tracks in opposite directions at speeds of 62 kilometres per hour and 208 kilometres per hour respectively. A passenger sitting in one train observes that the other train completely passes him in 15 seconds. What is the length of each train?
exp: The trains move in opposite directions, so the relative speed is 62 + 208 = 270 km/h = 75 m/s. In 15 seconds the train covers 75 x 15 = 1,125 metres, which is its length.

q: A solid disc and a ring are released together from rest from the same height on the same inclined plane. Both objects roll without slipping. Which of the following reaches the bottom of the inclined plane first?
o: Solid disc or ring, depending on their mass
exp: Acceleration while rolling is a = g sin(theta) / (1 + I/MR squared). For a disc I/MR squared = 1/2 and for a ring it is 1, so the disc has the larger acceleration and reaches the bottom first.

q: A ring and a solid sphere of equal mass and radius are released from rest on the same inclined plane. If both objects roll without slipping, which one has greater linear acceleration?
o: The ring has greater linear acceleration
The solid sphere has greater linear acceleration
Their linear acceleration depends only on the angle of inclination
exp: For a solid sphere I/MR squared = 2/5 and for a ring it is 1. The smaller this ratio, the greater the acceleration, so the sphere accelerates faster.

q: Fill in the blank: Kinetic friction is generally ______ than the maximum static friction.
exp: Once an object starts sliding, the friction needed to keep it moving is less than the maximum static friction, so kinetic friction is smaller.

q: The slope of a distance-time graph represents which physical quantity?
exp: On a distance-time graph the slope is distance divided by time, which is speed.

q: What is the natural tendency of an object, due to which it resists any change in its state of rest or uniform motion, called?
exp: Inertia is the tendency of a body to stay at rest or in uniform motion unless an external force acts on it. It is the subject of Newton's first law.

q: The area under a velocity-time graph represents which physical quantity?
exp: On a velocity-time graph, area equals velocity times time, which gives displacement.

q: When velocity is constant, what is the value of acceleration?
exp: Acceleration is the rate of change of velocity. If the velocity does not change, the acceleration is zero.

q: Which physical quantity is represented by the slope of a line on a velocity-time graph?
exp: The slope of a velocity-time graph is change in velocity divided by time, which is acceleration.

q: Which physical reaction occurs in passengers inside a moving bus when it suddenly comes to a halt?
exp: The lower body stops with the bus but the upper body keeps moving because of the inertia of motion, so the passengers lurch forward.

q: Which quantity is calculated by dividing the total distance travelled by the total time interval?
exp: Total distance divided by total time is average speed. Average velocity uses displacement instead of distance.

q: Which force causes the Earth to bulge at the equator?
exp: The Earth's rotation produces a centrifugal effect that is strongest at the equator, so the Earth bulges there and is flattened at the poles.

q: Which of the following is a scalar quantity?
exp: Speed has magnitude only, so it is a scalar. Displacement, velocity and acceleration have direction as well, so they are vectors.

q: Which physical quantity is given by the product of force and the displacement in the direction of that force?
exp: Work is force multiplied by the displacement in the direction of the force, W = F d cos(theta). It is a scalar quantity measured in joules.

q: How many joules (J) are equivalent to 1 kilowatt hour (kWh)?
exp: 1 kWh = 1000 watts x 3600 seconds = 3.6 x 10^6 joules.

q: A 2 kilogram block moving with a speed of 6 metres per second makes a head-on collision with a stationary 4 kilogram block. After the collision, both blocks stick to each other. Assuming that no external horizontal force acts on the system, what fraction of the initial kinetic energy is lost?
exp: Momentum is conserved, so v = (2 x 6)/6 = 2 m/s. Initial KE = 36 J and final KE = 12 J, so the loss is 24/36, that is 2/3 of the initial energy.

q: Mechanical energy is equal to the sum of kinetic energy and which of the following forms of energy?
exp: Mechanical energy is the sum of kinetic energy and potential energy.

q: The semi-major axis (orbital radius) of an asteroid is 9 AU (astronomical units). According to Kepler's third law, what is the orbital period of the asteroid?
exp: By Kepler's third law, T squared is proportional to a cubed. With a = 9 AU, T = 9 raised to 3/2 = 27 years.

q: If the amplitude of an object undergoing simple harmonic motion is doubled while all other system parameters remain unchanged, how does its total mechanical energy change?
o: It becomes twice its original value
It becomes four times its original value
It becomes eight times its original value
exp: The energy of SHM is E = (1/2) k A squared, so it goes as the square of the amplitude. Doubling A makes the energy four times.

q: A particle executes simple harmonic motion with amplitude A. When its displacement from the mean position is A/2, what percentage of its total mechanical energy is kinetic energy?
exp: Potential energy at displacement x is E x squared / A squared. At x = A/2 that is one fourth of the total, so the kinetic energy is the remaining 75%.

q: A wire of length L and diameter d undergoes an extension when a tensile force F is applied. If both its length and diameter are doubled while applying the same force, what will be its new extension relative to the original extension? Assume that the material remains unchanged and the wire is within its elastic limit.
exp: Extension = FL / AY. Doubling the length doubles it, while doubling the diameter makes the area four times and divides it by four. The net result is half the original extension.

q: What is the process of converting a solid directly into gas called?
exp: Sublimation is the change from solid directly to gas, as happens with camphor, naphthalene balls and dry ice.

q: Why can a constant-volume gas thermometer provide nearly the same temperature reading regardless of the gas used?
o: The density of every gas is kept identical at all temperatures.
Gas pressure becomes independent of changes in volume.
Real gases approach ideal-gas behaviour at sufficiently low pressure.
Mercury expansion compensates for the non-ideal behaviour of gases.
exp: At low pressure all real gases behave almost like an ideal gas, so the thermometer gives nearly the same reading whichever gas is used.

q: A fixed amount of an ideal gas expands at constant pressure. If its volume becomes three times its initial volume, what will be its final absolute temperature in comparison with its initial absolute temperature?
o: It becomes twice the initial temperature
It becomes three times the initial temperature
It becomes nine times the initial temperature
exp: By Charles's law, at constant pressure volume is proportional to absolute temperature. If the volume becomes three times, so does the absolute temperature.

q: One mole of an ideal gas undergoes a reversible isothermal expansion from 10 L(liter) to 20 L (liter) at a constant temperature of 300 K (kelvin). What is the work done by the gas, approximately?
exp: W = nRT ln(V2/V1) = 1 x 8.314 x 300 x ln 2 = about 1,730 joules, which is nearest to 1,700 J.

q: In which of the following mediums do sound waves travel fastest at a given temperature?
exp: Sound travels fastest in solids because their particles are closely packed and elastic, and it cannot travel in a vacuum at all.

q: Which of the following is the frequency range of infrasonic sound waves?
exp: Infrasonic waves have frequencies below 20 Hz, under the range of human hearing. Above 20,000 Hz the waves are ultrasonic.

q: An ideal 12 V (volt) battery is connected across two resistors of 3 Ω (Omega) and 6 Ω (Omega) connected in series. What is the power dissipated in the 6 Ω (Omega) resistor?
exp: Total resistance = 3 + 6 = 9 ohm, so current = 12/9 = 1.33 A. Power in the 6 ohm resistor = I squared R = 1.78 x 6, which is about 10.7 W.

q: Two identical point charges separated by a distance (d) exert an electrostatic force (F) on each other. If the distance between them is reduced to d/3, while the charges and the surrounding medium remain unchanged, what will be the new electrostatic force?
exp: By Coulomb's law the force varies as 1 / distance squared. Reducing the distance to d/3 makes the force 9 times larger.

q: The capacitance of a capacitor is doubled, while the potential difference across it is reduced to half its initial value. By what factor does the energy stored in the capacitor change?
exp: Energy = (1/2) C V squared. Doubling C doubles it, while halving V divides it by four, so the energy becomes half.

q: The magnetic flux through a single-turn conducting loop changes uniformly from 8 weber to 2 weber in 0.5 seconds. What is the magnitude of the average induced emf (electromotive force) in the loop?
exp: By Faraday's law, emf = change in flux / time = (8 - 2) / 0.5 = 12 volts.

q: An object is placed 30 cm (centimeter) in front of a thin converging lens whose focal length is 15 cm (centimeter). What is the distance of the image from the lens?
exp: Using 1/v = 1/f + 1/u with f = 15 cm and u = -30 cm: 1/v = 1/15 - 1/30 = 1/30, so v = 30 cm. The object is at 2F, so the image forms at 2F on the other side.

q: The half-life of a radionuclide is 4 hours. If its initial mass is 160 g (gram), what mass of the radionuclide will remain undecayed after 12 hours?
exp: 12 hours is three half-lives of 4 hours each. The mass left is 160 / 2 / 2 / 2 = 20 grams.

q: Why is the first-order Stark energy correction zero for the non-degenerate hydrogen (1s) ground state in a uniform external electric field?
o: Because the electric field does not interact with bound electrons
Because the ground-state wave function is rotationally symmetric
Because the perturbation commutes with the hydrogen Hamiltonian
Because all excited states are degenerate in energy with the ground state
exp: The 1s ground state is spherically symmetric, so the average position of the electron is at the nucleus and the atom has no permanent dipole moment. The first-order Stark correction is therefore zero.

q: Which physical quantity does an odometer in a vehicle measure?
exp: An odometer records the total distance travelled by a vehicle. A speedometer shows the speed.

q: Which element has the highest electronegativity?
exp: Fluorine is the most electronegative element, with a value of about 4.0 on the Pauling scale. Electronegativity rises across a period and falls down a group.

q: In a hydrogen–oxygen fuel cell, why are porous electrodes coated or impregnated with a catalyst primarily used?
o: To provide large surface area and enhance reaction kinetics
To increase mechanical strength of the electrodes
To store hydrogen and oxygen inside the electrode permanently
To prevent formation of water during the reaction
exp: The electrodes are made porous and coated with a catalyst so that there is a large surface area for the reaction, which speeds up the cell reaction.

q: In the moving boundary method used to determine an ion's transport number, what is the primary purpose of adding an indicator electrolyte to the principal electrolyte?
o: To increase the conductivity of the solution
To ensure complete dissociation of the principal electrolyte
To form a sharp and visible boundary for measuring ion migration
To prevent current flow through the cell
exp: The indicator electrolyte makes a sharp, visible boundary between the two solutions, so the movement of the ions can be measured accurately.

q: Which gas is known as 'laughing gas'?
exp: Nitrous oxide (N2O) is called laughing gas. It is used as a mild anaesthetic and causes a feeling of euphoria.

q: Which intermediate filament protein is most specifically associated with muscle cells?
exp: Desmin is the intermediate filament protein of muscle cells. Vimentin is found in connective tissue, neurofilaments in nerve cells and GFAP in glial cells.

q: When a fully turgid plant cell is placed in a solution with the same solute concentration as its cell sap, which change is most likely to occur first?
exp: In a solution of the same concentration as the cell sap, no net water enters the cell. Water moves out slightly as the wall pushes back, so the turgor pressure falls first.

q: A single bacterial cell reproduces by binary fission, causing the number of cells to double every 20 minutes. How many bacterial cells will be present after 1 hour?
exp: One hour has three periods of 20 minutes. The cells double three times: 1 to 2 to 4 to 8, so 8 cells remain.

q: A fertilized egg, called a zygote, undergoes repeated cell divisions. The number of cells follows this pattern: 1 cell → 2 cells → 4 cells → 8 cells If the number of cells continues to double after each division, how many cells will be present after the next division?
exp: The cells double at each division, so after 8 cells the next division gives 16 cells.

q: Which of the following structural features serves as the defining evolutionary milestone of the division Pteridophyta?
exp: Pteridophytes, such as ferns, were the first plants with true vascular tissue (xylem and phloem), which let them grow tall on land.

q: Which of the following bird-group classifications is correct?
exp: Gulls and terns are seabirds. Ducks and geese are swimming birds, while stilts, sandpipers, herons and cranes are wading birds.

q: Which of the following pairs (Type of Algae – Nutrient Rich In) is correctly matched?
exp: Spirulina, a blue-green alga, is about 60% protein by dry weight, which is why it is sold as a protein supplement.

q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Buff-tip Moth:
1. The larvae of the Buff-tip moth are capable of defoliating an entire tree within a few weeks.
2. "Phalera cf. bucephala" is the scientific name of the Buff-tip moth.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
exp: Both statements are correct as per the key. The larvae of the Buff-tip moth can strip a tree of its leaves in a few weeks, and its scientific name is Phalera bucephala.

q: Two identical green plants are kept in different environmental conditions. Plant A is kept in sunlight, while Plant B is kept in complete darkness for a week. Plant B becomes weak and turns yellow. What is the main reason for this change?
exp: Without light the plant cannot photosynthesise, so it makes no food and loses chlorophyll. That is why it turns yellow and weak.

q: A healthy green plant is kept in complete darkness for three consecutive days. Which biological process is the plant unable to carry out because light is unavailable?
exp: Photosynthesis is the only one of these processes that needs light. Respiration, transpiration and germination go on in the dark.

q: On a hot day, a plant loses water vapour from its leaves through tiny openings on the leaf surface. What are these openings called?
exp: The tiny pores on the leaf surface are stomata. Water vapour escapes through them in transpiration, and gases are exchanged through them too.

q:
Under standard biochemical conditions, the hydrolysis of one mole of ATP (adenosine triphosphate) releases about 7.3 kilocalories of free energy. Assuming complete energy coupling, how many moles of ATP (adenosine triphosphate) must be hydrolysed to provide
29. 2 kilocalories of energy?
exp: 29.2 divided by 7.3 = 4, so four moles of ATP must be hydrolysed.

q: A person has difficulty in digesting fat because bile is not being produced properly. Which organ is most affected?
exp: Bile is made by the liver, so if bile is not produced properly the liver is the organ affected. Bile helps to break fat into small droplets.

q: Which mechanism is mainly responsible for the continuous renewal of the small intestinal epithelium?
o: Cell division occurring equally in the villi and crypts
Proliferation of stem cells in the crypts, producing cells that migrate
Re-entry of cells at the tips of the villi into the cell cycle
Division of Paneth cells, giving rise to all cell lineages
exp: Stem cells in the crypts of the small intestine keep dividing, and the new cells move up along the villus and are shed at the tip. The lining is replaced every few days.

q: A student takes 18 breaths per minute. How many breaths will the student take in 2 hours?
exp: 2 hours = 120 minutes. 18 breaths x 120 = 2,160 breaths.

q: A student repeatedly lifts a 5-kilogram bag and experiences muscle fatigue during the activity. Which substance is traditionally described as accumulating in the muscles when the oxygen supply is insufficient?
exp: When the oxygen supply falls short, the muscles break down glucose anaerobically and lactic acid builds up, which is linked with fatigue and cramps.

q: During physical exercise, a person's pulse rate rises from 70 beats per minute to 110 beats per minute. By how many beats per minute does the pulse rate increase?
exp: 110 - 70 = 40 beats per minute.

q: The cardiac output is 5 litres per minute and the heart rate is 100 beats per minute. What will be the stroke volume?
exp: Stroke volume = cardiac output / heart rate = 5,000 ml / 100 = 50 millilitres.

q: Excessive curvature of the eye lens causes which defect?
exp: If the eye lens is too curved, the image of a distant object forms in front of the retina. This defect is myopia, corrected with a concave lens.

q: What is the major health risk associated with long-term use of anabolic steroids by athletes?
exp: Long-term use of anabolic steroids upsets the body's hormone balance and damages organs such as the liver and heart.

q: Which important micronutrient is essential for DNA replication and whose deficiency causes megaloblastic anaemia?
exp: As per the answer key the answer is vitamin B12. Both vitamin B12 and folate are needed for DNA synthesis, and a lack of either causes megaloblastic anaemia.

q: A child consumes a diet that contains very few fresh fruits and vegetables. After several months, the child develops bleeding gums and reduced resistance to infections. Which vitamin deficiency is the most likely cause of these symptoms?
exp: Bleeding gums and poor resistance to infection point to scurvy, which comes from a lack of vitamin C. Fresh fruit and vegetables are its main source.

q: A rural community uses contaminated pond water for drinking and other daily activities. After a few days, many residents develop complaints of severe diarrhoea and vomiting. Which disease is most likely to spread through the contaminated water?
exp: Cholera, caused by Vibrio cholerae, spreads through water contaminated with faeces and causes severe diarrhoea and vomiting.

q: Which component of innate immunity functions through a regulated proteolytic cascade that can culminate in membrane attack complex formation and pathogen lysis?
exp: The complement system is a set of plasma proteins that act in a cascade. The end product is the membrane attack complex, which punches holes in the pathogen.

q: A vaccine may introduce weakened or inactivated microorganisms, or some of their parts, into the body. What is the main purpose of vaccination?
o: To develop immunity against a specific disease
exp: A vaccine makes the body form antibodies and memory cells against a particular germ, so the person becomes immune to that disease.

q: A child develops soft and weak bones that become bowed because of improper mineralisation. Which deficiency disease is most likely responsible for this condition?
exp: Soft, bowed bones in a child are the sign of rickets, caused by a lack of vitamin D, calcium or phosphate. In adults the same deficiency causes osteomalacia.

q: An antibody titre increases from 1:20 before vaccination to 1:320 after vaccination. By how many times has the antibody titre increased?
exp: 320 divided by 20 = 16, so the titre has risen 16 times.

q: A person who smokes regularly develops damage to the alveoli, the tiny air sacs in the lungs, and experiences difficulty breathing. Which disease is most likely responsible for this condition?
exp: In emphysema the walls of the alveoli are destroyed, so the surface for gas exchange shrinks and breathing becomes difficult. Smoking is the main cause.

q:
Which of the below statement(s) is/are incorrect about B-cells:
1. Produce antibodies
2. Mature in thymus
3. Part of adaptive immunity
4. Derived from bone marrow
exp: Only statement 2 is wrong. B-cells are formed and mature in the bone marrow; it is the T-cells that mature in the thymus.

q: Which process is most directly responsible for the majority of cancer-related deaths?
o: Increased local proliferation of tumor cells
Loss of cell cycle checkpoints in dividing cells
Formation of metastases in distant organs
Formation of benign tumor masses in primary tissue
exp: Most cancer deaths are caused by metastasis, the spread of cancer cells to distant organs, rather than by the primary tumour itself.

q: In a population, the number of prey increases from 400 individuals to 600 individuals in one year. What is the percentage increase in the population during this period?

In a pond ecosystem, pesticide exposure causes a substantial decline in the population of fish that help regulate aquatic insect populations. After some time, the mosquito population increases rapidly. What is the most likely ecological explanation for this increase?
o: Reduced competition among mosquito larvae for aquatic resources
Increased reproductive activity of mosquitoes due to pesticide exposure
Reduced predation on mosquito larvae following the decline in fish population
Decreased water temperature leading to greater mosquito survival
exp: The fish ate the mosquito larvae. When the fish died, that predation stopped, so more larvae survived and the mosquito population shot up.

q: A region experiences rapid deforestation followed by irregular river flow, floods during monsoon, and drought afterward. Which ecological principle does this most strongly demonstrate?
o: Competitive exclusion among species for water resources
Ecological succession after water related disturbance
Regulation of water flow within watersheds
Stabilisation of energy pyramids in water based ecosystems
exp: Forests hold the soil and let rain soak in, so they regulate the flow of water in a watershed. Once the trees go, rain runs off at once, causing floods and then drought.

q: A region experiences deforestation, soil erosion, changes in river flow and changes in the local climate. Which conclusion reflects the most holistic view of the ecosystem?
o: Only the carbon cycle is affected.
Soil erosion occurs independently of biodiversity loss.
Abiotic components are restored immediately after a disturbance.
exp: A disturbance in one part of an ecosystem spreads to the others, so soil, water, climate and living things are all affected together.

q:
With reference to Earth's biosphere, consider the following statements and select the correct option:
1. Photosynthesis is the main process for oxygen production.
2. Forests are the only natural source of oxygen on Earth.
3. Marine ecosystems play an important role in maintaining atmospheric oxygen levels.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
exp: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Photosynthesis produces the oxygen, and marine phytoplankton supply a large part of it, so statement 2 is wrong when it says forests are the only source.

q: Which of the following best explains why ecosystems are considered interdependent systems?
o: Every ecosystem contains equal numbers of organisms.
Abiotic components function independently of living organisms.
Disturbance in one environmental sphere affects the functioning of others.
Ecosystems depend only on climatic conditions.
exp: Ecosystems are interdependent because a disturbance in one sphere, such as the loss of forest, changes the soil, the water and the climate as well.

q: Which statement best explains the ecological significance of protozoa and zooplankton in aquatic ecosystems?
o: They are top carnivores in aquatic ecosystems.
They form the base of aquatic food chains.
They are responsible for coral bleaching.
Their presence is limited only to marine ecosystems.
exp: Protozoa and zooplankton feed on phytoplankton and are eaten by small fish, so they form the base of aquatic food chains.

q: Which statement best distinguishes abiotic components from biotic components in an ecosystem?
o: Soil bacteria are abiotic because they are microscopic.
Organic compounds belong exclusively to biotic components.
Temperature and topography affect species distribution.
Producers are abiotic because they convert solar energy.
exp: Abiotic components are the non-living factors such as temperature, rainfall, soil and topography, and they decide where species can live.

q: Why are pollinators such as insects, birds, and bats considered ecologically important?
o: They are more economically valuable than entire forest ecosystems.
They demonstrate the ecological interdependence between forests and agriculture.
They are the primary species threatened by tourism.
They directly support industrial manufacturing processes.
exp: Pollinators move between forest and farmland and are needed for many crops, which shows how closely forests and agriculture depend on each other.

q: Which of the following best describes the primary ecological function of a food web within a natural habitat?
o: It shows a series of branching lines of interconnected food chains
It shows the seasonal migration routes of various animal species in a region
It estimates the total biomass of producers present at a given trophic level
It identifies the dominant predators that control the population sizes of other species
exp: A food web is a network of interconnected food chains, showing the many feeding links in a habitat.

q: Which type of plasmid lacks a complete conjugation system and therefore requires a self-transmissible helper plasmid for transfer between bacterial cells?
exp: A mobilizable plasmid has the origin of transfer but not the full set of transfer genes, so it needs a conjugative helper plasmid to move to another cell.

q: A bacterial culture initially has 200 bacteria and its number doubles every hour. How many bacteria will be present after 3 hours?
exp: Doubling every hour for 3 hours: 200 to 400 to 800 to 1,600 bacteria.

q: What does the term "PM₂.₅ " mean in the context of air pollution?
o: Particulate matter with a diameter of 2.5 millimeters
Particulate matter with a diameter of 2.5 micrometers
Particulate matter with a diameter of 3.5 millimeters
Particulate matter with a diameter of 3.5 micrometers
exp: PM2.5 means particulate matter with a diameter of 2.5 micrometres or less. These fine particles go deep into the lungs, so they are the most harmful.

q: Which plant is used as a bio-indicator to detect pollution from automobile exhaust?
exp: Lichens are very sensitive to sulphur dioxide and vehicle exhaust, so they disappear from polluted areas. This makes them bio-indicators of air pollution.

q: Under what condition can renewable natural resources become depleted?
o: Renewable natural resources regenerate only through artificial means.
Population growth has no effect on renewable natural resources.
Human consumption of renewable natural resources may exceed their rate of natural regeneration.
Renewable natural resources are immune to environmental degradation.
exp: A renewable resource refills itself over time, but only at a certain rate. If people use it faster than it is renewed, it still runs out.

q: Which of the following pollutants has only an annual National Ambient Air Quality Standard and is therefore not included in India's routine Air Quality Index (AQI) calculation?
exp: Ammonia has only an annual standard under the NAAQS, so it is not used in the routine AQI calculation, as the key states.

q: What is the main objective of the Air Quality Index?
o: To convey earthquake forecasts in a simple form
To convey the status of soil fertility in a simple form
To convey the status of water pollution in a simple form
To convey the status of air quality in a simple form
exp: The AQI turns complex pollution data into a single number and colour, so that ordinary people can understand the day's air quality at a glance.

q: In Air Quality Index (AQI) health guidance, which type of outdoor activity is classified as heavy exertion?
o: An intense activity that causes a person to breathe hard
A light activity that causes little or no physical exertion
A sedentary activity that involves sitting outdoors for an extended period
An indoor activity that is performed exclusively inside a building
exp: In AQI health guidance, heavy exertion means an intense outdoor activity that makes a person breathe hard, such as running or heavy labour.

q: Which of the following is a significant environmental concern in the Indian Ocean?
exp: Warmer seas cause coral bleaching, which is a serious problem in the Indian Ocean, including Lakshadweep and the Andaman islands.

q: Which of the following strategies is ecologically the most sustainable for long-term water-resource management?
o: Construction of large dams, diversion of rivers and centralised water storage.
Groundwater extraction, expansion of deep wells and emergency pumping.
Rainwater harvesting, afforestation and local watershed management.
Expansion of canals, irrigation of cash crops and greater diversion of water.
exp: Rainwater harvesting, afforestation and local watershed management work with nature and recharge groundwater, so they are the most sustainable for the long term.

q: Which of the following situations most clearly expresses Environmental Injustice?
o: Urban communities dependent on rivers that receive adequate water supply
Excessive and disproportionate displacement of tribal communities by the construction of dams despite not receiving equitable benefits
Increase in hydroelectric power generation in industrial areas
Farming communities adopting drip irrigation for water conservation
exp: Environmental injustice means the costs of a project fall on poor or tribal communities while the benefits go elsewhere, as when tribal people are displaced by a dam.

q: The concept of "secondary pollutants" in the Air Quality Index (AQI) is best illustrated by:
o: Direct emission of particulate matter from industrial sources.
Sulphur dioxide emitted from power plants.
Ozone formed by the interaction of NOx and VOCs.
Carbon monoxide released from vehicle exhaust.
exp: A secondary pollutant is not emitted directly but forms in the air. Ground-level ozone, formed when NOx reacts with volatile organic compounds in sunlight, is the standard example.

q: Large-scale environmental degradation in modern societies was mainly caused by which of the following?
o: By rejecting all forms of traditional ecological knowledge.
By using technological innovations that generated no economic benefit.
By pushing economic development forward without considering ecological consequences.
By establishing wildlife sanctuaries that restricted industrial development.
exp: Large-scale damage happened because economic growth was pushed ahead without weighing its ecological cost.

q: Which of the following conclusions can be drawn from India's traditional practices of respect for nature and its conservation?
o: In India, conservation is the responsibility of governments alone.
In India, human existence is independent of the functioning of ecosystems.
Environmental ethics are deeply rooted in Indian traditions.
In India, urbanisation completely separates people from nature.
exp: Indian tradition treats rivers, trees and animals as sacred and protects sacred groves, which shows that environmental ethics are deeply rooted in it.

q: Natural capital is often compared to money deposited in a bank. Which of the following best explains the implication of this analogy?
o: Natural resources can always regenerate if managed by governments.
Sustainable use means utilizing only the regenerative capacity of resources.
Non-renewable resources are equivalent to fixed deposits.
Economic growth depends entirely on resource extraction.
exp: Natural capital is like money in a bank: living off the interest is sustainable, but spending the principal is not. So only the regenerative capacity should be used.

q: Which of the following types of tourism is most directly promoted in India to support the conservation of cultural and natural heritage?
exp: Sustainable tourism is promoted so that visitors do not damage the heritage sites and natural areas they come to see.

q: Which pollutant is primarily responsible for the formation of acid rain?
exp: Sulphur dioxide, along with oxides of nitrogen, turns into sulphuric and nitric acid in the atmosphere and falls as acid rain.

q: A wetland ecosystem is invaded by aquatic weeds after nutrient enrichment from fertilizers. Which sequence correctly describes the ecological process?
o: Oxygen enrichment → fish proliferation → reduced decomposition → algal decline
Nutrient loading → eutrophication → oxygen depletion → aquatic mortality
Weed invasion → salinity increase → coral bleaching → reef degradation
Nutrient reduction → increased decomposition → oxygen depletion → fish extinction
exp: Fertiliser runoff adds nutrients to water. This is nutrient loading, which causes eutrophication, then algal growth and decay use up the oxygen, and aquatic life dies.

q: Large dams are often described as creating a "development paradox" because they:
o: Completely fail to generate electricity and provide irrigation benefits.
Improve agricultural productivity and generate electricity without causing ecological damage.
Promote economic growth while causing ecological and social disruption.
Reduce irrigation efficiency and limit water availability in all regions.
exp: Large dams give irrigation and power but also submerge forests and displace people. Growth with damage alongside it is the development paradox.

q: Under India's National Air Quality Index framework, at least one of the pollutants used for calculating Air Quality Index (AQI) must be which of the following?
exp: In India's AQI, at least one of the pollutants used must be PM2.5 or PM10, because particulate matter is the main health risk.

q: What is a major challenge in accurately assessing the Air Quality Index (AQI) in remote areas?
exp: Remote areas lack continuous monitoring stations and equipment, so there is not enough data to compute a reliable AQI.

q: Under the U.S. (United States) EPA (Environmental Protection Agency) Air Quality Index system, how is the overall Air Quality Index value for a day determined?
o: By considering only the AQI (Air Quality Index)value for ozone
By selecting the lowest AQI (Air Quality Index)value among the monitored pollutants
By selecting the highest AQI (Air Quality Index)value among the monitored pollutants
By calculating the average AQI (Air Quality Index)value of all monitored pollutants
exp: The AQI for a day is the highest of the sub-indices of the monitored pollutants, because the worst pollutant decides the health risk.

q: Under India's National Air Quality Index framework, data for at least how many pollutants are required to calculate the Air Quality Index?
exp: India's AQI needs data for at least three pollutants, one of which must be PM2.5 or PM10.

q: How many categories does the USA Air Quality Index (AQI) use to classify air quality?
exp: The US EPA AQI has six categories, from Good to Hazardous, each with its own colour.

q: As of April 2026, what is the total number of notified Biosphere Reserves in India, and how many among them are part of UNESCO's World Network of Biosphere Reserves (WNBR)?
exp: As per the answer key, India has 18 notified Biosphere Reserves, of which 13 are in UNESCO's World Network of Biosphere Reserves.

q: Which statement best explains how biodiversity contributes to food security?
o: Food security depends only on increasing fertilizer use.
Conserving wild relatives of crops is essential for future agricultural resilience.
Protected areas have no role in food security.
exp: Wild relatives of crops carry genes for resistance to drought, pests and disease. Keeping them alive gives breeders material for future crops, which protects food security.

q: In biodiversity conservation, why is the preservation of wild relatives of crop plants considered strategically important?
o: They are aesthetically valuable tourist attractions.
They reduce dependence on forests for timber.
They provide useful genes for crop improvement.
exp: Crop wild relatives are a reservoir of useful genes. Breeders use them to improve yield and to add resistance to pests, disease and drought.

q: Which of the following organisations is correctly matched with one of its major contributions?
o: World Wide Fund for Nature–India (WWF-India) — Conducting systematic faunal surveys in India
Bombay Natural History Society (BNHS) — Leading wildlife research and influencing conservation policy
Zoological Survey of India (ZSI) — Publishing Down To Earth magazine
Centre for Science and Environment (CSE) — Managing wildlife protected-area networks
exp: The Bombay Natural History Society (1883) is known for wildlife research and for shaping conservation policy. Faunal surveys are done by the Zoological Survey of India, and 'Down To Earth' is published by the Centre for Science and Environment.

q: Which of the following statements about the gharial is most accurate?
o: Gharials are widely found throughout India.
Gharials are endangered mainly due to a lack of natural prey.
The gharial is endemic to India and critically endangered.
Gharials are generally found in both freshwater and marine habitats.
exp: The gharial is a fish-eating crocodilian of the northern Indian river systems. It is critically endangered and is treated as endemic to India in the key.

q: Which environmentalist from Assam is known for single-handedly developing a forest through his own efforts and is popularly called the "Forest Man of India"?
exp: Jadav Payeng of Jorhat, Assam, planted trees on a sandbar for decades and grew a whole forest, so he is called the 'Forest Man of India'.

q: Which of the following situations most appropriately represents the "Option Value" of nature?
o: Rapidly exploiting forests and prioritising short-term economic gains.
Setting up industries near wetlands and maximising employment opportunities.
Conserving biodiversity and preserving its potential future benefits and uses.
Converting land into agricultural plantations by completely replacing natural forests.
exp: Option value is the value of keeping something available for possible future use. Conserving biodiversity today keeps open benefits we may need later.

q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Chhari-Dhand wetland:
1. It is located in Kachchh district of Gujarat and was designated as a Ramsar site in January 2026.
2. This wetland is a habitat for threatened species such as the Dalmatian Pelican, Oriental Darter and Indian Skimmer.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
exp: Both statements are correct as per the key. Chhari-Dhand is in Kachchh district, Gujarat, on the edge of the Banni grasslands, and it supports threatened birds such as the Dalmatian Pelican and Indian Skimmer.

q: Which of the following is a major cause of the decline in the amphibian population in India?
o: Expansion of natural wetlands and suitable habitats
Habitat loss, climate change and environmental pollution
Increase in breeding habitats and availability of resources
Absence of invasive species and ecological competition
exp: Amphibians have thin, moist skin and breed in water, so habitat loss, climate change and pollution hit them hardest.

q: Which statement most accurately captures the relationship between biodiversity and human survival described?
o: Biodiversity has aesthetic value but no economic importance.
Human societies function independently of ecosystems.
Only domesticated species support human welfare.
exp: Biodiversity supplies ecosystem services such as clean air and water, pollination, soil formation and climate regulation, on which human survival depends.

q:
Consider the following statements about Shekha Jheel Bird Sanctuary:
1. It is located in the Aligarh district of Uttar Pradesh.
2. It was designated as Uttar Pradesh's 12th Ramsar site and India's 99th Ramsar site in April 2026.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
exp: Both statements are correct as per the key: Shekha Jheel is in Aligarh district of Uttar Pradesh and was named a Ramsar site in 2026.

q:
Consider the following statements about the One Sun, One World, One Grid (OSOWOG) initiative:
1) It promotes cross-border solar energy sharing among nations.
2) It replaces energy storage with coal-based backup systems.
Which of the above is/are correct?
exp: Statement 1 is correct: OSOWOG is about sharing solar power across borders through a connected grid. Statement 2 is wrong, since the idea is to replace fossil fuels, not to use coal backup.

q: Which ecological goal is not a primary aim of the Aravalli Green Wall Initiative?
exp: The Aravalli Green Wall Project aims to check desertification, store carbon and recharge groundwater. Monoculture farming is not one of its goals.

q: According to the National Green Hydrogen Mission, what is India's annual green hydrogen production target for the year 2030?
exp: The National Green Hydrogen Mission (2023) targets 5 million tonnes of green hydrogen production a year by 2030.

q: In India, under the PM-PRANAM (PM Programme for Restoration, Awareness Generation, Nourishment, and Amelioration of Mother Earth) scheme, States/UTs that reduce their chemical fertilizer consumption are rewarded with what percentage of the fertilizer subsidy saved by the Centre as a grant?
o: 50% of the fertilizer subsidy saved by the Centre as a grant
25% of the fertilizer subsidy saved by the Centre as a grant
75% of the fertilizer subsidy saved by the Centre as a grant
100% of the fertilizer subsidy saved by the Centre as a grant
exp: Under PM-PRANAM, a state that cuts its chemical fertiliser use gets back 50% of the subsidy the Centre saves, as a grant for other work.

q: According to the Urban and Regional Development Plans Formulation and Implementation (URDPFI) Guidelines, 2014, which of the following concepts is associated with climate change mitigation?
exp: In the URDPFI Guidelines, the green building concept, with energy and water efficiency and low emissions, is linked to climate change mitigation.

q: The National Mission on Biodiversity and Human Well-being mentioned in the 2025 vision document is primarily driven by which of the following?
o: NITI Aayog and Ministry of Finance
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change and PM-STIAC
Ministry of Science and Technology and ISRO
exp: The National Mission on Biodiversity and Human Well-being is driven by the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change along with the PM's Science, Technology and Innovation Advisory Council.

q: What is the name of the system that provides location-specific air quality and weather forecasts?
exp: SAFAR stands for System of Air Quality and Weather Forecasting And Research. It gives location-specific air quality and weather forecasts in major cities.

q: Under the MISHTI (Mangrove Initiative for Shoreline Habitats & Tangible Incomes) initiative, which resource is prioritized for conservation and plantation along India's shoreline?
o: Bamboo clusters in the North East
exp: MISHTI is for planting and protecting mangroves along India's coastline and on salt pan lands.

q: What was the main goal of the Mangrove Co-Management Committee formed in Navghar under the climate resilience project?
o: To promote seasonal fishing and crab collection
To protect mangroves and revive local livelihoods
To increase tourism in coastal Maharashtra
To replace mangroves with modern aquaculture farms
exp: The Mangrove Co-Management Committee at Navghar was formed to protect the mangroves and at the same time restore local livelihoods such as fishing and crab farming.

q: What is the natural tendency of an object, due to which it resists any change in its state of rest or uniform motion, called?
exp: Inertia is the tendency of a body to stay at rest or in uniform motion unless an external force acts on it. It is the subject of Newton's first law.

q: A child consumes a diet that contains very few fresh fruits and vegetables. After several months, the child develops bleeding gums and reduced resistance to infections. Which vitamin deficiency is the most likely cause of these symptoms?
exp: Bleeding gums and poor resistance to infection point to scurvy, which comes from a lack of vitamin C. Fresh fruit and vegetables are its main source.

q: The semi-major axis (orbital radius) of an asteroid is 9 AU (astronomical units). According to Kepler's third law, what is the orbital period of the asteroid?
exp: By Kepler's third law, T squared is proportional to a cubed. With a = 9 AU, T = 9 raised to 3/2 = 27 years.

q: What is the commercial unit used for measuring electrical energy?
exp: Electrical energy is sold in kilowatt-hours (kWh), which is what an electricity bill calls one 'unit'. One kWh = 3.6 million joules.

q: Which statement most accurately captures the relationship between biodiversity and human survival described?
o: Biodiversity has aesthetic value but no economic importance.
Human societies function independently of ecosystems.
Only domesticated species support human welfare.
exp: Biodiversity supplies ecosystem services such as clean air and water, pollination, soil formation and climate regulation, on which human survival depends.

q: Under India's National Air Quality Index framework, at least one of the pollutants used for calculating Air Quality Index (AQI) must be which of the following?
exp: In India's AQI, at least one of the pollutants used must be PM2.5 or PM10, because particulate matter is the main health risk.

q: In a hydrogen–oxygen fuel cell, why are porous electrodes coated or impregnated with a catalyst primarily used?
o: To provide large surface area and enhance reaction kinetics
To increase mechanical strength of the electrodes
To store hydrogen and oxygen inside the electrode permanently
To prevent formation of water during the reaction
exp: The electrodes are made porous and coated with a catalyst so that there is a large surface area for the reaction, which speeds up the cell reaction.

q: In which of the following mediums do sound waves travel fastest at a given temperature?
exp: Sound travels fastest in solids because their particles are closely packed and elastic, and it cannot travel in a vacuum at all.

q: Excessive curvature of the eye lens causes which defect?
exp: If the eye lens is too curved, the image of a distant object forms in front of the retina. This defect is myopia, corrected with a concave lens.

q: The slope of a distance-time graph represents which physical quantity?
exp: On a distance-time graph the slope is distance divided by time, which is speed.

q: Which of the following is a significant environmental concern in the Indian Ocean?
exp: Warmer seas cause coral bleaching, which is a serious problem in the Indian Ocean, including Lakshadweep and the Andaman islands.

q: Large-scale environmental degradation in modern societies was mainly caused by which of the following?
o: By rejecting all forms of traditional ecological knowledge.
By using technological innovations that generated no economic benefit.
By pushing economic development forward without considering ecological consequences.
By establishing wildlife sanctuaries that restricted industrial development.
exp: Large-scale damage happened because economic growth was pushed ahead without weighing its ecological cost.

q: A region experiences rapid deforestation followed by irregular river flow, floods during monsoon, and drought afterward. Which ecological principle does this most strongly demonstrate?
o: Competitive exclusion among species for water resources
Ecological succession after water related disturbance
Regulation of water flow within watersheds
Stabilisation of energy pyramids in water based ecosystems
exp: Forests hold the soil and let rain soak in, so they regulate the flow of water in a watershed. Once the trees go, rain runs off at once, causing floods and then drought.

q: What is a major challenge in accurately assessing the Air Quality Index (AQI) in remote areas?
exp: Remote areas lack continuous monitoring stations and equipment, so there is not enough data to compute a reliable AQI.

q: A fixed amount of an ideal gas expands at constant pressure. If its volume becomes three times its initial volume, what will be its final absolute temperature in comparison with its initial absolute temperature?
o: It becomes twice the initial temperature
It becomes three times the initial temperature
It becomes nine times the initial temperature
exp: By Charles's law, at constant pressure volume is proportional to absolute temperature. If the volume becomes three times, so does the absolute temperature.

q: Which of the following pairs correctly matches the physical quantity with its SI unit?
exp: Inductance is measured in henry, so pair C is right. Magnetic flux is in weber, flux density in tesla and charge in coulomb.

q: A fertilized egg, called a zygote, undergoes repeated cell divisions. The number of cells follows this pattern: 1 cell → 2 cells → 4 cells → 8 cells If the number of cells continues to double after each division, how many cells will be present after the next division?
exp: The cells double at each division, so after 8 cells the next division gives 16 cells.

q: Two trains of equal length are running on parallel tracks in opposite directions at speeds of 62 kilometres per hour and 208 kilometres per hour respectively. A passenger sitting in one train observes that the other train completely passes him in 15 seconds. What is the length of each train?
exp: The trains move in opposite directions, so the relative speed is 62 + 208 = 270 km/h = 75 m/s. In 15 seconds the train covers 75 x 15 = 1,125 metres, which is its length.

q: On a hot day, a plant loses water vapour from its leaves through tiny openings on the leaf surface. What are these openings called?
exp: The tiny pores on the leaf surface are stomata. Water vapour escapes through them in transpiration, and gases are exchanged through them too.

q: In India, under the PM-PRANAM (PM Programme for Restoration, Awareness Generation, Nourishment, and Amelioration of Mother Earth) scheme, States/UTs that reduce their chemical fertilizer consumption are rewarded with what percentage of the fertilizer subsidy saved by the Centre as a grant?
o: 50% of the fertilizer subsidy saved by the Centre as a grant
25% of the fertilizer subsidy saved by the Centre as a grant
75% of the fertilizer subsidy saved by the Centre as a grant
100% of the fertilizer subsidy saved by the Centre as a grant
exp: Under PM-PRANAM, a state that cuts its chemical fertiliser use gets back 50% of the subsidy the Centre saves, as a grant for other work.

q: The concept of "secondary pollutants" in the Air Quality Index (AQI) is best illustrated by:
o: Direct emission of particulate matter from industrial sources.
Sulphur dioxide emitted from power plants.
Ozone formed by the interaction of NOx and VOCs.
Carbon monoxide released from vehicle exhaust.
