exp: A secondary pollutant is not emitted directly but forms in the air. Ground-level ozone, formed when NOx reacts with volatile organic compounds in sunlight, is the standard example.

q: Which of the following is a scalar quantity?
exp: Speed has magnitude only, so it is a scalar. Displacement, velocity and acceleration have direction as well, so they are vectors.

q: Ampere-second is the unit of which physical quantity?
exp: Current is charge per unit time, so charge = current x time. Ampere-second is therefore a unit of electric charge, the same as the coulomb.

q: Two identical point charges separated by a distance (d) exert an electrostatic force (F) on each other. If the distance between them is reduced to d/3, while the charges and the surrounding medium remain unchanged, what will be the new electrostatic force?
exp: By Coulomb's law the force varies as 1 / distance squared. Reducing the distance to d/3 makes the force 9 times larger.

q: Which physical quantity is given by the product of force and the displacement in the direction of that force?
exp: Work is force multiplied by the displacement in the direction of the force, W = F d cos(theta). It is a scalar quantity measured in joules.

q: Which of the following structural features serves as the defining evolutionary milestone of the division Pteridophyta?
exp: Pteridophytes, such as ferns, were the first plants with true vascular tissue (xylem and phloem), which let them grow tall on land.

q: A person who smokes regularly develops damage to the alveoli, the tiny air sacs in the lungs, and experiences difficulty breathing. Which disease is most likely responsible for this condition?
exp: In emphysema the walls of the alveoli are destroyed, so the surface for gas exchange shrinks and breathing becomes difficult. Smoking is the main cause.

q: Why are pollinators such as insects, birds, and bats considered ecologically important?
o: They are more economically valuable than entire forest ecosystems.
They demonstrate the ecological interdependence between forests and agriculture.
They are the primary species threatened by tourism.
They directly support industrial manufacturing processes.
exp: Pollinators move between forest and farmland and are needed for many crops, which shows how closely forests and agriculture depend on each other.

q: In biodiversity conservation, why is the preservation of wild relatives of crop plants considered strategically important?
o: They are aesthetically valuable tourist attractions.
They reduce dependence on forests for timber.
They provide useful genes for crop improvement.
exp: Crop wild relatives are a reservoir of useful genes. Breeders use them to improve yield and to add resistance to pests, disease and drought.

q: The National Mission on Biodiversity and Human Well-being mentioned in the 2025 vision document is primarily driven by which of the following?
o: NITI Aayog and Ministry of Finance
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change and PM-STIAC
Ministry of Science and Technology and ISRO
exp: The National Mission on Biodiversity and Human Well-being is driven by the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change along with the PM's Science, Technology and Innovation Advisory Council.

q: Which force causes the Earth to bulge at the equator?
exp: The Earth's rotation produces a centrifugal effect that is strongest at the equator, so the Earth bulges there and is flattened at the poles.

q: Which physical reaction occurs in passengers inside a moving bus when it suddenly comes to a halt?
exp: The lower body stops with the bus but the upper body keeps moving because of the inertia of motion, so the passengers lurch forward.

q: Which pollutant is primarily responsible for the formation of acid rain?
exp: Sulphur dioxide, along with oxides of nitrogen, turns into sulphuric and nitric acid in the atmosphere and falls as acid rain.

q: Which element has the highest electronegativity?
exp: Fluorine is the most electronegative element, with a value of about 4.0 on the Pauling scale. Electronegativity rises across a period and falls down a group.

q: In Air Quality Index (AQI) health guidance, which type of outdoor activity is classified as heavy exertion?
o: An intense activity that causes a person to breathe hard
A light activity that causes little or no physical exertion
A sedentary activity that involves sitting outdoors for an extended period
An indoor activity that is performed exclusively inside a building
exp: In AQI health guidance, heavy exertion means an intense outdoor activity that makes a person breathe hard, such as running or heavy labour.

q: Under the MISHTI (Mangrove Initiative for Shoreline Habitats & Tangible Incomes) initiative, which resource is prioritized for conservation and plantation along India's shoreline?
o: Bamboo clusters in the North East
exp: MISHTI is for planting and protecting mangroves along India's coastline and on salt pan lands.

q: A vaccine may introduce weakened or inactivated microorganisms, or some of their parts, into the body. What is the main purpose of vaccination?
o: To develop immunity against a specific disease
exp: A vaccine makes the body form antibodies and memory cells against a particular germ, so the person becomes immune to that disease.

q:
Which of the below statement(s) is/are incorrect about B-cells:
1. Produce antibodies
2. Mature in thymus
3. Part of adaptive immunity
4. Derived from bone marrow
exp: Only statement 2 is wrong. B-cells are formed and mature in the bone marrow; it is the T-cells that mature in the thymus.

q: What does the term "PM₂.₅ " mean in the context of air pollution?
o: Particulate matter with a diameter of 2.5 millimeters
Particulate matter with a diameter of 2.5 micrometers
Particulate matter with a diameter of 3.5 millimeters
Particulate matter with a diameter of 3.5 micrometers
exp: PM2.5 means particulate matter with a diameter of 2.5 micrometres or less. These fine particles go deep into the lungs, so they are the most harmful.

q: A 2 kilogram block moving with a speed of 6 metres per second makes a head-on collision with a stationary 4 kilogram block. After the collision, both blocks stick to each other. Assuming that no external horizontal force acts on the system, what fraction of the initial kinetic energy is lost?
exp: Momentum is conserved, so v = (2 x 6)/6 = 2 m/s. Initial KE = 36 J and final KE = 12 J, so the loss is 24/36, that is 2/3 of the initial energy.

q: Which statement best explains how biodiversity contributes to food security?
o: Food security depends only on increasing fertilizer use.
Conserving wild relatives of crops is essential for future agricultural resilience.
Protected areas have no role in food security.
exp: Wild relatives of crops carry genes for resistance to drought, pests and disease. Keeping them alive gives breeders material for future crops, which protects food security.

q: Which of the following strategies is ecologically the most sustainable for long-term water-resource management?
o: Construction of large dams, diversion of rivers and centralised water storage.
Groundwater extraction, expansion of deep wells and emergency pumping.
Rainwater harvesting, afforestation and local watershed management.
Expansion of canals, irrigation of cash crops and greater diversion of water.
exp: Rainwater harvesting, afforestation and local watershed management work with nature and recharge groundwater, so they are the most sustainable for the long term.

q: Which of the following is a major cause of the decline in the amphibian population in India?
o: Expansion of natural wetlands and suitable habitats
Habitat loss, climate change and environmental pollution
Increase in breeding habitats and availability of resources
Absence of invasive species and ecological competition
exp: Amphibians have thin, moist skin and breed in water, so habitat loss, climate change and pollution hit them hardest.

q: A single bacterial cell reproduces by binary fission, causing the number of cells to double every 20 minutes. How many bacterial cells will be present after 1 hour?
exp: One hour has three periods of 20 minutes. The cells double three times: 1 to 2 to 4 to 8, so 8 cells remain.

q: Which statement best explains the ecological significance of protozoa and zooplankton in aquatic ecosystems?
o: They are top carnivores in aquatic ecosystems.
They form the base of aquatic food chains.
They are responsible for coral bleaching.
Their presence is limited only to marine ecosystems.
exp: Protozoa and zooplankton feed on phytoplankton and are eaten by small fish, so they form the base of aquatic food chains.

q: A wire of length L and diameter d undergoes an extension when a tensile force F is applied. If both its length and diameter are doubled while applying the same force, what will be its new extension relative to the original extension? Assume that the material remains unchanged and the wire is within its elastic limit.
exp: Extension = FL / AY. Doubling the length doubles it, while doubling the diameter makes the area four times and divides it by four. The net result is half the original extension.

q: The area under a velocity-time graph represents which physical quantity?
exp: On a velocity-time graph, area equals velocity times time, which gives displacement.

q: The half-life of a radionuclide is 4 hours. If its initial mass is 160 g (gram), what mass of the radionuclide will remain undecayed after 12 hours?
exp: 12 hours is three half-lives of 4 hours each. The mass left is 160 / 2 / 2 / 2 = 20 grams.

q: Which of the following is equivalent to the SI unit of electrical resistance?
exp: From Ohm's law, R = V/I, so resistance is volt per ampere, which is the ohm.

q: Of which of the following physical quantities is 'candela' the SI unit?
exp: The candela is the SI base unit of luminous intensity, that is, the light given out by a source in a particular direction.

q: Which statement best distinguishes abiotic components from biotic components in an ecosystem?
o: Soil bacteria are abiotic because they are microscopic.
Organic compounds belong exclusively to biotic components.
Temperature and topography affect species distribution.
Producers are abiotic because they convert solar energy.
exp: Abiotic components are the non-living factors such as temperature, rainfall, soil and topography, and they decide where species can live.

q: During physical exercise, a person's pulse rate rises from 70 beats per minute to 110 beats per minute. By how many beats per minute does the pulse rate increase?
exp: 110 - 70 = 40 beats per minute.

q: What is the name of the system that provides location-specific air quality and weather forecasts?
exp: SAFAR stands for System of Air Quality and Weather Forecasting And Research. It gives location-specific air quality and weather forecasts in major cities.

q: Which of the following conclusions can be drawn from India's traditional practices of respect for nature and its conservation?
o: In India, conservation is the responsibility of governments alone.
In India, human existence is independent of the functioning of ecosystems.
Environmental ethics are deeply rooted in Indian traditions.
In India, urbanisation completely separates people from nature.
exp: Indian tradition treats rivers, trees and animals as sacred and protects sacred groves, which shows that environmental ethics are deeply rooted in it.

q: According to the Urban and Regional Development Plans Formulation and Implementation (URDPFI) Guidelines, 2014, which of the following concepts is associated with climate change mitigation?
exp: In the URDPFI Guidelines, the green building concept, with energy and water efficiency and low emissions, is linked to climate change mitigation.

q: A person has difficulty in digesting fat because bile is not being produced properly. Which organ is most affected?
exp: Bile is made by the liver, so if bile is not produced properly the liver is the organ affected. Bile helps to break fat into small droplets.

q:
Under standard biochemical conditions, the hydrolysis of one mole of ATP (adenosine triphosphate) releases about 7.3 kilocalories of free energy. Assuming complete energy coupling, how many moles of ATP (adenosine triphosphate) must be hydrolysed to provide
29. 2 kilocalories of energy?
exp: 29.2 divided by 7.3 = 4, so four moles of ATP must be hydrolysed.

q: A region experiences deforestation, soil erosion, changes in river flow and changes in the local climate. Which conclusion reflects the most holistic view of the ecosystem?
o: Only the carbon cycle is affected.
Soil erosion occurs independently of biodiversity loss.
Abiotic components are restored immediately after a disturbance.
exp: A disturbance in one part of an ecosystem spreads to the others, so soil, water, climate and living things are all affected together.

q: Which of the following bird-group classifications is correct?
exp: Gulls and terns are seabirds. Ducks and geese are swimming birds, while stilts, sandpipers, herons and cranes are wading birds.

q: An ideal 12 V (volt) battery is connected across two resistors of 3 Ω (Omega) and 6 Ω (Omega) connected in series. What is the power dissipated in the 6 Ω (Omega) resistor?
exp: Total resistance = 3 + 6 = 9 ohm, so current = 12/9 = 1.33 A. Power in the 6 ohm resistor = I squared R = 1.78 x 6, which is about 10.7 W.

q: What is the SI unit of magnetic flux density?
exp: The SI unit of magnetic flux density (B) is the tesla. Weber is the unit of magnetic flux and gauss is the older CGS unit.

q: Which of the following is the frequency range of infrasonic sound waves?
exp: Infrasonic waves have frequencies below 20 Hz, under the range of human hearing. Above 20,000 Hz the waves are ultrasonic.

q: What is the SI unit of electric current?
exp: The SI unit of electric current is the ampere (A). Volt is for potential difference, ohm for resistance and watt for power.

q:
Consider the following statements about the One Sun, One World, One Grid (OSOWOG) initiative:
1) It promotes cross-border solar energy sharing among nations.
2) It replaces energy storage with coal-based backup systems.
Which of the above is/are correct?
exp: Statement 1 is correct: OSOWOG is about sharing solar power across borders through a connected grid. Statement 2 is wrong, since the idea is to replace fossil fuels, not to use coal backup.

q: Two identical green plants are kept in different environmental conditions. Plant A is kept in sunlight, while Plant B is kept in complete darkness for a week. Plant B becomes weak and turns yellow. What is the main reason for this change?
exp: Without light the plant cannot photosynthesise, so it makes no food and loses chlorophyll. That is why it turns yellow and weak.

q:
With reference to Earth's biosphere, consider the following statements and select the correct option:
1. Photosynthesis is the main process for oxygen production.
2. Forests are the only natural source of oxygen on Earth.
3. Marine ecosystems play an important role in maintaining atmospheric oxygen levels.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
exp: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Photosynthesis produces the oxygen, and marine phytoplankton supply a large part of it, so statement 2 is wrong when it says forests are the only source.

q: Which of the following statements about the gharial is most accurate?
o: Gharials are widely found throughout India.
Gharials are endangered mainly due to a lack of natural prey.
The gharial is endemic to India and critically endangered.
Gharials are generally found in both freshwater and marine habitats.
exp: The gharial is a fish-eating crocodilian of the northern Indian river systems. It is critically endangered and is treated as endemic to India in the key.

q: Natural capital is often compared to money deposited in a bank. Which of the following best explains the implication of this analogy?
o: Natural resources can always regenerate if managed by governments.
Sustainable use means utilizing only the regenerative capacity of resources.
Non-renewable resources are equivalent to fixed deposits.
Economic growth depends entirely on resource extraction.
exp: Natural capital is like money in a bank: living off the interest is sustainable, but spending the principal is not. So only the regenerative capacity should be used.

q: A body is projected vertically upward with an initial speed of 20 metres per second. Neglecting air resistance and taking g (gravity) = 10 m/s², what is the maximum height it reaches above the point of projection?
exp: Using v squared = u squared - 2gh with v = 0: h = u squared / 2g = 400 / 20 = 20 metres.

q: A solid disc and a ring are released together from rest from the same height on the same inclined plane. Both objects roll without slipping. Which of the following reaches the bottom of the inclined plane first?
o: Solid disc or ring, depending on their mass
exp: Acceleration while rolling is a = g sin(theta) / (1 + I/MR squared). For a disc I/MR squared = 1/2 and for a ring it is 1, so the disc has the larger acceleration and reaches the bottom first.

q: What is the process of converting a solid directly into gas called?
exp: Sublimation is the change from solid directly to gas, as happens with camphor, naphthalene balls and dry ice.

q: If the amplitude of an object undergoing simple harmonic motion is doubled while all other system parameters remain unchanged, how does its total mechanical energy change?
o: It becomes twice its original value
It becomes four times its original value
It becomes eight times its original value
exp: The energy of SHM is E = (1/2) k A squared, so it goes as the square of the amplitude. Doubling A makes the energy four times.

q: Why can a constant-volume gas thermometer provide nearly the same temperature reading regardless of the gas used?
o: The density of every gas is kept identical at all temperatures.
Gas pressure becomes independent of changes in volume.
Real gases approach ideal-gas behaviour at sufficiently low pressure.
Mercury expansion compensates for the non-ideal behaviour of gases.
exp: At low pressure all real gases behave almost like an ideal gas, so the thermometer gives nearly the same reading whichever gas is used.

q: When velocity is constant, what is the value of acceleration?
exp: Acceleration is the rate of change of velocity. If the velocity does not change, the acceleration is zero.

q: Which of the following situations most clearly expresses Environmental Injustice?
o: Urban communities dependent on rivers that receive adequate water supply
Excessive and disproportionate displacement of tribal communities by the construction of dams despite not receiving equitable benefits
Increase in hydroelectric power generation in industrial areas
Farming communities adopting drip irrigation for water conservation
exp: Environmental injustice means the costs of a project fall on poor or tribal communities while the benefits go elsewhere, as when tribal people are displaced by a dam.

q: Which of the following best explains why ecosystems are considered interdependent systems?
o: Every ecosystem contains equal numbers of organisms.
Abiotic components function independently of living organisms.
Disturbance in one environmental sphere affects the functioning of others.
Ecosystems depend only on climatic conditions.
exp: Ecosystems are interdependent because a disturbance in one sphere, such as the loss of forest, changes the soil, the water and the climate as well.

q: Under what condition can renewable natural resources become depleted?
o: Renewable natural resources regenerate only through artificial means.
Population growth has no effect on renewable natural resources.
Human consumption of renewable natural resources may exceed their rate of natural regeneration.
Renewable natural resources are immune to environmental degradation.
exp: A renewable resource refills itself over time, but only at a certain rate. If people use it faster than it is renewed, it still runs out.

q: Which ecological goal is not a primary aim of the Aravalli Green Wall Initiative?
exp: The Aravalli Green Wall Project aims to check desertification, store carbon and recharge groundwater. Monoculture farming is not one of its goals.

q: Which process is most directly responsible for the majority of cancer-related deaths?
o: Increased local proliferation of tumor cells
Loss of cell cycle checkpoints in dividing cells
Formation of metastases in distant organs
Formation of benign tumor masses in primary tissue
exp: Most cancer deaths are caused by metastasis, the spread of cancer cells to distant organs, rather than by the primary tumour itself.

q: Which of the following organisations is correctly matched with one of its major contributions?
o: World Wide Fund for Nature–India (WWF-India) — Conducting systematic faunal surveys in India
Bombay Natural History Society (BNHS) — Leading wildlife research and influencing conservation policy
Zoological Survey of India (ZSI) — Publishing Down To Earth magazine
Centre for Science and Environment (CSE) — Managing wildlife protected-area networks
exp: The Bombay Natural History Society (1883) is known for wildlife research and for shaping conservation policy. Faunal surveys are done by the Zoological Survey of India, and 'Down To Earth' is published by the Centre for Science and Environment.

q: Which of the following is the SI unit of resistivity?
exp: Resistivity is a property of the material and its SI unit is the ohm-metre. Resistance alone is measured in ohms.

q: Which physical quantity does an odometer in a vehicle measure?
exp: An odometer records the total distance travelled by a vehicle. A speedometer shows the speed.

q: Mechanical energy is equal to the sum of kinetic energy and which of the following forms of energy?
exp: Mechanical energy is the sum of kinetic energy and potential energy.

q: The magnetic flux through a single-turn conducting loop changes uniformly from 8 weber to 2 weber in 0.5 seconds. What is the magnitude of the average induced emf (electromotive force) in the loop?
exp: By Faraday's law, emf = change in flux / time = (8 - 2) / 0.5 = 12 volts.

q: Large dams are often described as creating a "development paradox" because they:
o: Completely fail to generate electricity and provide irrigation benefits.
Improve agricultural productivity and generate electricity without causing ecological damage.
Promote economic growth while causing ecological and social disruption.
Reduce irrigation efficiency and limit water availability in all regions.
exp: Large dams give irrigation and power but also submerge forests and displace people. Growth with damage alongside it is the development paradox.

q: A student takes 18 breaths per minute. How many breaths will the student take in 2 hours?
exp: 2 hours = 120 minutes. 18 breaths x 120 = 2,160 breaths.

q: Which gas is known as 'laughing gas'?
exp: Nitrous oxide (N2O) is called laughing gas. It is used as a mild anaesthetic and causes a feeling of euphoria.

q: What is the main objective of the Air Quality Index?
o: To convey earthquake forecasts in a simple form
To convey the status of soil fertility in a simple form
To convey the status of water pollution in a simple form
To convey the status of air quality in a simple form
exp: The AQI turns complex pollution data into a single number and colour, so that ordinary people can understand the day's air quality at a glance.

q: What is the major health risk associated with long-term use of anabolic steroids by athletes?
exp: Long-term use of anabolic steroids upsets the body's hormone balance and damages organs such as the liver and heart.

q: Under the U.S. (United States) EPA (Environmental Protection Agency) Air Quality Index system, how is the overall Air Quality Index value for a day determined?
o: By considering only the AQI (Air Quality Index)value for ozone
By selecting the lowest AQI (Air Quality Index)value among the monitored pollutants
By selecting the highest AQI (Air Quality Index)value among the monitored pollutants
By calculating the average AQI (Air Quality Index)value of all monitored pollutants
exp: The AQI for a day is the highest of the sub-indices of the monitored pollutants, because the worst pollutant decides the health risk.

q: How many joules (J) are equivalent to 1 kilowatt hour (kWh)?
exp: 1 kWh = 1000 watts x 3600 seconds = 3.6 x 10^6 joules.

q: Which of the following is the SI unit of magnetic flux?
exp: The SI unit of magnetic flux is the weber. One weber equals one tesla times one square metre.

q: The capacitance of a capacitor is doubled, while the potential difference across it is reduced to half its initial value. By what factor does the energy stored in the capacitor change?
exp: Energy = (1/2) C V squared. Doubling C doubles it, while halving V divides it by four, so the energy becomes half.

q: Which of the following best describes the primary ecological function of a food web within a natural habitat?
o: It shows a series of branching lines of interconnected food chains
It shows the seasonal migration routes of various animal species in a region
It estimates the total biomass of producers present at a given trophic level
It identifies the dominant predators that control the population sizes of other species
exp: A food web is a network of interconnected food chains, showing the many feeding links in a habitat.

q: A student repeatedly lifts a 5-kilogram bag and experiences muscle fatigue during the activity. Which substance is traditionally described as accumulating in the muscles when the oxygen supply is insufficient?
exp: When the oxygen supply falls short, the muscles break down glucose anaerobically and lactic acid builds up, which is linked with fatigue and cramps.

q: How many categories does the USA Air Quality Index (AQI) use to classify air quality?
exp: The US EPA AQI has six categories, from Good to Hazardous, each with its own colour.

q: A bacterial culture initially has 200 bacteria and its number doubles every hour. How many bacteria will be present after 3 hours?
exp: Doubling every hour for 3 hours: 200 to 400 to 800 to 1,600 bacteria.

q: A particle executes simple harmonic motion with amplitude A. When its displacement from the mean position is A/2, what percentage of its total mechanical energy is kinetic energy?
exp: Potential energy at displacement x is E x squared / A squared. At x = A/2 that is one fourth of the total, so the kinetic energy is the remaining 75%.

q: One mole of an ideal gas undergoes a reversible isothermal expansion from 10 L(liter) to 20 L (liter) at a constant temperature of 300 K (kelvin). What is the work done by the gas, approximately?
exp: W = nRT ln(V2/V1) = 1 x 8.314 x 300 x ln 2 = about 1,730 joules, which is nearest to 1,700 J.

q: Which physical quantity is represented by the slope of a line on a velocity-time graph?
exp: The slope of a velocity-time graph is change in velocity divided by time, which is acceleration.

q: Which of the following pairs (Type of Algae – Nutrient Rich In) is correctly matched?
exp: Spirulina, a blue-green alga, is about 60% protein by dry weight, which is why it is sold as a protein supplement.

q: A child develops soft and weak bones that become bowed because of improper mineralisation. Which deficiency disease is most likely responsible for this condition?
exp: Soft, bowed bones in a child are the sign of rickets, caused by a lack of vitamin D, calcium or phosphate. In adults the same deficiency causes osteomalacia.

q: What was the main goal of the Mangrove Co-Management Committee formed in Navghar under the climate resilience project?
o: To promote seasonal fishing and crab collection
To protect mangroves and revive local livelihoods
To increase tourism in coastal Maharashtra
To replace mangroves with modern aquaculture farms
exp: The Mangrove Co-Management Committee at Navghar was formed to protect the mangroves and at the same time restore local livelihoods such as fishing and crab farming.

q: An antibody titre increases from 1:20 before vaccination to 1:320 after vaccination. By how many times has the antibody titre increased?
exp: 320 divided by 20 = 16, so the titre has risen 16 times.

q: An object is placed 30 cm (centimeter) in front of a thin converging lens whose focal length is 15 cm (centimeter). What is the distance of the image from the lens?
exp: Using 1/v = 1/f + 1/u with f = 15 cm and u = -30 cm: 1/v = 1/15 - 1/30 = 1/30, so v = 30 cm. The object is at 2F, so the image forms at 2F on the other side.

q: Which environmentalist from Assam is known for single-handedly developing a forest through his own efforts and is popularly called the "Forest Man of India"?
exp: Jadav Payeng of Jorhat, Assam, planted trees on a sandbar for decades and grew a whole forest, so he is called the 'Forest Man of India'.

q: A rural community uses contaminated pond water for drinking and other daily activities. After a few days, many residents develop complaints of severe diarrhoea and vomiting. Which disease is most likely to spread through the contaminated water?
exp: Cholera, caused by Vibrio cholerae, spreads through water contaminated with faeces and causes severe diarrhoea and vomiting.

q: Which of the following types of tourism is most directly promoted in India to support the conservation of cultural and natural heritage?
exp: Sustainable tourism is promoted so that visitors do not damage the heritage sites and natural areas they come to see.

q: Fill in the blank: Kinetic friction is generally ______ than the maximum static friction.
exp: Once an object starts sliding, the friction needed to keep it moving is less than the maximum static friction, so kinetic friction is smaller.

q: According to the National Green Hydrogen Mission, what is India's annual green hydrogen production target for the year 2030?
exp: The National Green Hydrogen Mission (2023) targets 5 million tonnes of green hydrogen production a year by 2030.

q: Which quantity is calculated by dividing the total distance travelled by the total time interval?
exp: Total distance divided by total time is average speed. Average velocity uses displacement instead of distance.

q: Which plant is used as a bio-indicator to detect pollution from automobile exhaust?
exp: Lichens are very sensitive to sulphur dioxide and vehicle exhaust, so they disappear from polluted areas. This makes them bio-indicators of air pollution.

q: In a pond ecosystem, pesticide exposure causes a substantial decline in the population of fish that help regulate aquatic insect populations. After some time, the mosquito population increases rapidly. What is the most likely ecological explanation for this increase?
o: Reduced competition among mosquito larvae for aquatic resources
Increased reproductive activity of mosquitoes due to pesticide exposure
Reduced predation on mosquito larvae following the decline in fish population
Decreased water temperature leading to greater mosquito survival
exp: The fish ate the mosquito larvae. When the fish died, that predation stopped, so more larvae survived and the mosquito population shot up.

q: In a population, the number of prey increases from 400 individuals to 600 individuals in one year. What is the percentage increase in the population during this period?
A healthy green plant is kept in complete darkness for three consecutive days. Which biological process is the plant unable to carry out because light is unavailable?
exp: Photosynthesis is the only one of these processes that needs light. Respiration, transpiration and germination go on in the dark.

q: The cardiac output is 5 litres per minute and the heart rate is 100 beats per minute. What will be the stroke volume?
exp: Stroke volume = cardiac output / heart rate = 5,000 ml / 100 = 50 millilitres.

q: Which of the following situations most appropriately represents the "Option Value" of nature?
o: Rapidly exploiting forests and prioritising short-term economic gains.
Setting up industries near wetlands and maximising employment opportunities.
Conserving biodiversity and preserving its potential future benefits and uses.
Converting land into agricultural plantations by completely replacing natural forests.
exp: Option value is the value of keeping something available for possible future use. Conserving biodiversity today keeps open benefits we may need later.

q: Which of the following is the SI unit of electrical capacitance?

q: In June 2026, which of the following protected areas in Assam recorded its first-ever sighting of the Yellow-throated Marten?
exp: Kaziranga National Park in Assam recorded its first sighting of the yellow-throated marten in June 2026.

q: Which Indian-origin author won the Women's Prize for Fiction in 2023 for "Demon Copperhead", inspired by Dickens' David Copperfield?
exp: Barbara Kingsolver won the Women's Prize for Fiction 2023 for 'Demon Copperhead', a retelling of Dickens's 'David Copperfield'.

q: Which of the following countries has an HDI value classified as "Very High Human Development"?
exp: Japan is in the 'very high human development' group of the HDI. India and Brazil are in the medium to high groups, and Chad is near the bottom.

q: Which of the following options correctly identifies the launch vehicle and the launch site used for the successful launch of ISRO's Space Docking Experiment (SpaDeX) mission?
exp: SpaDeX was launched on PSLV-C60 from Sriharikota. The mission demonstrated the docking of two satellites in orbit.

q: Smt. Naseem Bano received Padma Shri for excellence in which of the following fields?
exp: Naseem Bano of Lucknow received the Padma Shri for her work in embroidery, the chikankari craft of the city.

q: Who is the first Indian monk to be honored with the American President's Volunteer Service Award?
exp: Jain Acharya Lokesh Muni is the first Indian monk to receive the American President's Volunteer Service Award.

q: What is the purpose of the Platform Aggregator Module launched on the e-Shram portal?
o: A tool to aggregate crop prices
A module for registering platform aggregators
A system to aggregate voter lists
exp: The Platform Aggregator Module on the e-Shram portal lets platform companies, such as app-based delivery and cab firms, register themselves and their gig workers.

q: Which of the following pairs of author and language (Poetry category) for the Sahitya Akademi Award 2025 is correctly matched?
exp: Prasun Bandyopadhyay writes in Bengali, so that is the correctly matched pair for the Sahitya Akademi Award 2025 in poetry.

q: Who assumed office as the Chief of the Naval Staff of India in April 2024?
exp: Admiral Dinesh K Tripathi took over as the 26th Chief of the Naval Staff on 30 April 2024.

q: DR. Bhim Singh Bhavesh, who was honoured with the Padma Shri in 2025, is known for his social work in which Indian state?
exp: Dr. Bhim Singh Bhavesh, honoured with the Padma Shri in 2025 for social work, is from Bihar, where he works with the Musahar community.

q: Who became the first Indian athlete to win two medals in a single edition at the Paris 2024 Olympics?
exp: Manu Bhaker won two medals at Paris 2024, in the 10 m air pistol and the 10 m air pistol mixed team, the first Indian to do so at a single Olympics since independence.

q: Which Indian state's Eravikulam National Park closed for the Nilgiri Tahr calving season in February 2025?
exp: Eravikulam National Park in Idukki district, Kerala, is closed to visitors every year during the calving season of the Nilgiri tahr.

q: Which Indian state hosted the Global Investors Summit 2025 in February?
exp: Madhya Pradesh hosted the Global Investors Summit 2025 at Bhopal in February 2025.

q: Who was appointed as the Governor of Tamil Nadu by the then President of India Ram Nath Kovind in September 2021?
exp: R.N. Ravi, a retired IPS officer, was appointed Governor of Tamil Nadu in September 2021.

q: Who is the author of the short story collection "Bharkhama", which received the Sahitya Akademi Award 2025?
exp: Jitender Kumar Soni, an IAS officer of the Rajasthan cadre, wrote the short story collection 'Bharkhama', which won the Sahitya Akademi Award 2025.

q: Which of the following top-level bureaucratic positions does T. V. Somanathan hold in the Indian government as of 2026?
exp: Dr. T.V. Somanathan, a former Finance Secretary, is the Cabinet Secretary, the senior-most civil servant in the country.

q: Which award was conferred upon Justice (Retd.) Shri Jagdish Singh Khehar in 2025?
exp: Justice J.S. Khehar, the 44th Chief Justice of India, was conferred the Padma Vibhushan in 2025.

q: Dr. V. Narayanan, former Director of ISRO's (Indian Space Research Organisation) Liquid Propulsion Systems Centre, played a key role in which major space technology achievement?
o: Developing the CE-20 cryogenic engine for heavy rockets
Designing the LUPEX (LUnar Polar EXploration) rover
exp: Dr. V. Narayanan led the development of the CE-20 cryogenic engine, which powers the upper stage of the LVM3 rocket.

q: Who is serving as the Chairperson of the Competition Commission of India (CCI) in 2026, responsible for regulating digital markets and preventing anti-competitive practices?
exp: Ravneet Kaur, an IAS officer, is the Chairperson of the Competition Commission of India.

q: Who has been India's 30th Minister of External Affairs since May 2019?
exp: Dr. S. Jaishankar, a former Foreign Secretary, has been India's 30th External Affairs Minister since May 2019.

q: How many medals in total did India win at the Paris 2024 Summer Olympics?
exp: India won 6 medals at Paris 2024: one silver (Neeraj Chopra) and five bronze.

q: At the Paris Olympics 2024, which Indian female shooter won an Olympic medal in the 10m Air Pistol event, becoming the first-ever woman from India to do so?
exp: Manu Bhaker won bronze in the women's 10 m air pistol at the Paris Olympics 2024, the first Olympic medal by an Indian woman shooter.

q: At the 2022 Asian Games held in Hangzhou in 2023, India achieved a historic milestone by crossing which medal count for the first time?
exp: India crossed 100 medals for the first time at the Asian Games, winning 107 at Hangzhou in 2023.

q: The World Happiness Report combines well-being data from how many countries?
exp: The World Happiness Report uses survey data from more than 140 countries, drawn from the Gallup World Poll.

q: The Prime Minister's Development Initiative for North East Region (PM-DevINE) in India is fully funded by which organization?
exp: PM-DevINE, announced in the Union Budget 2022-23, is a 100% centrally funded scheme for projects in the North East.

q: Which wrestler became India's youngest Olympic medallist by winning the bronze medal in the 57 kg category at the Paris 2024 Olympics?
exp: Aman Sehrawat won bronze in the 57 kg freestyle wrestling at Paris 2024 and became India's youngest Olympic medallist.

q: Who was the Director General of Air Operations during Operation Sindoor?
exp: As per the source, Air Marshal A.K. Bharti was the Director General of Air Operations during Operation Sindoor.

q: As of 2026, which statutory anti-corruption post does Praveen Kumar Srivastava hold in India?
o: Director of the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI)
exp: Praveen Kumar Srivastava heads the Central Vigilance Commission as the Central Vigilance Commissioner.

q: The name of the lander used in the Chandrayaan-3 mission is:
exp: The Chandrayaan-3 lander was named Vikram, after Dr. Vikram Sarabhai. The rover was named Pragyan.

q: As of 2026, M. Jagadesh Kumar completed his tenure as the head of which statutory education body in India?
o: National Council of Educational Research and Training (NCERT)
exp: Professor M. Jagadesh Kumar completed his term as Chairman of the University Grants Commission, the body that regulates higher education.

q: Which ISRO (Indian Space Research Organisation) scientist served as the Project Director of India's first solar observation mission, Aditya-L1?
exp: Nigar Shaji of ISRO was the Project Director of Aditya-L1, India's first solar observation mission.

q: Under Atal Mission for Rejuvenation and Urban Transformation (AMRUT) 2.0, 100% water supply coverage is targeted for households in which areas in India?
o: All households in all statutory towns
exp: AMRUT 2.0 aims at 100% water supply coverage for households in all statutory towns, so that cities become water secure.

q: What is a key element of the IMEC (India-Middle East-Europe Economic Corridor) infrastructure?
exp: Along with the rail and shipping links, IMEC includes a pipeline network, for hydrogen and energy, as well as a data cable.

q: The state of Uttarakhand has recently taken steps towards implementing a Uniform Civil Code. What is a key feature of the proposed Uniform Civil Code(UCC) in Uttarakhand?
o: Uniform laws for marriage, divorce, and inheritance, excluding tribal communities.
Abolition of all existing personal laws immediately.
Introduction of Sharia law for all citizens.
exp: Uttarakhand's Uniform Civil Code lays down common rules for marriage, divorce, succession and live-in relationships, while keeping Scheduled Tribes outside its scope.

q: IMEC (India-Middle East-Europe Economic Corridor) aims to significantly reduce the following:
o: Transit time of goods between Asia and Europe
exp: IMEC is expected to cut the transit time for goods between Asia and Europe by offering a shorter combined sea-and-rail route.

q: The PM SHRI (PM Schools for Rising India) scheme is primarily designed to achieve which of the following objectives?
o: Providing free laptops to all school students in rural areas
Developing and upgrading selected schools as model institutions showcasing the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020
Privatising government schools through public-private partnership
Focusing only on higher education and university reforms
exp: PM SHRI upgrades selected existing schools into model schools that show how the National Education Policy 2020 works in practice.

q: Which of the following propellant combinations is used in ISRO's semi-cryogenic engine (SE2000)?
exp: ISRO's semi-cryogenic engine SE2000 burns liquid oxygen with refined kerosene (ISROSENE), which is cheaper and safer to handle than liquid hydrogen.

q: Who was the President of India during whose tenure the "One Nation, One Election" legislative roadmap was presented to Parliament in March 2026?
exp: Droupadi Murmu, the 15th President of India, has been in office since July 2022.

q: As of May 2025, the Vice Chairperson of NITI Aayog and Chairman of the Economic Advisory Council to the Prime Minister (EAC-PM) is ______.
exp: Suman Bery became Vice Chairperson of NITI Aayog in May 2022, and he also heads the Economic Advisory Council to the Prime Minister.

q: Exercise MITRA SHAKTI 2025 is a bilateral military exercise between which of the following countries?
exp: Exercise MITRA SHAKTI is the annual joint military exercise between the Indian Army and the Sri Lanka Army.

q: The government has a target to create 6 crore Lakhpati Didis. To fast-track this goal, which Ministry launched the National Campaign on Entrepreneurship in January 2026 in India?
o: Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare
Ministry of Women and Child Development
exp: The National Campaign on Entrepreneurship for Lakhpati Didis was launched by the Ministry of Rural Development, which runs the Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana and the self-help group programme.

q: Fill in the blanks: 18th Circle Style National Kabaddi Championship (Women) was held in ______
exp: The 18th Circle Style National Kabaddi Championship for women was held at Charkhi Dadri in Haryana.

q: General Anil Chauhan, whose tenure was extended in late 2025, has served as the principal military adviser to the Government of India in which role?
exp: General Anil Chauhan is India's Chief of Defence Staff, the principal military adviser to the government, appointed in September 2022.

q: Dalavai Kullayappa is an artist trying to revive which of the following art forms?
exp: Dalavai Kullayappa of Nimmalakunta in Andhra Pradesh works to revive Tholu Bommalata, the leather shadow puppetry of the state.

q: What is the main objective of RBI's (Reserve Bank of India) Unified Lending Interface (ULI) initiative in India?
o: To replace UPI for digital payments
To enable inclusive and frictionless access to credit
exp: The Unified Lending Interface of the RBI brings land records, KYC and other data onto one platform so that loans, especially small and rural loans, can be given quickly and easily.

q: Ravi Agrawal is the head of which tax administration body in 2026?
o: Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs
exp: Ravi Agrawal, an IRS officer, is the Chairman of the Central Board of Direct Taxes, which administers income tax and other direct taxes.

q: The "Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY)" focuses on a specific sector of the Indian economy. Which sector does this scheme primarily aim to develop?
exp: Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana, launched in 2020, is for the development of fisheries and aquaculture.

q: What is the designation of Parvathaneni Harish in 2026, who made headlines in 2025 for advocating India's stance on United Nations Security Council (UNSC) reforms at the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA)?
o: Ambassador of India to the United States
Permanent Representative of India to the United Nations
High Commissioner of India to the United Kingdom
exp: Parvathaneni Harish is India's Permanent Representative to the United Nations, where he has pressed India's case for Security Council reform.

q: What is the focus of ISRO's Ladakh Human Analogue Mission?
o: Simulating lunar/Martian habitats for astronaut training
exp: The Ladakh Human Analogue Mission sets up a habitat in a cold, dry, high-altitude area that resembles the Moon and Mars, to test living conditions and train for future missions.

q: Which Maithili memoir was honoured with the Sahitya Akademi Award 2025?
exp: The Maithili memoir 'Dhatri Pat San Gaam' won the Sahitya Akademi Award 2025.

q: How many gold medals did India win at the 2022 Asian Games held in Hangzhou in 2023?
exp: India won 28 gold medals at the Hangzhou Asian Games, part of a record haul of 107 medals.

q: Who has been appointed as the new Managing Director of Indraprastha Gas Limited (IGL) in June 2026?
exp: Kumar Shankar was appointed Managing Director of Indraprastha Gas Limited in June 2026.

q: For which achievement was Arundhati Reddy recognised in March 2026?
o: International Cricket Council (ICC) Women's Player of the Month
exp: Arundhati Reddy, the India women's team bowler, was named ICC Women's Player of the Month in March 2026.

q: The Chabahar project mainly strengthens India's ability to reach Afghanistan through which route?
exp: Chabahar port lies on Iran's coast on the Arabian Sea side, so goods go by sea from India to Chabahar and then overland through Iran to Afghanistan.

q: At which venue was the fourth edition of the Oriental Cup football tournament held from 7–16 July 2025?
exp: The fourth Oriental Cup football tournament was held at the Dr. Ambedkar Stadium in New Delhi in July 2025.

q: What is the primary objective of the "Saa ₹ thi 2.0" mobile application launched by SEBI (Securities and Exchange Board of India)?
o: Listing of new startups on the stock exchange
Empowering investors with knowledge about the securities market
Registering complaints against fraudulent insurance agents
exp: SEBI's Saarthi 2.0 app is an investor education tool. It explains the basics of the securities market, KYC, mutual funds and grievance redressal.

q: Which Hindi memoir won the Sahitya Akademi Award 2025?
exp: The Hindi memoir 'Jeete Jee Allahabad' by Mamta Kalia won the Sahitya Akademi Award 2025.

q: In September 2022, who was named the Director General of the Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR)?
exp: Dr. Rajiv Bahl was named Director General of the Indian Council of Medical Research in September 2022.

q: Under the PMDDKY (Pradhan Mantri Dhan-Dhaanya Krishi Yojana) in India, which institution partners with each district to provide technical knowledge and support?
o: National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (NABARD)
exp: Under PMDDKY each district is paired with a central or state agricultural university, which supplies technical knowledge and crop advice.

q: Under the Chabahar International Transport and Transit Corridor Agreement, what will the Contracting Parties provide to drivers and passengers during transport?
exp: The contracting parties agreed to give drivers and passengers the visas and transit facilities needed for the movement of goods.

q: Who is the ninth chairperson of the National Commission for Women (NCW)?
exp: Vijaya Rahatkar is the ninth Chairperson of the National Commission for Women, appointed in October 2024.

q: In Swachh Survekshan 2024, which city retained the title of India's cleanest city for the 7th consecutive year?
exp: Indore retained the title of India's cleanest city in Swachh Survekshan 2024, for the seventh year in a row.

q: Which spacecraft platform serves as the base structure for the NISAR satellite?
exp: NISAR is built on ISRO's I-3K spacecraft bus, used for satellites of about the 3,000 kg class.

q: Who won the 2025 Shakti Bhatt Prize for her debut memoir The Lucky Ones?
exp: Zara Chowdhary won the 2025 Shakti Bhatt Prize for her debut memoir 'The Lucky Ones'.

q: Under India's PM Vidyalaxmi scheme, eligible students from families with an annual income between ₹4.5 lakh and ₹8 lakh are entitled to interest subvention at what rate during the moratorium period?
o: Full interest subvention for all loans
exp: Under PM Vidyalaxmi, students from families earning Rs 4.5 lakh to Rs 8 lakh a year get 3% interest subvention on loans up to Rs 10 lakh during the moratorium period.

q: What is the main objective of the 'Amrit Bharat Station Scheme' launched by the Ministry of Railways, Government of India?
o: Continuous development of railway stations with a long-term vision
Providing free Wi-Fi at 100% rural stations
exp: The Amrit Bharat Station Scheme of the Ministry of Railways provides for the continuous upgrade of railway stations under a long-term master plan, instead of one-time works.
